title: Physics-constrained and geometry-aware deep reconstruction for limited-angle CBCT.
abstract: Objective Limited-angle cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) is attractive for imageguided radiotherapy and imaging-guided procedure when full-arc acquisition is impractical, but the incomplete angular sampling leads to severe streaking, shading, and structural distortion. This study aimed to develop a physics-constrained and geometry-aware deep reconstruction framework for recovering anatomically faithful volumetric CBCT from limited-angle projections. Approach: We propose PCGA-Net, a dual-domain reconstruction framework that combines projection completion, analytic geometric reconstruction, and image-domain refinement within a unified cross-domain design. Specifically, a projection completion module first estimates missingangle information from the measured limited-angle projections. A geometry-aware reconstruction module then maps the completed projections into image space using differentiable cone-beam forward and backward-projection operators. Finally, a volumetric refinement module suppresses residual artifacts and restores anatomical detail under geometry-guided cross-domain consistency supervision. The framework was evaluated on three cohorts: gynecologic highdose-rate brachytherapy, abdominal liver 4DCT, and head-and-neck CBCT. Main Results: Across all three cohorts, PCGA-Net consistently outperformed conventional limitedangle FDK reconstruction and the compared learning-based baselines, cGAN and PatRecon-Net, in both qualitative and quantitative evaluation. On the gynecologic HDR brachytherapy cohort, PCGA-Net achieved an MAE of 34.47 ± 6.28 HU, an SSIM of 0.87 ± 0.04, and a PSNR of 35.79 ± 0.95 dB. On the abdominal liver 4DCT cohort, PCGA-Net achieved 39.27 ± 6.10 HU MAE, 0.82 ± 0.03 SSIM, and 36.85 ± 1.16 dB PSNR.On the head-and-neck CBCT cohort, PCGA-Net achieved 28.42 ± 4.88 HU MAE, 0.91 ± 0.05 SSIM, and 38.52 ± 0.95 dB PSNR. In all three cohorts, PCGA-Net exceeded cGAN and PatRecon-Net across all evaluated metrics. Significance: These results indicate that jointly enforcing projection-domain completion, analytic imaging geometry, and image-domain refinement is an effective strategy for limited-angle CBCT reconstruction. PCGA-Net provides a robust short-arc reconstruction framework across multiple anatomical sites, supporting its potential utility in constrained imageguided therapeutic and procedural settings.

title: Nonlinear stability phenotypes and collapse dynamics of multi-organ radiomics in total-body PET imaging: toward digital twin-oriented robustness assessment.
abstract: Objective Radiomics analysis in PET offers a high-dimensional representation of tissue characteristics, yet its reliability is limited by sensitivity to acquisition perturbations, particularly dose reduction. This study aims to introduce a nonlinear stability phenotyping framework to characterize dose-response behavior of multi-organ radiomics and evaluate their potential relevance for future digital twin-oriented applications. Approach: A multi-center dataset of 550 total-body PET scans was analyzed. Dose reduction was simulated using list-mode subsampling (dose reduction factor - DRF = 2-100). A total of 107 radiomics features were extracted per organ. Stability was quantified using Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC) and summarized as stability fractions. Nonlinear models were fitted to organ- and feature-level trajectories. Stability phenotypes and critical thresholds were derived, along with organ-level instability metrics. Main results: Radiomics stability exhibited strongly nonlinear, organ-dependent behavior. Feature-level analysis identified frequent sigmoid-associated collapse patterns with high descriptive model fits (R²>0.90). The liver showed the highest instability burden (30.8% unstable features), followed by esophagus and kidneys (18-20%). Texture features were the primary source of instability, whereas shape features remained robust. Organ-level trajectories demonstrated heterogeneous responses, with some organs maintaining high stability (0.80-0.95) across DRFs, while others showed sharp declines (down to 0.64). Linear (stable) behavior dominated at the organ level, though masking underlying nonlinear feature dynamics. Significance: Radiomics stability in total-body PET follows nonlinear, phenotype-driven dynamics with identifiable tipping points and organ-specific sensitivity. The proposed framework provides a behavior-based approach for evaluating radiomics robustness and supports the selection of reliable features and organs for robust quantitative imaging and may inform future digital twin-oriented applications.

title: Spot-wise compensation of proton beam deflection and radiation field deformation in the transverse magnetic field of an in-beam MR scanner using a research version of a commercial treatment planning system.
abstract: Objective Magnetic resonance-integrated proton therapy (MRiPT) offers the potential for high-precision, image-guided particle therapy but is challenged by magnetic field (MF)-induced proton beam deflection and radiation field deformation. Unless compensated for, these effects compromise dose conformity and prohibit clinical implementation. This work aims to develop and experimentally validate a spot-wise compensation method capable of restoring proton dose distributions in the presence of a measured 3D magnetic vector field map within a clinical treatment planning system (TPS). Approach A spot-wise compensation framework was implemented in a research version of RayStation, a TPS commercially available for clinical use. The method compensates both lateral beam deflection and MF-induced radiation field deformation by shifting individual pencil-beam spots based on displacement vectors derived from dose calculations in water phantoms using the measured MF of an in-beam MR scanner integrated with a horizontal proton beamline. Two complementary strategies were implemented: a patient-specific approach based on plan-specific displacement calculations, and a generic approach using precomputed displacement maps derived from a reference phantom. Compensation performance was evaluated in representative clinical cases. Dose distributions were experimentally validated using 2D ionisation chamber array measurements. Main Results Both compensation methods effectively restored target coverage, dose homogeneity, and organ-at-risk sparing to the level of no-MF reference plans. The patient-specific method generally achieved a higher performance, whereas the generic compensation method enabled rapid automated correction with sufficient accuracy for clinical workflows involving deep-seated tumours. Local γ-analysis demonstrated excellent agreement between measured and calculated doses, with pass rates exceeding 98.5% for 3%/3 mm criteria. Significance This work demonstrates that compensation of MF-induced proton beam deflection and field deformation can be achieved entirely within a research version of the RayStation TPS using measured, MR scanner-specific MF data. The proposed method provides a scalable, robust framework for future MRiPT clinical applications.&#xD.

title: Silver sodium nitroprusside nano-aggregates for ultrasound-activated immunomodulatory therapy of MRSA pneumonia.
abstract: The clinical management of methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA) pneumonia is hindered by biofilm infections and cytokine storms. A key challenge is the lack of real-time monitoring tools for the inflammatory microenvironment during treatment. In this study, we developed a theranostic platform (CS@EAgNP) using TPP-modified chitosan to load silver sodium nitroprusside nano-aggregates (AgNP) and epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG). This system combines ultrasound (US) imaging with US-activated therapy. The CS@EAgNP nano-aggregates can act as an excellent US contrast enhancer. In vivo US imaging indicated that AgNP generated significantly enhanced echo signals at the infection site, providing real-time and high-contrast visualization of the inflammatory foci that was unattainable with normal lung tissue. Moreover, these nano-aggregates release NO, silver and EGCG under US. The NO and silver penetrate biofilms to kill MRSA, while EGCG scavenges reactive oxygen species and modulates inflammation. This reduces pro-inflammatory cytokines like IL-6 and TNF- α , mitigating the cytokine storm. In vivo results further confirm that this image-guided strategy achieves significant bacterial clearance and promotes lung tissue regeneration without detectable toxicity to major organs. This integrated approach bridges diagnosis and treatment, offering a promising solution for managing MRSA pneumonia.

title: Pre-clinical evaluation of a smartphone-assisted navigation system for surgical pin positioning in total knee arthroplasty.
abstract: Total knee arthroplasty (TKA) success is highly dependent on accurate implant alignment, however, 80% of procedures globally are performed manually. Manual procedures have higher alignment errors compared to robotic platforms and patient-specific instrumentation, yet these have limitations of high cost and intraoperative inflexibility, respectively. This study aimed to evaluate the intraoperative pin positioning accuracy and flexibility of a smartphone-assisted navigation system using CT-derived surgical plans. Three participants used the navigation system to perform 108 guide pin insertions (54 femoral, 54 tibial) on surrogate bone models based on CT-derived surgical plans. Testing included both default mechanical axis targets (0°) and user-selected navigated targets ranging from -3° to 3°. Accuracy was assessed by comparing achieved pin trajectories with the preoperative surgical plan. Median absolute angular deviations achieved ranged from 0.9° to 1.6° across all component-plane combinations, with an overall median deviation of 1.3° (IQR 0.6-2.1°). The proportion of insertions within a predefined ±3° clinical accuracy threshold ranged from 83.3% to 100%, and all component-plane combinations demonstrated deviations significantly within this threshold (p < 0.00001). These findings support the technical feasibility of the smartphone-assisted navigation system for surgical pin positioning under controlled pre-clinical conditions. Further studies will evaluate the navigation system in cadaveric models with experienced orthopaedic surgeon participants.

title: A Practical Pipeline for Patient-Specific Musculoskeletal Modeling: A Comprehensive MRI-Based Framework.
abstract: Patient-specific musculoskeletal (MS) modeling can provide estimates of internal joint loading that canot be measured directly. However, limitations in automated segmentation due to data-scarce environments, morphing difficulty caused by anatomical variability, and functional non-alignment are major bottlenecks that hinder the practical application of modeling and reduce productivity in musculoskeletal research. To comprehensively address these practical issues, this study proposes and validates an integrated, automated modeling framework.. First, we automatically segmented the lower extremity bones of the 4 knee osteoarthritis patients using a multi-atlas-based segmentation algorithm. By integrating the segmented bone with motion capture and force plate data, a modeling pipeline including multi-stage morphing and functional alignment processes was implemented. Using the constructed customized model, the medial and lateral knee contact forces (FMC and FLC) were estimated during a single-leg step-up exercise, and these were compared and evaluated against the results based on manual segmentation. The contact forces estimated through the automated segmentation framework demonstrated high consistency with the manual results. The mean absolute error ranged from 0.04 ± 0.03 to 0.06 ± 0.03 BW for FMC, and from 0.06 ± 0.04 to 0.09 ± 0.07 BW for FLC, and the intraclass correlation coefficient demonstrated a high correlation of over 0.99 across all patients. This study demonstrated that the proposed automated pipeline provides a practical approach to address misalignment caused by anatomical variability, while generating joint load estimates equivalent to the manual approach. By addressing key methodological challenges, this study will bring patient-specific models closer to future clinical application, where they could help assess individual loading across different activities and inform treatment and rehabilitation strategies.

title: A compact teacher-student knowledge-distillation framework for lumbar MRI segmentation.
abstract: Accurate segmentation of lumbar magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is important for quantitative assessment of degenerative spine disease, but it remains challenging because spinal structures show low contrast, variable morphology, and severe pixel-class imbalance. This study evaluates a compact teacher-student knowledge-distillation framework for multi-class lumbar MRI segmentation. The student network integrates a Res2Net encoder-decoder, a lightweight transformer bottleneck, and deep supervision; a manifold-constrained hyper-skip (MHC) module is evaluated as an optional constrained skip-fusion variant rather than assumed to be the sole source of improvement. A UNet++ teacher transfers soft probability, class-focused, and boundary-weighted information to guide boundary-sensitive anatomical regions. Under five-fold case-level GroupKFold validation on the primary public axial lumbar MRI dataset, the MHC full-KD variant achieved Dice 0.9141 ± 0.0021, foreground Dice 0.8934 ± 0.0026, IoU 0.8519 ± 0.0033, and HD95 3.1451 ± 0.2101. A no-MHC student trained with the same full distillation objective achieved essentially the same Dice (0.9141 ± 0.0021) with lower HD95 and lower measured latency, indicating that the full distillation objective, rather than the MHC block alone, explained most of the performance recovery toward the teacher. Replication on the 2026 Medical Lumbar Spine 3D Axial MRI Dataset achieved Dice 0.8960 ± 0.0032 and IoU 0.8224 ± 0.0047. A fixed label-harmonized train-on-primary/test-on-2026 transfer stress test achieved macro Dice 0.7002 ± 0.0181 and foreground Dice 0.6280 ± 0.0225. The results suggest that compact class-aware distillation can support reproducible lumbar MRI segmentation for future computer-aided measurement pipelines, while prospective and strict cross-institutional validation remain necessary.

title: 3D ViT network with selective feature enhancement and cross-dimensional interaction for colorectal T-stage classification in CT images.
abstract: Background. Obstructive colorectal cancer (OCC) often manifests on computed tomography (CT) as highly variable in morphology and location, with indistinct margins, atypical infiltration signs, and frequent adherence to surrounding structures. In addition, motion artifacts caused by intestinal peristalsis further degrade image quality and interfere with the identification of subtle structures. These factors readily lead to misassessment in T-stage evaluation, and accurately distinguishing between T4 and non-T4 stages is critical as it directly influences surgical planning and clinical decision-making. Purpose. To address challenges of imaging heterogeneity and motion artifacts in T-stage evaluation, we proposed a 3D vision transformer (ViT) based model with feature enhancement and cross-dimensional interaction for T4/non-T4 classification of OCC. Methods. First, we extended ViT into 3D and incorporate a selective feature enhancement module. This module computes attention weights based on feature means, adaptively enhancing discriminative information while suppressing redundant responses. It effectively mitigates difficulties in identifying subtle structures like serosal invasion caused by motion artifacts and low contrast in CT images, enabling the model to focus on diagnostically critical regions. Second, we introduced a cross-dimensional adaptive feature aggregation mechanism that established multi-scale 3D spatial dependencies, integrating global context with fine-grained local details. This significantly improves the model's ability to characterize tumors with complex and variable morphological features, thereby reducing staging inaccuracies due to underutilized spatial information. Furthermore, cross-domain knowledge transfer was employed to enrich the model's representational capacity and alleviate the inherent data scarcity in 3D medical image analysis. Results. Evaluated on a private dataset of 127 CT scans, the proposed model achieved an AUC of 0.8917 and an accuracy of 0.7917 in T4/non-T4 classification, significantly outperforming mainstream 3D medical image classification networks. Conclusions. Our approach offers clinicians a reliable decision support tool for accurate OCC staging, allowing surgeons to tailor operative strategies based on quantitatively reliable imaging assessments.

In addition, motion artifacts caused by intestinal peristalsis further degrade image quality and interfere with the identification of subtle structures. These factors readily lead to misassessment in T-stage evaluation, and accurately distinguishing between T4 and non-T4 stages is critical as it directly influences surgical planning and clinical decision-making.Purpose.To address challenges of imaging heterogeneity and motion artifacts in T-stage evaluation, we proposed a 3D vision transformer (ViT) based model with feature enhancement and cross-dimensional interaction for T4/non-T4 classification of OCC.Methods.First, we extended ViT into 3D and incorporate a selective feature enhancement module. This module computes attention weights based on feature means, adaptively enhancing discriminative information while suppressing redundant responses. It effectively mitigates difficulties in identifying subtle structures like serosal invasion caused by motion artifacts and low contrast in CT images, enabling the model to focus on diagnostically critical regions. Second, we introduced a cross-dimensional adaptive feature aggregation mechanism that established multi-scale 3D spatial dependencies, integrating global context with fine-grained local details. This significantly improves the model's ability to characterize tumors with complex and variable morphological features, thereby reducing staging inaccuracies due to underutilized spatial information. Furthermore, cross-domain knowledge transfer was employed to enrich the model's representational capacity and alleviate the inherent data scarcity in 3D medical image analysis.Results.Evaluated on a private dataset of 127 CT scans, the proposed model achieved an AUC of 0.8917 and an accuracy of 0.7917 in T4/non-T4 classification, significantly outperforming mainstream 3D medical image classification networks.Conclusions.Our approach offers clinicians a reliable decision support tool for accurate OCC staging, allowing surgeons to tailor operative strategies based on quantitatively reliable imaging assessments.

title: 3D SE-ResUNet for accurate dose prediction in head and neck IMRT: a structure-specific ensemble approach.
abstract: Accurate three-dimensional dose prediction is important for automated treatment planning and radiotherapy in head and neck cancer. This study investigates an ensemble-based deep learning framework for dose prediction from computed tomography images and anatomical structures, with particular emphasis on structure-specific model weighting. A dataset of 340 head and neck cancer patients from the Open Knowledge-Based Planning dataset was used for model development and evaluation. Three three-dimensional convolutional neural network architectures, including U-Net, SE-UNet, and SE-ResUNet, were trained for dose prediction. Their predictions were first combined using a global weighted ensemble. To account for differences in prediction performance across anatomical structures, a structure-specific ensemble was subsequently developed. For each structure, the relative contribution of the three models was optimized independently on the validation set using an exhaustive grid search with weight increments of 0.1. Performance was evaluated using the Dose Score and dose-volume histograms (DVHs) Score. Among the individual models, SE-ResUNet achieved the lowest DVH Score (2.067 Gy), while the global weighted ensemble achieved a Dose Score of 2.77 Gy and a DVH Score of 2.068 Gy. The proposed structure-specific ensemble substantially reduced the DVH Score to 1.75 Gy, although its overall Dose Score increased slightly to 2.81 Gy. The proposed structure-specific ensemble provides an anatomy-aware strategy for combining complementary dose predictions from heterogeneous deep learning models. While it does not improve the overall Dose Score relative to the global weighted ensemble, it substantially improves the DVH Score and provides a more structure-aware characterization of dose prediction performance. The approach may therefore be useful for deep learning-based dose prediction in head and neck intensity-modulated radiation therapy.

title: Integrating radiomic features and spatial semantic features from multiparametric MRI for IDH genotyping in glioma.
abstract: Gliomas, one of the most prevalent primary tumors of the central nervous system, have IDH molecular subtypes that are strongly linked to patient survival, prognosis, and treatment plans. However, there are currently few noninvasive preoperative prediction techniques, and postoperative pathology and genetic testing are the main approaches used to assess IDH status. Radiomics features can quantitatively characterize intratumoral heterogeneity, whereas spatial semantic features may provide additional information related to tumor location and macroscopic growth patterns. When it comes to characteristics like glioma invasiveness, growth patterns, and angiogenesis, spatial semantic features can enhance radiomics features. In order to predict IDH molecular subtypes in gliomas, this study suggests a combined analytical approach that incorporates clinical data, spatial semantic features, and multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) radiomic features. This technique uses the IBSI standard to extract radiomic data from raw multiparametric MRI images and combines morphological analysis, gradient statistics, and 3D geometric modeling to create spatial semantic information. To eliminate redundant features and account for multicollinearity, Pearson correlation analysis and the variance inflation factor were utilized. The best feature subset was then obtained through a multi-stage feature selection procedure that combined random forests (RFs), LASSO regression, and recursive feature elimination. Lastly, imaging characteristics and clinical data were combined using a RF model to identify IDH molecular subtypes in gliomas. According to experimental findings, the suggested model's area under the ROC curve (AUC) in a five-fold cross-validation was 96.08%. The model had the AUC of 95.62%, ACC of 91.67%, sensitivity of 88.89%, and specificity of 93.94% in the final test set. The limitations of radiomics in conveying tumor macroscopic development patterns and spatial invasion relationships can be somewhat compensated for by spatial semantic aspects, according to additional investigation. title: External evaluation of a deep learning-based algorithm for automated lung tumor and esophagus segmentation on CBCT.
abstract: Online adaptive radiotherapy requires fast and accurate delineation of targets and organs at risk on cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT). Although deep learning (DL)-based CBCT auto-segmentation methods have been proposed, their clinical generalizability remains insufficiently validated. This study aimed to externally evaluate a pretrained DL model for lung tumor and esophagus segmentation on CBCT. Originally trained using C-arm linac CBCT images, the model was directly applied to an independent cohort of 12 lung cancer patients, each with 5 CBCT images acquired at a separate institution on an O-ring linac. Rigid propagation of planning CT contours served as a minimal baseline to determine whether the model matched or outperformed conventional rigid registration for gross tumor volume (GTV) and esophagus segmentation using geometric and dosimetric measures. Compared with rigid contour propagation, the model significantly improved GTV segmentation accuracy, with mean Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) increasing from 0.66 to 0.76. Significant differences in GTV D98% were observed between the model-generated contours and the reference contours (50.69 vs 53.58 Gy). The model showed a statistically non-significant decrease in performance compared with previously reported results on its original testing dataset (mean DSC = 0.84), which shared the same distribution as the training dataset. For esophagus segmentation, evaluation of 26 scans from 6 patients showed that the model achieved geometric accuracy within peri-target contour rings comparable to rigid propagation, with mean DSC of 0.72 and 0.70, respectively. Similar esophagus V32Gy values were observed between the model-generated and reference contours (0.06 vs 0.06 cc). Significantly reduced accuracy was observed compared with previously reported results, with mean DSC decreasing from 0.79 to 0.72. These findings highlight that DL-based CBCT auto-segmentation may suffer performance degradation under domain shifts across patient populations, clinical workflows, and imaging systems, emphasizing the necessity of external evaluation beyond the original development environment.

title: Patient-specific dosimetric impact of online adaptive radiotherapy for locally advanced cervical cancer.
abstract: Background: When cervical cancer patients are treated with external beam radiation therapy, patient-specific anatomical changes, particularly bladder filling, alter the position and shape of the target volume throughout treatment. Online adaptive radiotherapy (oART) accounts for these interfractional changes by generating a treatment plan based on the patient's daily anatomy. Purpose: This study evaluated the dosimetric impact of oART and investigated the relationship between patient-specific anatomical changes and the dosimetric of benefit of adaptation using standard cone-beam CT (CBCT) images for locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC). Methods: Ten patients previously treated for LACC at our institution were identified. A reference treatment plan incorporating a 5 mm clinical target volume (CTV)-to-planning target volume (PTV) margin was generated within the planning system simulator. Three CBCT images (Fractions 1, 13, and 25) were used to retrospectively simulate an adaptive treatment session. For each CBCT, the reference plan was recalculated on the daily anatomy to generate a scheduled plan, and an adapted plan was generated for comparison based on target coverage and organ at risk (OAR) dose metrics. The relationship between interfraction anatomical variation and the dosimetric benefit of adaptation was evaluated. Results: Adapted plans improved target coverage while generally maintaining or reducing OAR dose relative to the scheduled plans. However, the magnitude of benefit from adaptation varied between patients. Moderate associations were observed between interfraction anatomical variation of the bladder volume change and improvements in target coverage. Conclusion: The dosimetric benefit of oART was patient-specific and was partially associated with interfraction anatomical variation. These findings support an individualized approach to identify patient-specific characteristics that may help determine what patients would benefit the most from adaptive radiotherapy.

title: Dosimetric comparison of the anisotropic analytical algorithm and Acuros XB for single-fraction cranial stereotactic radiosurgery with a 6 MV flattening filter-free beam.
abstract: Stereotactic radiosurgery delivers an ablative single-fraction dose to small intracranial targets, and the reported dose depends on the calculation algorithm. This exploratory case series quantified the change in reported dosimetry when plans clinically finalised with the anisotropic analytical algorithm (AAA) were recalculated with Acuros XB (AXB) in dose-to-medium mode. Seven consecutive brain metastases in six patients, treated with 6 MV flattening filter-free volumetric modulated arc therapy, were recalculated on the same CT dataset using identical arc geometry, control points, multileaf collimator sequences and monitor units, without re-optimisation or renormalisation. Dose-volume histogram parameters were compared for the planning target volume (PTV), normal brain and organs at risk, and plan quality with the RTOG prescription-isodose-to-target-volume (PITV) ratio, the Paddick conformity index (PCI) and the gradient index (GI). Paired comparisons used exact two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank tests and are interpreted as exploratory. AXB reported lower PTV dose metrics than AAA for the same deliverable plans, with mean D95% falling from 21.66 to 21.10 Gy, D98% from 21.19 to 20.58 Gy and Dmean from 24.58 to 24.13 Gy (all p = 0.016). The mean paired D98% difference was 3.00 ± 0.80% of the prescription dose. The PITV ratio fell from 1.19 to 1.10 and GI rose from 3.23 to 3.43 (both p = 0.016), whereas PCI did not differ (0.79 versus 0.82, p = 0.188). Normal-brain V12Gy and V10Gy were unchanged. Routine electronic portal imaging device dosimetry of the delivered plans gave a mean 2%/2 mm gamma passing rate of 98.5 ± 1.7%, documenting deliverability rather than validating either algorithm. These findings support careful review of target-dose metrics when an established AAA workflow is transitioned to AXB. The cohort is small and no independent reference dosimetry was available, so the study establishes neither clinical superiority nor an effect on tumour control or toxicity.

title: A multi-atlas ensemble learning framework for autism spectrum disorder diagnosis.
abstract: Objective. Clinical autism spectrum disorder (ASD) relies on subjective scales and neuroimaging, with traditional approaches suffering from high subjectivity and insufficient feature extraction, increasing misdiagnoses risk. Approach. To improve the diagnostic accuracy, we propose a multimodal ASD prediction network (APN) that integrates resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging with non-imaging data. Algorithmically, we first introduce a novel cumulative distribution divergence score (CDDS) feature selection method based on the multi-atlas functional connectivity (FC), which quantifies statistical distributional differences between positive and negative samples, effectively addressing the limitations of the traditional F -score in overlapping or weakly discriminative features. Building upon this, we adapt existing deep learning (DL) paradigms to construct a deep neural architecture (variational autoencoder-denoising autoencoder (VAEA)), combining a variational autoencoder (VAE), a denoising autoencoder, and a multilayer perceptron. The combination of these modules is non-trivial: the novel CDDS first purifies the high-dimensional feature space, enabling the VAEA to learn robust latent probabilistic representations via unsupervised pre-training without suffering from the curse of dimensionality. This is followed by the supervised fine-tuning to optimize parameters. We further incorporate demographic factors including age, full-scale intelligence quotient, and gender via a late-fusion strategy to prevent them from being overshadowed by imaging features, thereby enhancing the discriminability. FC features from three atlases including AAL, CC400, and Dosenbach160 are weighted and integrated to achieve the effective multi-source fusion. Main results. We conduct 10-fold cross-validations on the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE) dataset, and the proposed APN achieves 81.63% accuracy, 81.89% sensitivity and 81.46% specificity, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art methods. Interpretability analysis identifies hippocampus, amygdala, and cingulate gyrus as strongly ASD-associated regions, offering neural mechanistic insights. Significance. This study provides an efficient, objective, and interpretable multimodal DL framework for ASD assisted diagnosis, with substantial clinical application and neuroscience value.

title: CT protocol optimization for oncologic surveillance imaging: phantom-based comparison of multi-scan and single-scan acquisition strategies.
abstract: Computed tomography (CT) plays an important role in oncologic surveillance after treatment of gynecological malignancies, including patients treated with vaginal electronic brachytherapy. This phantom study evaluated CT acquisition strategies for oncologic surveillance, focusing on radiation dose reduction and objective image quality in the cranial, thoracic, and upper abdominal regions assessed quantitatively. CT acquisition protocols were investigated using an anthropomorphic Kyoto Kagaku phantom. Two acquisition strategies were analyzed: a multi-scan approach with separate acquisitions for the head, neck, thorax, and abdomen-pelvis, and a single-scan head-torso acquisition with region-specific reconstructions. Different exposure parameter settings and reconstruction kernels were evaluated. Objective image quality was assessed using semi-automated region-of-interest measurements with a custom FIJI/ImageJ macro. Signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), and Artifact Index (AI) were calculated for cranial, thoracic, and abdominal regions. For the single-scan protocols, CTDIvol decreased from 4.21 mGy in the standard protocol to 2.97-3.99 mGy in the optimized protocols, while DLP decreased from 410 mGy.cm to 287-388 mGy.cm. Across all anatomical regions, SNR and CNR remained comparable with the standard protocol. Thoracic CNR ranged from 2.68 to 3.01, abdominal CNR remained stable in both liver and aortic regions, and AI demonstrated only moderate variability across the optimized protocols. Optimized CT acquisition protocols reduced radiation dose while preserving the evaluated objective image quality metrics in the cranial, thoracic, and upper abdominal regions. Among the evaluated configurations, a reduced dose single scan head-torso acquisition using reduced tube voltage and tube current modulation showed a favorable balance between radiation dose reduction and objective image quality under the investigated phantom conditions and was identified as a candidate protocol for subsequent clinical and reader performance validation.

title: Wavelet-based adaptive image fusion of CT and MRI with local neighborhood variance for nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
abstract: Multimodal imaging of nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) requires complementary representation of CT-derived bony anatomy and MRI-derived soft-tissue contrast. Existing fusion methods may fail to preserve both structural detail and soft-tissue information in a transparent and reproducible manner. We present a wavelet-based fusion framework that employs local neighborhood variance for adaptive weighting. This interpretable variance-driven strategy selectively integrates CT bony structures and MRI soft-tissue textures according to regional information content. The neighborhood configuration was selected through an ablation analysis of 232 clinical cases. Quantitative evaluation showed improved image-quality performance over the selected comparison methods across entropy, spatial frequency, average gradient, standard deviation, and edge information preservation factor, with respective gains of approximately 5.5%, 2.4%, 6.7%, 5.1%, and 3.2% relative to the best-performing baseline for each metric. These findings support the proposed method as an image fusion methodology for preserving complementary multimodal information; direct effects on target delineation, workflow efficiency, or dosimetric outcomes require future clinical validation.

title: Self-Supervised, Physics-Driven Sparse-Array XACT Reconstruction Using Sinusoidal Implicit Neural Representation.
abstract: X-ray induced acoustic computed tomography (XACT) enables high-contrast bone imaging but typically relies on dense and expensive transducer arrays. Sparse array sampling introduces severe streak artifacts and loss of fine structural details in conventional reconstruction. This work aims to establish a robust reconstruction framework that achieves high-fidelity structural imaging under sparse sampling, thereby overcoming hardware density limitations and facilitating low-cost, high-resolution skeletal health assessment. We propose a self-supervised, physics-driven framework based on sinusoidal implicit neural representation. The unknown initial pressure distribution is parameterized as a continuous coordinate-to-pressure function via a sinusoidal representation network, and is coupled end-to-end with a differentiable acoustic forward simulator implemented in j‑Wave. Network optimization is performed by minimizing waveform residuals between measured and predicted signals, eliminating the need for paired ground-truth data. To improve training stability and accelerate convergence, an adjoint-based warm start and total variation regularization are employed. In experiments on simulated hand and femoral bone sparse array datasets, the proposed method consistently outperforms conventional approaches under various sparse sampling conditions. Notably, for an osteoporotic femur imaged with only 64 transducer elements, the method effectively suppresses artifacts and faithfully preserves fine trabecular structures, achieving a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 32.43 dB and a root mean square error of 0.0239, surpassing the structural and quantitative accuracy of traditional reconstruction using a full 256‑element array. These results demonstrate that the framework supports stable XACT reconstruction under sparse array conditions and, with its favorable artifact suppression and microstructural preservation capabilities, offers a practical computational pathway toward low-cost, high-quality XACT imaging.
originalAbstract: X-ray induced acoustic computed tomography (XACT) enables high-contrast bone imaging but typically relies on dense and expensive transducer arrays. Sparse array sampling introduces severe streak artifacts and loss of fine structural details in conventional reconstruction. This work aims to establish a robust reconstruction framework that achieves high-fidelity structural imaging under sparse sampling, thereby overcoming hardware density limitations and facilitating low-cost, high-resolution skeletal health assessment. We propose a self-supervised, physics-driven framework based on sinusoidal implicit neural representation. The unknown initial pressure distribution is parameterized as a continuous coordinate-to-pressure function via a sinusoidal representation network, and is coupled end-to-end with a differentiable acoustic forward simulator implemented in j‑Wave. Network optimization is performed by minimizing waveform residuals between measured and predicted signals, eliminating the need for paired ground-truth data. To improve training stability and accelerate convergence, an adjoint-based warm start and total variation regularization are employed. In experiments on simulated hand and femoral bone sparse array datasets, the proposed method consistently outperforms conventional approaches under various sparse sampling conditions. Notably, for an osteoporotic femur imaged with only 64 transducer elements, the method effectively suppresses artifacts and faithfully preserves fine trabecular structures, achieving a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 32.43 dB and a root mean square error of 0.0239, surpassing the structural and quantitative accuracy of traditional reconstruction using a full 256‑element array. These results demonstrate that the framework supports stable XACT reconstruction under sparse array conditions and, with its favorable artifact suppression and microstructural preservation capabilities, offers a practical computational pathway toward low-cost, high-quality XACT imaging.

title: High-Frequency Enhancement and Dual-Model Ensemble for Language-Guided COVID-19 Pneumonia Lesion Segmentation.
abstract: Accurate segmentation of COVID-19 pneumonia lesions in chest X-ray (CXR) images is critical for disease quantification and clinical decision-making. However, existing methods suffer from blurred lesion boundaries, missed detection of tiny lesions, and limited generalization performance. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a language-guided multimodal medical image segmentation method integrating high-frequency enhancement and a dual-model ensemble. The method is developed along three dimensions: frequency-domain detail enhancement, spatial alignment optimization, and dual-model ensemble. First, a frequency-domain decomposition-based high-frequency enhancement module is designed to mitigate detail attenuation caused by encoder downsampling. Second, a two-dimensional (2D) spatial position encoding module is introduced to improve the spatial alignment between text descriptions and visual regions. Third, a dual-model ensemble architecture with differentiated frequency-domain masks is constructed to address the performance ceiling of individual models. Finally, experiments on two public datasets with different imaging modalities and data characteristics demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms existing single-modal and multimodal baseline methods and achieves competitive performance comparable to state-of-the-art approaches, verifying the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed framework. On the QaTa-COV19 dataset, the Dice coefficient reaches 91.85% and the mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) reaches 84.98%. On the multi-institutional MosMedData+ dataset, the Dice coefficient reaches 78.48% and the mIoU reaches 64.66%. The proposed method provides effective technical support for clinical diagnosis and follow-up assessment of pneumonia.

title: Meaningful thresholds for change in quantitative computed tomography-derived fibrosis extent in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
abstract: Rationale Validated thresholds for clinically meaningful change in quantitative computed tomography (QCT) for fibrosis extent across algorithms remain unclear in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). Objectives To evaluate minimal clinically important difference (MCID) for 1-year change in QCT metrics in IPF using different algorithms than previously reported and to identify prognostically meaningful thresholds for effective risk stratification. Methods This multicenter retrospective study included IPF patients with baseline and 1-year follow-up CT. Minimal clinically important differences for change in fibrosis score (ΔFS) derived from fully automated CT quantification were estimated using an anchor-based approach with 1-year changes in FVC and diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLco), and a prognostic threshold was estimated using maximally selected log-rank statistics. Prognostic significance of ΔFS was evaluated in discovery and validation cohorts. Results The discovery cohort included 524 patients (mean age = 66.8 years; 79% men), and the external validation cohort included 224 patients (mean age = 69.6 years; 83% men). Anchor-based MCIDs were 2.72% for FVC and 4.52% for DLco, with a prognostic threshold of 4.05%. In the discovery cohort, 1-year ΔFS were independently associated with transplant-free survival (TFS), with greater risk when ΔFS exceeded MCID or prognostic thresholds (all, P < .001). In the validation cohort, ΔFS remained associated with TFS (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] = 1.11; 95% CI, 1.04-1.18), and all prespecified ΔFS thresholds were prognostic for overall TFS, with the prognostic threshold of ΔFS ≥ 4.05% showing the most consistent associations with overall (aHR = 2.78; 95% CI, 1.36-5.68) and 3-year TFS (aHR = 2.88; 95% CI, 1.11-7.48). Conclusion One-year change in FS and its thresholds were significantly associated with TFS, supporting annual CT follow-up with predefined QCT thresholds for monitoring and risk stratification in IPF.

title: An update to the classification, evaluation, and management of childhood interstitial lung disease in infancy: an official American Thoracic Society Clinical Practice Guideline.
abstract: Background Childhood interstitial lung diseases (chILD) are a heterogeneous group of rare disorders. In 2013, the American Thoracic Society (ATS) developed a guideline regarding the classification, evaluation, and management of children <2 years old with chILD. The current guideline provides updated recommendations regarding genetic testing, chest imaging, lung biopsy, and lung transplant referral. Methods The Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation approach was used to form clinical questions, summarize evidence, and develop recommendations, following ATS policies and procedures. A multidisciplinary panel with expertise in chILD formulated recommendations addressing diagnostic tools and referral for lung transplant evaluation. Results Rapid and broad genetic testing is recommended for infants with chILD and respiratory failure (strong recommendation). Chest computed tomography (CT) remains an important part of the diagnostic evaluation (conditional recommendation). Surgical lung biopsy is recommended when there is urgency to identify a specific chILD disorder and genetic testing is not feasible, timely, or inconclusive; to identify histopathologic "treatable traits"; or to inform prognosis (strong recommendation). Referral for lung transplant evaluation is recommended for children with specific chILD disorders with predictable poor outcomes (strong recommendation). Repeat chest CT to aid decision-making, prognosis, and/or change therapies is suggested for children with chILD diagnosed before age 2 years (conditional recommendation). Conclusions This guideline provides evidence-based recommendations for genetic testing, chest imaging, lung biopsy, and referral for lung transplant evaluation to improve the diagnostic evaluation and management of children <2 years with chILD. Implementing this guideline will hopefully increase genetic testing for chILD, inform the diagnostic evaluation and disease monitoring of chILD, and identify future research priorities for chILD.

title: Geo-economic variations in structure and organization of intensive care units: the ISOREA survey.
abstract: Purpose Little is known on critical care services globally. This study aimed to describe ICU resources and organization across countries and assess variability by income group, between countries, and within countries. Methods Participating centers provided structured data on hospital and ICU characteristics via electronic case report form (January 2018 to July 2020). Questionnaire included 237 items covering general characteristics (2 topics) and ICU resources and organization (18 topics). We computed standardized functional domain scores (ISOREA score), classified ICUs using Marshall criteria, and readiness for essential emergency and critical care using a modified Schell score. Results A total of 1,426 ICUs from five continents were recruited, and 1,225 were analyzed, from high-income countries (HICs, 58%), upper-middle-income (20%), and low/lower-middle-income countries (LLMICs, 22%). Most ICUs were in referral centers (90%) and large urban areas (80%). Most variables (93%) were significantly associated with income group, Most variables (93%) were significantly associated with income group, with 88% showing higher levels in HICs and lower levels in LLMICs. Six domains showed major disparities: extracorporeal support, respiratory support, emergency access to interventional radiology and surgery, neurology and trauma care, patient file and general monitoring, and cardiovascular and hemodynamic monitoring. According to the Marshall classification, 79% of ICUs in HICs were classified as level III, whereas 55% of ICUs in LLMICs were classified as level I. Domains with higher ISOREA scores varied primarily between countries, whereas lower-performing domains exhibited greater variability across ICUs within the same country. Adjustment for income group reduced, but did not eliminate, country-level clustering. Conclusion Substantial disparities exist in ICU resources and organization across income groups, countries, and ICUs. ICU capacities appeared multidimensional, extending beyond resource limitations.

title: Serial Mass Tuberculosis Screening Among the Elderly in Eastern China from 2021-2023.
abstract: Rationale The impact of repeated community-wide tuberculosis screening is uncertain because evidence from large-scale, multi-round screening campaigns is limited. Objectives We evaluated whether annual, community-based, chest-radiography screening was associated with reduced tuberculosis prevalence and detection of asymptomatic disease across multiple screening rounds. Methods We conducted three annual chest X-ray screening rounds (2021-2023) among adults aged ≥60 years in Lanxi City, Zhejiang Province. All participants underwent chest radiography at community health centers, with referral for diagnostic evaluation and bacteriological testing. We estimated detection yields per 100,000 screened persons, assessed trends, and used direct standardization and repeated-participation analyses. Measurements and main results Across all rounds, 214,948 screening encounters were completed. From Round 1 to Round 3, screening-detected prevalence declined for overall tuberculosis (233.1 [95% CI, 194.2-279.7] to 146.3 [95% CI, 123.1-173.9] per 100,000 screened persons) and bacteriologically-confirmed tuberculosis (162.1 [95% CI, 130.3-201.7] to 108.6 [95% CI, 88.8-132.7] per 100,000 screened persons). From Round 1 to Round 3, asymptomatic tuberculosis decreased as both a proportion of cases (47.8% to 26.6%) and prevalence among screened participants (111.5 to 38.9 per 100,000). Compared with Round 1, tuberculosis prevalence was lower in Round 2 (-28.1% change; 95% CI, -44.0 to - 7.5) and Round 3 (-37.2% change; 95% CI, -51.2 to - 19.2). The Round 2-to-Round 3 difference was smaller and included the null (-12.8% change; 95% CI, -31.7 to 11.4). Standardization and repeated-participation analyses yielded broadly similar patterns. Conclusions Serial community-level screening was associated with declining tuberculosis prevalence, including asymptomatic disease, with the largest reduction occurring between the first and second screening rounds.

title: Withdrawn as duplicate: Pulmonary Blood Volumes on CT Predict Residual Pulmonary Hypertension Post-Pulmonary Endarterectomy.
abstract: Pulmonary blood volumes (PBV), currently not assessed by computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA), could provide additional information to routine investigations performed for chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH). We investigated CTPA-based PBV in evaluating hemodynamic outcome from pulmonary endarterectomy (PEA) surgery. A deep learning-based CTPA vascular segmentation model, differentiating arteries and veins, was applied for automated PBV measurements in CTEPH patients who underwent PEA at U.K.'s national CTEPH service. Pulmonary arteries were compartmentalised into "central" (main pulmonary and proximal lobar) and "intrapulmonary". Mean pulmonary arterial pressure >30 mmHg post-PEA defined "clinically relevant" residual PH. Logistic regression models applying CTPA-based PBV to identify residual PH were trained and tested on the discovery and validation cohorts respectively. Paired pre- and postoperative CTPA, in the discovery (n = 71) and validation (n = 102) cohorts showed that central pulmonary artery volume and total artery to vein volume ratio (A-VR) decreased and pulmonary vein volume increased with hemodynamic improvement post-PEA. Postoperative central pulmonary artery volume, A-VR and pulmonary vein volume helped to non-invasively identify patients without clinically relevant residual PH (AUROC 0.91 and 0.88 in the discovery and validation cohorts). Automated quantification of CTPA-based PBV at diagnosis can help stratify risk for residual PH in patients managed with PEA. Utilizing CTPA-derived PBV post-PEA to identify patients without residual PH can potentially reduce the need for routine postoperative right heart catheterization.

title: Regional micro-computed tomography analysis enables longitudinal detection of compensatory ventilation effects in a mouse model of pulmonary fibrosis.
abstract: Accurate lung function assessment is essential in preclinical idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) research, yet conventional whole-lung endpoints overlook spatial heterogeneity and compensatory mechanisms. We present a micro-computed tomography (µCT)-based pipeline for longitudinal, regional quantification of structural and functional changes in a murine bleomycin (BLM)-induced fibrosis model to improve evaluation of disease progression and therapeutic effects. C57BL/6 mice received triple oropharyngeal administrations of saline or BLM. Respiratory-gated µCT scans were acquired in free-breathing at baseline and days 7, 14, and 21. A deep-learning algorithm segmented the lungs into left and right lobes, further subdivided into apical and caudal regions using airway landmarks. Regional volumes, aeration compartments, and ventilation maps were extracted to assess structural and functional alterations. Saline-treated mice showed stable metrics over time, with minimal interanimal variability, demonstrating the robustness and physiological consistency of our segmentation procedure. BLM-treated animals exhibited early and heterogeneous fibrotic changes, with the apical regions appearing as most affected. The caudal-right region displayed a compensatory functional increase of respiratory parameters derived from multivolume µCT. µCT-based regional analysis can detect localized dysfunction and compensatory effects not captured by whole-lung measurements. This strategy is applicable to different models of heterogeneous lung disease and may contribute to reduce the translational gap in IPF research.

title: Quantitative CT in the real-world evaluation of progressive pulmonary fibrosis; the REVISE PPF multicentre observational study.
abstract: Rationale and objective We assessed whether an FDA-cleared quantitative CT (qCT) tool (Brainomix, e-Lung) identifies progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PPF) earlier than routine clinical diagnosis and evaluated the prognostic value of baseline and serial imaging biomarkers. Methods Multicentre retrospective study involving University of Alabama (UAB), Weill Cornell Medicine (WCM) and University of Chicago (UChicago); n = 509. HRCTs were analysed with e-Lung to derive Weighted Reticulovascular Score (WRVS, %), Total Disease Extent (TDE, %), and e-Lung Volume (mL). Prespecified progression thresholds were an absolute WRVS increase of ≥ 3 percentage points, an absolute TDE increase of ≥ 1.5 percentage points, and a relative e-Lung Volume decline of ≥ 10%, over less than 2 years. We compared the earliest qCT progression date with recorded clinical PPF diagnoses, assessed clinically stable controls, and modelled associations with future PPF and mortality using adjusted time-varying Cox models. Results Among 200 patients with PPF and serial HRCTs meeting the prespecified timing criterion, qCT identified progression earlier in 78% (UAB), 83% (WCM), and 47% (UChicago), with mean lead times of 434, 847, and 220 days, respectively. Among 187 clinically stable patients meeting the same serial-imaging criterion, progression thresholds were met in 67%, 56%, and 42%, respectively. High-risk baseline WRVS (≥15%) predicted future PPF (OR 4.09, 2.48, and 2.30) and mortality (HR 2.03 pooled UAB/WCM; 2.75 UChicago). Per 1-percentage-point increase, adjusted mortality HRs were 1.15 and 1.19 for WRVS and 1.05 and 1.04 for TDE in pooled UAB/WCM and UChicago, respectively. Threshold crossings were also associated with mortality (WRVS: HR 6.50 pooled UAB/WCM, 4.05 UChicago; TDE: 7.60 and 3.26; e-Lung Volume: 8.20 and 2.59). Conclusion qCT detects radiological progression months to years before clinical PPF diagnoses. Integrating e-Lung into ILD pathways could accelerate treatment decisions and personalize follow-up.

title: Evaluation of Costal Cartilage Calcification Using Plain Radiographic Images.
abstract: Background Costal cartilage is a vital autologous graft for structural rhinoplasty, but calcification complicates surgical planning and graft manipulation. Chest computed tomography is the conventional evaluation method but is not routinely used owing to radiation exposure and cost. Objectives To evaluate, using plain rib series radiography, the prevalence, morphological patterns, and predictors of costal cartilage calcification in patients undergoing rhinoplasty. Methods Two reviewers jointly assessed bilateral 6th-8th costal cartilages from 183 rhinoplasty patients (1,098 rib segments) on preoperative chest radiographs, grading calcification (0-4) and classifying morphological pattern (marginal, granular, or central). Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of calcification presence and severity. Results Costal cartilage calcification (grade ≥1) was present in 54.1% of segments, with significantly higher prevalence (62.9% vs 46.6%, P < 0.001) and severity in females than males. Calcification was predominantly marginal in males (95.4%), whereas 15.1% and 17.6% of females showed granular and central patterns, respectively. Severe calcification (grade ≥3) peaked unexpectedly in the 40-49-year group (25.8%) rather than in older patients. On multivariable analysis, female sex (OR 3.01; 95% CI, 1.11-8.12) and age 40-49 years (OR 6.28; 95% CI, 1.69-23.36) were independent predictors of severe calcification. Conclusions Routine rib series imaging should be considered even in younger candidates to optimize donor site selection and avoid unexpected intraoperative findings.

title: RibXcar: Safety Fundamentals and Surgical Protocol for Controlled Costal Osteotomy in Body Contouring Surgery: A Prospective Study of 100 Patients.
abstract: Background Aesthetic body contouring surgery has incorporated costal modification techniques to improve waist definition. The lack of standardized protocols and prospective safety data has generated controversy. The RibXcar technique proposes a controlled monocortical costal osteotomy as an alternative to rib resection; however, no prospective studies have comprehensively evaluated its safety profile. Objectives To describe a standardized surgical protocol for the RibXcar technique and prospectively evaluate its safety, efficacy, impact on pulmonary function, postoperative pain, and patient satisfaction. Methods A prospective study of 100 consecutive patients who underwent RibXcar alone (n=80) or combined with body liposuction (n=20). A 10-step protocol was described, and outcomes were evaluated: complications, pulmonary function (spirometry), waist diameter, costal angulation (ultrasound), pain (VAS), and satisfaction (Body-Q) preoperatively and at 6 months. Results The overall minor complication rate was 8%, with no cases of pneumothorax or hemothorax. Pulmonary function showed no significant changes at 6 months in either group. Waist diameter reduction was 5.0 cm (IQR: 3.75-7.0) in the RibXcar group and 10.50 ± 1.73 cm in the combined group (P < .001). Costal angulation decreased significantly in all evaluated ribs (P < .0001). Body-Q scores improved significantly (P < .00001), and pain resolved by 6 months. Conclusions The results of this series suggest that RibXcar, when performed under a standardized protocol, may constitute a safe and effective alternative for aesthetic rib remodeling in selected patients. The preservation of pulmonary function and the low complication rate observed would support its implementation in advanced body contouring surgery.

title: XCREST II: The X-factor in Iliac Crest Remodeling for Advanced Waist-to-hip Definition.
abstract: Background Modern body contouring has evolved toward structural reshaping, with the waist-hip-gluteal unit as a key determinant of body contour aesthetics. The iliac crest is a critical landmark for lower waist contour. Objectives To evaluate the aesthetic outcomes, safety, and anatomical contribution of XCREST II, a combined bony and myofascial technique for lower waist contouring. Methods A multicenter retrospective cohort study included 480 patients who underwent XCREST II between 2024 and 2026. Patients were categorized into four groups: XCREST II alone (n = 180), XCREST II + gluteal fat grafting (n = 84), XCREST II + RibXcar (n = 132), and XCREST II + RibXcar + gluteal fat grafting (n = 84). All underwent ultrasound-guided iliac crest remodeling with partial gluteus medius detachment. Anthropometric and BODY-Q outcomes were assessed preoperatively and at 12 months. Results Four hundred eighty patients were included. Baseline characteristics were comparable, except for longer operative time in combined procedures (p < 0.001). At 12 months, all anthropometric measures improved significantly from baseline across groups (p < 0.001), without intergroup differences. Complications were low; prolonged postoperative pain and iliac crest pain were more frequent in groups including RibXCar (p = 0.020 and p = 0.017, respectively), without chronic pain. BODY-Q scores improved significantly across all domains (p < 0.001), differing only in body image (p = 0.019) and scar assessment (p < 0.001). Conclusions XCREST II, a refinement of XCREST incorporating partial gluteus medius detachment, demonstrated favorable 12-month waist contour improvement and high patient satisfaction, with a low complication rate. Outcomes were consistent across subgroups.

title: Breast Implant Flipping: Prevalence, Clinical Correlation, and Independent Risk Factors in a Consecutive Ultrasound Cohort.
abstract: Background Silicone breast implants are designed with an anterior domed surface, and relatively flat posterior surface that contains the cured silicone patch. With implant flipping (an anterior-posterior malposition), the posterior patch rotates to an anterior position. Objectives There are currently no prospective published studies reporting the prevalence of implant flipping and its associated symptoms in aesthetic patients. This prospective study used in-office high-resolution ultrasound (HRUS) to evaluate the prevalence of breast implant flipping, assess associated changes in breast shape, appearance, and symptoms, and identify potential risk factors. Methods Consecutive patients with silicone breast implants presenting for routine follow-up underwent HRUS at 7 study sites in the United States over a 4-month period between April 1st and August 1st, 2026. Demographic data included age and BMI. Implant data included time since surgery, whether a primary of revision procedure, number of revisions, manufacturer, size, style, surface, use of ADM or scaffold, pocket location, capsule grade, flipped or not, and rupture. Results Five hundred and ninety consecutive patients were enrolled over 4 months. Mean age 43 years with range 22-82, mean BMI 23 with range of 16-34.5. Primary augmentations accounted for 64.6% of procedures, while revision augmentations accounted for 35.4%. Device manufacturer distribution, 63.9% Allergan, 12.4% Mentor, 15.9% Motiva, and 7.1% Sientra. Implant flipping was identified in 75 patients (12.7%). Conclusions Implant flipping was identified by HRUS in one in eight patients. Larger implant volume, prepectoral placement, and lack of soft tissue support were independently associated with flipping. HRUS improves detection, patient counseling, and surgical planning.

title: Epicardial and pericardial adipose tissue: anatomy, physiology, imaging, segmentation, and treatment effects.
abstract: Epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) and pericardial adipose tissue (PAT) are increasingly recognized as distinct fat depots with implications for cardiovascular disease. This review discusses their anatomical and physiological characteristics, as well as their pathophysiological roles. EAT, in direct contact with the myocardium, exerts local inflammatory and metabolic effects on the heart, while PAT influences cardiovascular health rather systemically. We sought to discuss the currently used imaging modalities to assess these fat compartments-CT, MRI, and echocardiography-emphasizing their advantages, limitations, and the urgent need for standardization for both scanning and image reconstruction. Advances in image segmentation, particularly deep learning-based approaches, have improved the accuracy and reproducibility of EAT and PAT quantification. This review also explores the role of EAT and PAT as risk factors for cardiovascular outcomes, summarizing conflicting evidence across studies. Finally, we summarize the effects of medical therapy and lifestyle interventions on reducing EAT volume. Understanding and accurately quantifying EAT and PAT is essential for cardiovascular risk stratification and may open new pathways for therapeutic interventions.

title: Coronary computed tomography angiography as a screening tool.
abstract: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) has evolved into a key non-invasive tool for evaluating coronary artery disease, offering high sensitivity, detailed anatomical visualization, and strong prognostic value. Current Society of Cardiovascular Computed Tomography guidelines recommend CCTA as a first-line test for symptomatic patients, while limiting its use in asymptomatic individuals to select high-risk cases. Advantages in a screening context include early detection of subclinical atherosclerosis, prognostic assessment through high-risk plaque features, and facilitation of personalized preventive strategies. However, widespread screening faces challenges: procedural complexity, contrast and radiation exposure, psychological impact, and economic cost. Emerging integration of artificial intelligence promises to enhance efficiency, automate plaque quantification, and enable individualized risk prediction, potentially improving cost-effectiveness and clinical adoption. Future validation through randomized controlled trials and real-world data is needed to confirm the impact of CCTA-based screening on cardiovascular event reduction, healthcare resource use, and patient quality of life.

title: Extracardiac imaging biomarkers of cardiovascular health: a comprehensive review.
abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading global cause of morbidity and mortality. Beyond clinical risk factors and cardiac imaging, extracardiac imaging biomarkers provide complementary insight into cardiometabolic health. Routine non-cardiac imaging often depicts the liver, kidneys, pancreas, lung, brain, adipose tissue, muscle, vasculature, breast, and bone, enabling opportunistic risk assessment. Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), detectable on MRI, CT, and ultrasound, independently predicts major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Chronic kidney disease-related markers including kidney size, vascular calcification, and renal resistive index also correlate with adverse outcomes. Reduced pancreas volume is similarly associated with cardiovascular disease. CT-quantified emphysema and lung hyperinflation are associated with coronary artery disease and cardiovascular mortality. Cerebral small vessel disease markers, such as white matter hyperintensities and silent brain infarcts, demonstrate associations with cardiovascular events. Ectopic adiposity and sarcopenia quantified by CT, MRI, and ultrasound add prognostic value beyond body mass index. Extracardiac vascular and skeletal biomarkers, such as breast arterial calcification and low bone mineral density, further associate with cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Collectively, these markers improve risk stratification and enable screening without added cost or radiation. Future priorities include standardization, external validation, and integration into risk prediction models to advance precision cardiovascular medicine.

title: Optimization and technological advances in cardiovascular magnetic resonance to improve access and screening.
abstract: Cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) can comprehensively assess cardiac function and structure, with a unique capability for tissue characterization. However, its access remains limited due to general availability. Additionally, CMR has lengthy preparation and acquisition times. Various optimization methods and techniques have been proposed to streamline CMR workflow and shorten total acquisition times. These include patient preparation, rapid imaging protocols, sequences developments, deep learning-based image acceleration and reconstruction, as well as automated image analysis and report generation. Together, these advances may grant CMR access to more patients and even enable more accessible non-invasive cardiac screening of high-risk and general population in the future. This narrative review provides an overview of different concepts and technologies aiming at optimizing CMR in terms of workflow and image acquisition and highlights the opportunities for high-volume CMR studies to support more patient-centred cardiovascular care.
authorString: Li X, Sprinkart AM, Isaak A, Luetkens JA.

title: Pericoronary adipose tissue imaging: quantitative assessment, artificial intelligence integration, and therapeutic modulation.
abstract: Pericoronary adipose tissue (PCAT) is increasingly recognised as a biosensor of vascular inflammation. The guideline-driven widespread adoption of coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) as the first-line investigation for coronary artery disease (CAD) has created opportunities for evaluating the inflammatory burden through quantitative assessment of PCAT. Standardising raw PCAT imaging data for technical, anatomical, and biological variability provides the Fat-Attenuation Index (FAI) Score, which shows promise as a metric of coronary inflammation. Quantification of coronary inflammation has implications for the diagnosis, risk stratification, and monitoring of treatment in atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. This review examines the anatomical and physiological basis of PCAT, highlighting the importance of standardising PCAT imaging for the implementation as a clinical biomarker, and reviews the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in enhancing precision and scalability. Emerging evidence on the modulation of FAI Score by therapeutic agents, including statins, biologics, and cardiometabolic drugs, and the potential utility of serial imaging in guiding clinical care is also discussed. With ongoing large-scale validation and emerging AI -based approaches, PCAT imaging is poised to complement traditional risk factors and plaque metrics; however, current evidence remains evolving, and the integration of inflammatory risk assessment could be useful to guide emerging anti-inflammatory treatments in personalised cardiovascular medicine.
authorString: Eveson L, Sobirov I, Chan K.

title: Coronary artery calcium score-emerging role for opportunistic screening on thoracic CT and novel applications.
abstract: Coronary artery calcium (CAC) can be identified on thoracic CT performed for a variety of clinical indications, including routine thoracic CT, lung cancer screening CT, and attenuation correction CT. Identification of CAC on thoracic CT as part of opportunistic screening can improve the assessment of cardiovascular risk and can identify patients who may benefit from preventative medical therapies. This approach enhances early detection of coronary artery disease within existing healthcare workflows. However, at present, there are no randomized trials that assess the clinical impact of this approach. Recently, the development of artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) models has facilitated the automated identification and quantification of CAC, offering rapid and reproducible assessments. Artificial intelligence/machine learning models could reduce radiologist workload and provide end-to-end integration into routine clinical practice. Novel technologies such as photon-counting CT offer further potential for CAC detection and risk stratification through the use of high-resolution imaging and spectral imaging with virtual non-contrast images. This review discusses the evidence for opportunistic screening for CAC on thoracic CT and highlights novel applications including AI/ML assessments, CAC as a multi-system biomarker, and the potential for photon counting CT.
authorString: Patel R, Williams MC.

title: Advanced quantitative CT for coronary artery disease: integrating stenosis quantification, plaque quantification, and fractional flow reserve-CT.
abstract: Coronary artery disease (CAD) continues to be a leading cause of death globally. Radiological evaluation of CAD generally consists of stenosis detection by cardiac CT angiography (CCTA). However, this approach can be inefficient and subject to interobserver variability. In this review, we explore the newest developments related to CAD evaluation by CCTA, with an emphasis on plaque quantification. Artificial intelligence-based quantitative CT offers an efficient and reproducible method to analyze plaque biomarkers that support more refined risk stratification for major adverse cardiovascular events. Artificial intelligence-based coronary stenosis quantification can streamline workflow and improve consistency. The utilization of a photon-counting detector CT has been demonstrated to enhance spatial resolution, thereby allowing more precise coronary lumen analysis and artifact reduction. Fractional flow reserve-CT delivers a noninvasive physiologic assessment of stenotic lesions. Finally, we discuss the impact of these changes on risk stratification and guiding preventive therapy as well as possible future directions in this rapidly evolving field.

title: Incidental pulmonary embolism and the value of CT pulmonary angiography follow-up versus expert review.
abstract: Objectives Evaluate the prevalence of true-positive and false-positive incidental pulmonary embolism (iPE) diagnoses and the impact of expert review on diagnostic accuracy. Methods This single-center retrospective study included consecutive contrast-enhanced thoracic CT examinations without dedicated PE protocols which reported iPE over an 18-month period (2022-24). Electronic health records were reviewed to identify requests to confirm PE based on previous non-dedicated studies. Studies identifying iPE were graded from 1 (most certain) to 5 by original report diagnostic certainty and compared between PE-positive and PE-negative subgroups using Fisher's exact test. Identified imaging received retrospective expert review to calculate expert agreement with CTPA, where CTPA had been performed, using Cohen's kappa. Results Of 25 214 CT examinations, 260 (1%) reported iPE (mean age 73 ± 12 years; 51% women). Of these, 25% (n = 65/260) underwent confirmatory CTPA. Patients receiving CTPA had lower initial iPE diagnostic certainty (median 3 versus 1, P < .01) and 52% (n = 34/65) were PE-positive on CTPA. Patients with false-positive diagnoses had reduced diagnostic certainty on non-dedicated studies compared to those with a true-positive diagnosis (median 3 versus 2, P < .001). Agreement between the expert review of the iPE scan and the ground-truth CTPA diagnosis had κ of 0.96. Conclusions Expert review could be an effective tool to reduce CTPA requirement in cases of intermediate (grade 3) iPE diagnostic certainty. Advances in knowledge Low-certainty incidental pulmonary embolism diagnoses on initial non-dedicated CT are more likely to be false-positives according to CTPA findings or expert thoracic radiologist review. Expert review of initial CT may therefore reduce excessive imaging and avoid treating false-positive cases.

title: Ultrasound evaluation and outcome of breast masses in a cohort of pubertal children.
abstract: Objective To describe the ultrasound evaluation and outcome of breast masses in a cohort of pubertal children. Methods A single institution, institutional review board-approved, retrospective study was performed including 13- to 18-year-old patients who had a breast ultrasound from January 1990 to December 2024. Clinical information and the ultrasound results were collected. Ultrasound was deemed positive if it explained the patients' concern. Tissue sample was determined by the patient and ordering physician. Pathology results and follow-up ultrasounds were recorded as well. Descriptive analysis was performed. Results Two hundred forty patients (237 females) were included with a mean age of 17 years. The most common indication was a palpable mass (65%). Two hundred thirty-seven ultrasounds were positive (99%), 193 patients had a biopsy (80%). The most common diagnoses were fibroadenoma (69%), hamartoma (13%), and phyllodes tumor (7%). No primary or secondary breast malignancies were identified. Twenty-six patients with a positive ultrasound and without a biopsy underwent sonographic surveillance, 20 patients had unchanged findings, and 5 had decreased/resolved findings. Conclusion The prevalence of malignant pediatric breast masses is exceedingly low. No malignant breast masses were found in our cohort; however, diagnosis should be suspected based on the clinical presentation and ultrasound appearance. The low percentage of malignant breast masses suggests sonographic surveillance and patient education are feasible and safe management approaches in most adolescent breast mass cases. Advances in knowledge This study provides 1 of the largest analyses of adolescent breast ultrasounds, showing that malignancy is exceedingly rare and supporting sonographic surveillance as a safe management approach.
