title: Predominantly mild thrombocytopenia, haematoma expansion and clinical outcomes in intracerebral haemorrhage.
abstract: Introduction Evidence regarding the prognostic significance of thrombocytopenia in spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage (ICH) remains limited and inconsistent. We investigated its associations with haematoma expansion (HE), functional outcomes and mortality. Patients and methods We retrospectively analysed prospectively collected data from consecutive patients with spontaneous ICH in a single-centre registry between August 2022 and March 2025. Thrombocytopenia was defined as an admission platelet count <150 × 109/L. HE was defined as a haematoma-volume increase >6 mL or >33% on follow-up noncontrast computed tomography. Poor functional outcome was defined as a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 3-6 at 3 months. Associations were assessed using multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic splines, ordinal regression and sensitivity analyses. Results Among 496 patients, 106 (21.4%) had thrombocytopenia; 368 were included in the HE analysis. After adjustment, thrombocytopenia showed no statistically significant association with HE (adjusted OR 0.97, 95% CI, 0.52-1.76; P = .920), 3-month poor functional outcome (adjusted OR 0.88, 95% CI, 0.46-1.66; P = .693), or 3-month mortality (adjusted OR 1.43, 95% CI, 0.70-2.89; P = .324). Restricted cubic spline analysis showed no statistically significant overall association and the test for nonlinearity was not statistically significant. Findings were similar across platelet-count categories, continuous haematoma-volume changes, ordinal mRS analyses and sensitivity analyses addressing imaging timing, early surgery, acute treatments and prior anticoagulant use. Discussion Admission thrombocytopenia showed no statistically significant association with HE, poor functional outcome, or mortality after ICH. Because few patients had platelet counts <100 × 109/L, these findings mainly apply to mild thrombocytopenia.

title: Genetic analysis of bone morphometry and ivory vertebrae in threespine stickleback.
abstract: Previous genetic studies of skeletal variation in threespine stickleback fish (Gasterosteus aculeatus) have focused primarily on striking morphological differences. Here, we examine the largely unexplored genetic architecture of internal bone microstructural variation between marine and freshwater stickleback. Micro-computed tomography X-ray analysis revealed differences in the porosity, bone thickness, and bone volume fraction within armor plates and vertebrae from a marine and freshwater stickleback. Quantitative trait locus mapping in F2 progeny from a marine × freshwater stickleback cross identified a significant locus on chromosome 4 influencing multiple aspects of armor plate internal microstructure. This locus overlaps the well-characterized Eda region previously known to control armor plate number and size. Co-mapping of bone microstructure could be due to pleiotropic effects of Eda on multiple aspects of plate development or to changes in closely linked genes including Itm2a, which also plays a role in bone formation. Most bone microstructure traits in vertebrae showed weak or no genetic signal, consistent with a polygenic architecture. However, we identified a highly significant locus on chromosome 17 that is strongly associated with abnormally thickened "ivory vertebrae" that occurred in 8.4% of F2 offspring. This phenotype resembles Paget's disease in humans, and the major locus region contains Tnfrsf1b, the stickleback ortholog of a human Paget's disease susceptibility gene TNFRSF11A. Together, our findings identify genetic loci underlying natural variation in bone microstructure in wild fish and reveal a candidate gene associated with a disease-like skeletal phenotype, highlighting stickleback as a model for studying both evolutionary and pathological bone biology.

title: Structured reporting of diagnostic hysteroscopy findings in women with reproductive disorders: an ESGE-ESHRE-IFFS international consensus†ǂ.
abstract: Study question How should the findings of diagnostic hysteroscopy in women with reproductive disorders be reported? Summary answer This collaborative document by the European Society for Gynaecological Endoscopy (ESGE), the ESHRE, and the International Federation of Fertility Societies (IFFS) provides the first detailed structured reporting template for diagnostic hysteroscopy findings in women with reproductive disorders. What is known already Despite its widespread use in women with reproductive disorders, no standardized framework currently exists for reporting of hysteroscopic findings. This lack of uniformity may limit the utility of the procedure and contribute to substantial heterogeneity among operators and centers. As a result, the reproducibility of hysteroscopy is limited, making it difficult to conduct robust studies that define its prognostic value in specific patient subgroups. Study design, size, duration A dedicated working group from ESGE, ESHRE, and IFFS collaborated to develop a consensus for comprehensive structured reporting of diagnostic hysteroscopy findings in women with reproductive problems. Participants/materials, setting, methods This consensus paper focuses on grouping diagnostic hysteroscopic findings, structuring their reporting, and adopting standardized terminology for women with reproductive disorders. The virtual Nominal Group Technique, a structured consensus-building method, was adopted to ensure equal contribution from all members in the development of the final consensus. Main results and the role of chance The document provides a structured reporting of hysteroscopic findings into five sections, each systematically capturing patient characteristics, procedural findings, and pathological observations as follows: patient's characteristics, and findings from the vagina, cervix, uterine cavity, endometrium, and tubal ostia. Limitations, reasons for caution The inclusion of a finding in this structured report is not a proof of its clinical significance, but it could be used as a validation tool for further research. Wider implications of the findings The standardized reporting of hysteroscopic findings promotes consistent data collection across centers and could help inform research and exchange of clinical experience, enhancing the value of hysteroscopy in fertility evaluation. Funding No external funding was received for the development of the consensus process or manuscript preparation. Disclosures All authors declare that they have no competing interests. Trial registration number N/A.

title: Transperineal contrast-enhanced ultrasound: a rapid and reliable tool for differentiating abscesses from inflammatory masses in perianal Crohn's disease.
abstract: Background and aim Perianal abscesses are serious complications of Crohn's disease (CD) requiring timely and accurate diagnosis. Contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS), which in abdominal intestinal ultrasound (IUS) has shown diagnostic performance comparable to CT/MRI in distinguishing intra-abdominal abscesses from inflammatory masses, has not been systematically evaluated in the transperineal assessment of perianal Crohn's disease. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance, inter- and intra-observer agreement, and diagnostic confidence of transperineal CEUS versus conventional B-mode TPUS in CD patients with perianal symptoms and suspected septic complications. Methods We retrospectively reviewed 52 examinations of 37 adult CD patients presenting with painful perianal symptoms and suspected septic complications. Patients were included if TPUS detected lesions > 10 mm requiring CEUS characterization. Exclusion criteria were CEUS contraindications, simple fistulas, or large (>3 cm) obvious abscesses. All examinations were recorded, and three blinded experts independently assessed anonymized videos in random order. Lesions were classified as abscesses, inflammatory masses, or phlegmons. Agreement for lesion size, fluid content, and final diagnosis was evaluated using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) and Fleiss-Cohen's kappa (κ). Diagnostic confidence was assessed using a 5-point Likert scale. Results On B-mode, 17 abscesses, 32 inflammatory masses, and 3 phlegmons were identified. CEUS reclassified several, yielding 16 abscesses, 31 inflammatory masses, and 5 phlegmons. Of the 17 abscesses diagnosed on B-mode, only 4 were also classified as abscesses on CEUS, while 13 were reclassified; conversely, 11 inflammatory masses were reclassified as abscesses. Intra-observer reliability improved from κ = 0.55 with B-mode to κ = 0.95 with CEUS. Inter-observer agreement for diagnosis was poor with B-mode (κ = 0.31) but excellent with CEUS (κ = 0.83). Conclusions Transperineal CEUS significantly improves inter- and intra-observer agreement and diagnostic confidence compared with conventional B-mode TPUS when differentiating perianal abscesses from inflammatory masses/phlegmons in CD and frequently leads to lesion reclassification in clinically ambiguous cases.

title: Multi-modal ensemble learning prediction of anti-TNF treatment response in pediatric patients with Crohn's disease using clinical, radiomic, and deep learning MR enterography features.
abstract: Background Anti-tumor necrosis factor (TNF) medical therapy is a major advancement for Crohn's disease (CD) management, yet many patients fail to respond. This study aims to develop and evaluate a multi-modal ensemble model to predict anti-TNF treatment response in pediatric patients with CD using pre-treatment magnetic resonance enterography (MRE) and non-imaging clinical data. Methods This retrospective study included 92 pediatric CD patients (median [IQR] age, 14.6 [12.7, 16.6] years; 65.2% male; 37 responders and 55 non-responders) who underwent MRE within 3 months before initiating anti-TNF therapy between 2009 and 2021. Responders achieved mucosal healing within 36 months; non-responders did not, underwent surgery, or changed therapy. Four pre-treatment feature sets were used: (1) radiologist MRE assessment, (2) radiomic features from bowel regions, (3) deep learning features from representative bowel images, and (4) non-imaging clinical features. A 2-stage stacking ensemble model was trained and evaluated. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) was the primary performance metric. Results The multi-modal ensemble model integrating all MRE-based features achieved an AUROC of 0.771 [95% confidence intervals (CI): 0.745, 0.797], outperforming models using individual feature types (radiologist assessment: 0.706 [0.691, 0.721]; radiomic: 0.710 [0.691, 0.729]; deep learning: 0.724 [0.700, 0.749]). Combining MRE and clinical features (0.739 [0.696, 0.781]) achieved the highest AUROC of 0.817 [0.793, 0.842], though not significantly (P = .10). Radiomic features reflecting intensity distribution and texture heterogeneity were most predictive of treatment response. Conclusion A multi-modal ensemble model combining MRE-based radiologist assessment, radiomic, deep learning, and clinical features accurately predicted anti-TNF treatment response in pediatric CD patients.

title: Endoscopic and histologic healing distribution and persistent rectosigmoiditis in moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis.
abstract: Background Mucosal healing in ulcerative colitis (UC) is believed to follow a proximal-to-distal pattern. We evaluated colonic healing distribution in patients with moderate-to-severe UC receiving adalimumab. Methods Patients from the SERENE UC (Study of a Novel Approach to Induction and Maintenance Dosing with Adalimumab in Patients with Moderate to Severe Ulcerative Colitis) trial with full colonoscopies and segmental biopsies at screening, weeks 8, and 52 were included for endoscopic and histologic analyses if baseline Mayo endoscopic subscore (MES) or Robarts Histopathology Index (RHI) score, respectively, was >0 in the ascending, transverse, and/or descending colon. Data were analyzed using a mixed model for repeated measures to account for clustering of segments within a patient. Results Endoscopic and histologic analyses comprised 76 and 79 patients, respectively. Score reductions were significantly greater vs the rectum in the ascending (week 8: MES, mean -0.78 [95% confidence interval (CI), -1.03 to -0.52]; RHI, mean -4.70 [95% CI, -6.92 to -2.49]; week 52: MES, mean -0.63 [95% CI, -0.91 to -0.35]; RHI, mean -2.39 [95% CI, -4.64 to -0.15]), transverse (week 8: MES, mean -0.69 [95% CI, -0.94 to -0.43]; RHI, mean -3.57 [95% CI, -5.62 to -1.51]; week 52: MES, mean -0.64 [95% CI, -0.89 to -0.38]; RHI, mean -2.88 [95% CI, -4.99 to -0.77]), and descending colon (week 8: MES, mean -0.40 [95% CI, -0.67 to -0.13]; RHI, mean -2.55 [95% CI, -4.94 to -0.16]; week 52: MES, mean -0.52 [95% CI, -0.70 to -0.34]; RHI, mean -3.47 [95% CI, -5.37 to -1.56]). Endoscopic improvement/remission and histologic remission were significantly more likely in the ascending and transverse colon than the rectum. Conclusions Our findings demonstrate that endoscopic and histologic healing is more challenging in the rectum compared with proximal colonic segments.

Conclusions

Our findings demonstrate that endoscopic and histologic healing is more challenging in the rectum compared with proximal colonic segments.

title: Stenosis of a novel frozen elephant trunk in a patient with chronic dissection.
abstract: A partial elephant trunk (PET), a new type of frozen elephant trunk, was designed to prevent distal stent graft-induced new entry using a thinner nitinol wire with less radial force. We report a case of PET stenosis in chronic dissection. Total arch replacement was performed using a PET. After weaning from cardiopulmonary bypass, the lower-limb blood pressure decreased to 90% of the upper-limb blood pressure. Intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography revealed incomplete PET expansion, and on postoperative day 1, the lower-to-upper body blood pressure ratio further decreased to 70% due to PET stenosis at the steeply angulated arch. Emergency thoracic endovascular aortic repair was successfully performed, completely resolving the pressure gradient.

title: Long-term Outcomes in Previously Healthy non-HIV Individuals with Cryptococcal Meningitis Treated with Pulse-taper Corticosteroids for Post-infectious Inflammatory Syndrome.
abstract: Background Post-infectious inflammatory response syndrome (PIIRS) is an increasingly recognized complication of cryptococcal meningoencephalitis (CM) in non-HIV infected hosts with significant morbidity and mortality. Data describing long-term outcomes following immunomodulatory therapy are limited. Methods We conducted a prospective observational study of 15 immunocompetent adults with CM-PIIRS treated with a pulse corticosteroid taper (PCT) regimen. Performance status, neurocognitive, ophthalmologic, audiologic, and radiologic assessments were performed at greater than one year following CM diagnosis. Results After one year, performance status continued to improve from both baseline and the post-pulse periods. Neurocognitive testing revealed mild residual deficits, within the limits of normal, most prominently in information processing and psychomotor speed. Ocular abnormalities were frequent at baseline but showed substantial and sustained reductions following PCT, particularly in retinal nerve fiber layer thickness. Visual field deficits improved by 40% and remained stable thereafter. Evidence for changes in hearing sensitivity at post 1-year follow-up was mixed with 44.5% of ears meeting criteria for improvement, 11% for worsening, and 44.5% being stable. Radiologic abnormalities improved in 79% of patients, although intermittent inflammatory flares occurred during PCT but responded to dose escalation. A prolonged corticosteroid taper may be helpful, and MRI imaging can be used to evaluate response to taper. Conclusions In immunocompetent patients with CM-PIIRS, adjunctive corticosteroid therapy was associated with sustained improvement in neurologic, visual, and radiologic outcomes with mixed improvement in hearing after a year of therapy, with mild residual deficits.

title: Bridging healthcare gaps through public-private partnerships in Nigeria: a scoping review.
abstract: Nigeria's healthcare system faces several persistent structural challenges. Public-private partnerships (PPPs) have emerged as a strategy to address these gaps, although evidence on their implementation and impact remains fragmented. This scoping review mapped the implementation models, outcomes, challenges and future directions of PPPs in Nigeria's healthcare system, following the Arksey and O'Malley framework and PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Literature searches were conducted across PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar and grey literature sources. Studies were screened using Rayyan, while eligibility was guided by the population-concept-context framework. Data were synthesized using descriptive and thematic analysis. Twenty-four studies were included, covering PPP applications across primary, secondary, tertiary and community healthcare systems. Identified models included service delivery, financing, infrastructure, supply chain and governance partnerships. The included evidence reported improvements in healthcare access, diagnostic capacity, immunization coverage, infrastructure development and system efficiency, particularly in tuberculosis diagnostics, radiology, dialysis and radiotherapy services. However, weak governance, poor stakeholder coordination, funding instability, affordability barriers and inequitable urban concentration of benefits persisted. Strengthening regulatory frameworks, sustainable financing, accountability and equitable access may enhance PPP implementation and enable appropriately governed PPPs to contribute to selected dimensions of healthcare access and service capacity relevant to universal health coverage in Nigeria.

title: Positive Predictive Value and Breast Cancer Histology by the Method of Detection Across a Multistate Health Care Enterprise.
abstract: Objective To compare the pathology outcomes of image-guided breast biopsies across a multistate health care enterprise by the method of detection (MOD), including the positive predictive value (PPV3) and histological types. Methods Biopsies from October 31, 2017, to July 6, 2023, across 18 imaging sites in 4 states were extracted. Radiologists prospectively assigned MODs, including symptomatic presentations (self-examination, clinical examination) and imaging modalities (mammogram, tomosynthesis, US, MRI, contrast-enhanced mammogram, molecular breast imaging, other imaging). For each MOD, the rates of malignancy and cancer subtypes were calculated. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed. Results In 26 932 biopsies on 22 582 patients (mean age 57.6 years ± 14.2 [SD]; 22 416 women), 6068 (81.1%) cancers were detected by screening, and 1144 (15.3%) were detected by symptoms. Symptomatic presentation MODs had a higher PPV3 (43.0% vs 25.6%; P < .001), larger cancer lesion sizes (x̄ = 27.5 mm vs x̄ = 17.8 mm; P < 001), and a higher association with invasive carcinoma (96.7% vs 76.8%; P <.001) compared with screening imaging-based MODs. Methods of detection with higher PPV3s also tended to have higher rates of invasive carcinoma (Spearman's ρ = 0.83). Conclusion Compared with breast cancers detected after symptomatic presentations, those identified via image-based screening were smaller and less often invasive, confirming the value of screening in early detection. Positive predictive value and the rate of invasive carcinoma varied in parallel across MODs.

title: Lessons Learned in the Early Adoption of Method of Detection Reporting.
abstract: Until recently, no breast cancer database in the United States records how breast cancers are initially detected, and, therefore, current data lack the fundamental ability to link breast cancer outcomes to screening directly. Consequently, the magnitude and relative contributions that screening and treatment play in the reduction of breast cancer mortality are unknown, and the debate over breast cancer screening continues. To address these shortcomings, advocates have proposed that the Method of Detection (MOD) be documented with every breast cancer diagnosis. MOD data can then be abstracted to cancer registries to provide direct evidence of the impact of screening on breast cancer diagnoses and subsequent outcomes and thereby resolve the debate about the benefits of screening. Given the widespread support of MOD reporting, there is also great potential to improve and facilitate its clinical implementation. Barriers to MOD adoption include a lack of an organized national breast cancer screening program, the cost of implementation, a lack of radiologist MOD training, and technical lapses, among others. The American College of Radiology and the Society of Breast Imaging have addressed barriers to MOD implementation through educational opportunities and the Breast Imaging Reporting and Data System 6th Edition provides comprehensive education on the MOD program. However, consistent and accurate MOD reporting and linkage to tumor registries on a national level will require a multifaceted approach to achieve success. Ultimately, the information gained from the direct role of MOD will result in breast cancer screening recommendations built on science-based policy.

title: Identifying Interventions to Reduce Breast Cancer Screening Barriers using Community Centered Prioritization Exercises.
abstract: PICK charts are Lean Six Sigma tools used to prioritize improvements based on effort required and potential impact. Our purpose was to conduct PICK chart prioritization exercises with a low income, diverse community advisory group to identify and prioritize patient and community centered interventions to reduce mammography screening disparities. Community advisory focus group was composed of 22 adults from low-income neighborhoods in Madison, Wisconsin. Included participants were from the Wisconsin Network for Research Support Community Advisory on Research Design and Strategies, recruited from community centers and food banks that serve individuals from diverse racial, socioeconomic, and educational backgrounds. Structured, divergent thinking brainstorming sessions were conducted to identify interventions to improve the mammography screening process. The idea generation process revealed 52 unique ideas across 7 process map domains. Among participants, the most highly cited ideas that were classified as high impact, low effort ideas included: reminders, sharing positive stories about mammography experiences, offering reassurance during mammograms, and reducing co-pays. Community centered prioritization exercises identify patient-centered, contextually relevant interventions to improve cancer screening percentages in medically underserved patient populations, including high-quality, patient centered communication about the mammography screening process and reduced costs.

title: Dual-Layer Spectral CT-Based Models for the Differential Diagnosis of Breast Lesions.
abstract: Objective To develop a hybrid model integrating morphological features with quantitative parameters from dual-layer spectral computed tomography (DSCT) to noninvasively differentiate benign breast lesions from breast cancer. Methods This retrospective study included patients with breast lesions incidentally detected on spectral CT between January 2020 and May 2024. Lesions were categorized as benign or malignant based on histopathology or greater than two years' stability on follow-up imaging. Clinical variables, morphological characteristics, and DSCT parameters were collected. The cohort was randomly divided into training, validation, and independent testing sets using stratified sampling. Feature selection was performed exclusively within the training set using univariate analysis, collinearity assessment, and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression with the one-standard-error criterion. Clinico-radiological, DSCT-based, and hybrid models were constructed using multivariate logistic regression. Model discrimination was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis and, model stability was assessed using nested cross-validation. A nomogram was constructed based on the best-performing model. Results A total of 102 patients (mean age 52 ± 11 years) were included, including 27 patients (26%) with benign breast lesions and 75 patients (74%) with breast cancer. In the independent testing set, the DSCT-based model outperformed the clinical-radiological model (AUC = 0.967 vs 0.933), while the hybrid model achieved the highest diagnostic performance (AUC, 0.983). Calibration curves demonstrated strong concordance between predicted and observed outcomes. Decision curve analysis indicated favorable net benefit. Conclusion The hybrid model demonstrated good diagnostic performance in noninvasively differentiating benign from malignant breast lesions detected preoperatively on DSCT.

title: Institutional Review of BI-RADS 5 and BI-RADS 4C Lesions Over 5 Years Following Surgical Excision: Analysis of Radiology-Pathology Correlation.
abstract: Objective To evaluate the performance of radiologists' radiologic-pathologic (rad-path) assessment in BI-RADS 4C and 5 breast lesions with benign core biopsy pathology. Methods Institutional pathology records were reviewed, analyzing surgical excision results for benign core biopsies after BI-RADS 4C and 5 assessments from 2019 to 2024, and the rad-path correlation issued by the radiologist prior to excision was recorded. Pathologic diagnoses and imaging data were retrieved from the electronic medical record. Results A total of 523 BI-RADS 4C and 5 core biopsies were identified during the study period. The malignancy rate following BI-RADS 4C assessment was 74.1% and following BI-RADS 5 assessment was 93.2%. Fifty-one benign image-guided biopsies underwent radiology-pathology correlation analysis. Radiologists categorized 19/51 benign pathology results as radiology-pathology discordant, with an upgrade rate to malignancy of 47.3%, and 32/51 as concordant, with an upgrade rate of 9.4%. All concordant upgrades occurred in high-risk lesions (atypical ductal hyperplasia, papilloma) for which excision had been recommended at the time of concordance assessment. Discordant benign pathology upgraded to malignancy included diagnoses such as dense stromal fibrosis, fibrocystic change, chronic inflammation, atypical ductal hyperplasia, hematoma, and papilloma. Conclusion Radiologist-performed rad-path correlation is highly reliable for benign BI-RADS 4C and 5 lesions. Radiology-pathology discordant benign biopsies carry a high risk of malignancy and warrant surgical excision. In contrast, radiology-pathology concordant benign results are highly predictive of final benign outcome, particularly when high-risk features are absent. These findings support the essential role of radiologist rad-path correlation in reducing unnecessary surgery and avoiding missed cancers.

title: Benchmark Evaluation of Vision-Enabled Large Language Models in Mammography: A Case-Control Study.
abstract: Objective To compare the diagnostic performance of five contemporary vision-enabled large language models (LLMs) in mammography interpretation using a case-control benchmark design. Methods A total of 200 cases were analyzed using a quota-balanced case-control design (100 malignant, BI-RADS 4-5; 100 controls, BI-RADS 1-2). All models (ChatGPT-5T, ChatGPT-5I, ChatGPT-4o, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and Gemini 2.5 Flash) received standard mammography images. Models were evaluated for lesion detection, laterality, quadrant localization, lesion type, and malignant-benign discrimination. Performance was assessed using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, balanced accuracy, Cohen's κ, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Breast density was recorded for all cases, while histopathological subtype and lesion size were documented for malignant cases. Results Lesion detection accuracy ranged from 79% to 91%, with high malignant sensitivity (92%-100%) but lower specificity in normal cases (24%-82%). ChatGPT-5T performed best in laterality (83%; κ = 0.70) and quadrant localization (73%; κ = 0.62). Lesion type classification was modest (74%-85%). In malignant-benign discrimination, ChatGPT-5T achieved the highest balanced accuracy (87%), while ChatGPT-4o showed poor specificity (28%). The study cohort was predominantly composed of lower-density breasts, larger lesions, and invasive ductal carcinoma as the most common subtype. Conclusion Vision-enabled LLMs demonstrated high sensitivity for breast lesion detection and classification tasks. More deliberative models, particularly ChatGPT-5T, consistently outperformed faster counterparts, especially in spatial reasoning tasks. However, reduced specificity in normal cases underscores that current LLM outputs should remain under radiologist supervision as supportive second-reader tools rather than standalone diagnostic systems. Given the quota-balanced design and cohort composition, results should be interpreted as comparative benchmarking rather than real-world diagnostic performance.

Performance was assessed using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, balanced accuracy, Cohen's κ, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Breast density was recorded for all cases, while histopathological subtype and lesion size were documented for malignant cases.

Results

Lesion detection accuracy ranged from 79% to 91%, with high malignant sensitivity (92%-100%) but lower specificity in normal cases (24%-82%). ChatGPT-5T performed best in laterality (83%; κ = 0.70) and quadrant localization (73%; κ = 0.62). Lesion type classification was modest (74%-85%). In malignant-benign discrimination, ChatGPT-5T achieved the highest balanced accuracy (87%), while ChatGPT-4o showed poor specificity (28%). The study cohort was predominantly composed of lower-density breasts, larger lesions, and invasive ductal carcinoma as the most common subtype.

Conclusion

Vision-enabled LLMs demonstrated high sensitivity for breast lesion detection and classification tasks. More deliberative models, particularly ChatGPT-5T, consistently outperformed faster counterparts, especially in spatial reasoning tasks. However, reduced specificity in normal cases underscores that current LLM outputs should remain under radiologist supervision as supportive second-reader tools rather than standalone diagnostic systems. Given the quota-balanced design and cohort composition, results should be interpreted as comparative benchmarking rather than real-world diagnostic performance.

title: Is Risk-based Screening Justified by the WISDOM Trial?
abstract: Widespread mammography screening has resulted in a significant decline in breast cancer deaths, but it is resource intensive. The WISDOM (Women Informed to Screen Depending on Measures of Risk) trial attempts to assess screening based on individual risk as an alternative to age-based screening (annual screening starting at age 40 years). In their initial report, the authors concluded that risk-based screening is safe and acceptable. Their results do not support this conclusion. The first primary endpoint to test the noninferiority of risk-based screening used the metric of stage IIB and higher breast cancers. Many of these cancers would be apparent on physical exam, thus eliminating some advantages of early detection and ignoring shortcomings of the risk-based approach. In addition, the study set an extremely weak noninferiority margin, compromising their conclusion concerning noninferiority. Details of mammography and MRI use in WISDOM reflect poor compliance with screening protocols in both arms of the study. Substantial non-compliance as well as out-of-study imaging in both cohorts resulted in two nearly identical protocols, rather than a comparison of different screening strategies. The study's findings of substantial non-compliance to the risk-based protocol make it difficult to justify risk-based screening being acceptable to women. The trial's second primary endpoint, to test whether risk-based screening yielded fewer biopsies than annual screening, failed. The risk-based screening protocol is labor intensive and would be challenging to implement in the typical primary care practice. The vast majority of breast cancers occur in average-risk women and could be missed in a risk-based system, especially in women under age 50 and minority women.

title: Fat Necrosis: Correlation of Imaging Findings and Histopathology.
abstract: Fat necrosis is an inflammatory response arising from damage to adipose tissue. Fat necrosis is a commonly encountered benign entity in breast imaging and has a wide spectrum of imaging appearances. Although fat necrosis is most commonly seen after intervention or trauma, it may be idiopathic. Given the overlap in imaging characteristics between fat necrosis and malignancy, understanding the various manifestations of fat necrosis can aid accurate diagnosis and help avoid unnecessary biopsy. We describe the range of imaging characteristics, including both classic benign imaging features and nonspecific features that can look worrisome for malignancy. Finally, we describe the radiologic-pathologic correlation of fat necrosis in the breast since biopsy with pathology is the gold standard for diagnosis in equivocal cases.

title: Integrated host vulnerability assessment using prognostic nutritional index and psoas muscle index for predicting chemotherapy-related toxicity in ovarian cancer: a multicenter JGOG9005S cohort analysis.
abstract: Objective To evaluate associations of prechemotherapy prognostic nutritional index (PNI) and computed tomography (CT)-derived muscle measures with severe chemotherapy-related toxicity in ovarian cancer and explore their combined assessment. Methods This multicenter retrospective cohort included 109 patients treated with platinum-taxane chemotherapy. PNI was calculated from laboratory values obtained immediately before the first chemotherapy cycle, irrespective of treatment sequence. Psoas muscle index (PMI) was measured centrally on baseline CT images. Associations with grade ≥ 3 chemotherapy-related adverse events were estimated using separate age- and stage-adjusted logistic models. Discrimination was compared among nested models in the same complete-case cohort. Cutoff-based and treatment-sequence analyses were exploratory. Results Grade ≥ 3 toxicity occurred in 63 patients (57.8%). Higher PNI and PMI were associated with lower odds of severe toxicity (adjusted odds ratios, 0.966 per PNI unit; 95% CI, 0.935-0.994; P = 0.024; and 0.598 per cm2/m2; 0.379-0.899; P = 0.018, respectively). The combined PNI-PMI model showed numerically improved discrimination compared with individual parameters (area under the curve, 0.694). In exploratory cohort-defined groups, toxicity occurred in 36.4%, 58.3%, and 75.7% of patients with zero, one, and two vulnerability domains, respectively; the adjusted odds ratio was 2.38 per domain (95% CI, 1.41-4.20, P = 0.0018). Conclusions Lower prechemotherapy PNI and lower baseline PMI were associated with severe chemotherapy-related toxicity. The combined model showed modest discrimination, and cohort-derived classifications require prospective external validation before clinical implementation.

title: A new microsimulation model of HPV natural history for comparison of novel cervical screening strategies.
abstract: Background The cost-effectiveness of cervical cancer screening strategies is estimated by health decision models. Fidelity to HPV natural history and multi-state carcinogenesis is critical to improve evaluations of new screening tests. Methods We developed a new health decision model of the HPV genotype-specific causal pathway to cervical cancer based on cohort, trial, and cross-sectional data. The novel model presents several new approaches in representing early HPV natural history: 1) transitions between health states are estimated by new statistical approaches adapted to handle intermittently-observed data; 2) transitions are directly estimated from observational data (i.e., statistically identifiable) rather than calibrated to fit; and 3) precancer is rigorously defined using histopathology and HPV genotyping as a surrogate for cancer risk. Results We present a model for pending policy decisions in Brazil. Model outputs closely match age-specific prevalence data from São Paulo for thirteen carcinogenic HPV types 16/18/31/33/35/45/52/58 (modeled individually) and 39/51/56/59/68 (grouped). The model-projected median age of precancer is 30.0 years (95% CI: 27.9-32.3 years). Conclusions By restricting model health states and transitions to the essential, directly observable causal pathway, our approach can generate metrics with measurable standard errors for cost-effectiveness analyses. Comparative modeling analyses are underway to assess differences in results relative to existing state-of-the-art models. Our approach can be generalized to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of an HPV-based screen-triage-treat approach with extended genotyping that has been demonstrated efficacious in nine PAVE Consortium countries.

title: Changes In body composition and subsequent risk of relapse In childhood hodgkin lymphoma.
abstract: Background Whether changes in body composition (skeletal muscle and adipose tissue, measured using computed tomography [CT] scans) are associated with relapse in children with Hodgkin lymphoma (HL) remains unknown. Methods We examined changes in body composition (skeletal muscle area [SMA] and total adipose tissue [TAT] area) of children with intermediate- and high-risk HL enrolled on Children's Oncology Group trials AHOD0031 and AHOD0831 using commercially available software from pre-treatment to after two cycles of chemotherapy. SMA or TAT values exceeding the median increase were classified as excessive gain, and those exceeding the median decline were classified as excessive loss in SMA or TAT. Proportional sub-distribution hazard regression models examined the association between change in body composition and relapse from end of cycle 2 treating non-relapse-related death as competing risk and adjusting for prognosticators including baseline SMA and TAT. Results Among the 951 children included in this analysis, the median age at diagnosis was 15.2y, 53.8% were male and 63.5% were non-Hispanic White. Excessive gain in TAT (observed in 36.2%) was associated with a 1.73-fold greater adjusted hazard of relapse (95% confidence interval [CI]=1.08-2.77, P=0.02) among children with negative PET2, but not among those with positive PET2 (hazard ratio [HR]=0.90, 95%CI=0.51-1.57, P=0.70) after adjusting for prognosticators. Excessive change in SMA was not associated with relapse. Conclusions This candidate biomarker is associated with an increased risk of relapse and presents a need to understand the underlying mechanisms for this association.

title: Foundation models for cancer: advancing diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment response-an NCI workshop report.
abstract: From March 24-26, 2026, the National Cancer Institute convened the Foundation Models for Cancer Workshop, bringing together more than thirty speakers from academia, government, and industry and attracting more than 2,000 registrants worldwide. The workshop examined the current state and future potential of foundation models and related artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in oncology. Presentations spanned single-cell biology, computational pathology, medical imaging, electronic health records, drug discovery, federated learning, and clinical decision support. Several themes emerged across the three-day meeting. First, the development of robust foundation models depends on access to high-quality, multimodal cancer datasets that are representative of the patient populations, disease stages, and clinical settings encountered in routine care. Second, prospective validation and evaluation in real-world clinical environments are essential for establishing the reliability, generalizability, and utility of AI-enabled tools. Third, while technical advances continue at a rapid pace, successful translation into cancer research and patient care will also require attention to implementation, workflow integration, interpretability, and data governance. Collectively, the workshop highlighted both the opportunities and challenges associated with applying foundation models to cancer research and clinical care and provided a forum for discussing future directions for the field.

title: Catamenial haemolacria and ocular pain as rare manifestations of extra-pelvic endometriosis.
abstract: Ocular involvement in endometriosis is an exceptionally rare extrapelvic manifestation, typically presenting as catamenial haemorrhagia. We report the case of an adolescent girl who presented with recurrent eye bleeding and pain during her menstruation. A comprehensive physical examination and imaging, including orbital magnetic resonance imaging, were unremarkable. Hematologic and ophthalmological evaluations excluded coagulopathies and structural ocular pathologies. Given the cyclical pattern of her symptoms and the absence of other identifiable causes, a presumptive diagnosis of ocular endometriosis was made. The patient was treated with a combination of dienogest and ethinyl estradiol, leading to significant symptom improvement over a two-year follow-up period. Occasional minimal haemolacria persisted, but no further intervention was required. This case underscores the importance of considering endometriosis in the differential diagnosis of catamenial haemolacria, even in the absence of radiological confirmation. A multidisciplinary approach and individualized hormonal therapy can result in substantial symptom control and improved quality of life in affected patients with catamenial haemolacria.

title: Anterior rib giant cell tumor of bone mimicking a malignant chest-wall tumor: a case report.
abstract: Giant cell tumor of bone (GCTB) rarely arises in the rib, and anterior rib involvement may mimic malignant chest-wall tumors. A 44-year-old woman presented with a palpable mass in the left anterior chest wall. Computed tomography (CT) revealed an osteolytic mass arising from the anterior left third rib, enlarging from 31 to 55 mm over ~2 months. Magnetic resonance imaging showed diffusion restriction, and fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/CT demonstrated intense uptake with a maximum standardized uptake value of 15.7, raising suspicion for malignancy. Needle biopsy suggested GCTB, but malignancy could not be excluded. Wide resection of the left second to fourth ribs was performed. Histology showed no sarcomatous transformation, and nuclear histone H3.3 with a glycine-to-tryptophan substitution at amino acid position 34 positivity in mononuclear tumor cells supported the diagnosis of GCTB. The patient remained recurrence-free for ~2 years. Anterior rib GCTB can mimic malignancy, requiring integrated radiological and pathological evaluation.

title: Ancient schwannoma of the gluteal region: a case report.
abstract: Schwannomas are benign peripheral nerve sheath tumors that rarely develop in the gluteal region. We describe a 35-year-old man with a 5-year history of a slowly enlarging left gluteal mass, which became painful after superficial ulceration developed. Ultrasonography and magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a well-circumscribed, heterogeneously enhancing solid lesion without evidence of invasion. Because malignancy could not be excluded on imaging, the mass was excised en bloc with clean margins without prior biopsy. Histopathology revealed encapsulated spindle cells arranged in a palisading pattern, with cystic degeneration and hemorrhage; immunohistochemistry was positive for S100, vimentin and calponin, confirming the diagnosis of ancient schwannoma. No recurrence occurred during 3 years of follow-up. Schwannoma should be considered in the differential diagnosis of gluteal mass, even in the absence of a positive Tinel sign.

title: Duodenal perforation masquerading as an intra-abdominal abscess: successful management with pedicled falciformopexy.
abstract: Duodenal perforation typically presents as an acute abdomen. In contrast, presentation as an intra-abdominal abscess is rare and may delay diagnosis. We report a 25-year-old male who presented with 8 days of upper abdominal pain and 4 days of progressive abdominal distension. Despite marked abdominal distension, he had no signs of peritonitis. Laboratory investigations showed marked leukocytosis. Chest radiography showed no classical subdiaphragmatic free air, whereas computed tomography confirmed pneumoperitoneum. Emergency exploratory laparotomy revealed an intra-abdominal abscess with dense omental adhesions encasing the bowel. A 1 × 1 cm perforation on the anterior wall of the first part of the duodenum was identified. As the omentum was unsuitable for conventional patch repair, the perforation was successfully repaired using a pedicled falciform ligament flap. This case highlights an uncommon presentation of duodenal perforation and demonstrates the falciform ligament flap as an effective alternative when omental patch repair is not feasible.

title: Lymphogranuloma venereum presenting as a giant rectal ulcer with inguinal lymphadenitis: a case report.
abstract: Anorectal lymphogranuloma venereum (LGV) can mimic rectal malignancy, but diagnosis may be challenging when LGV-specific serovar testing is unavailable. A 26-year-old man who has sex with men presented with hematochezia and increased bowel movement frequency. Colonoscopy revealed a large deep rectal ulcer with mucopurulent exudate, and pelvic magnetic resonance imaging showed rectal wall thickening with regional lymphadenopathy, raising concern for rectal cancer. Histopathology showed inflammatory changes without malignancy. Rectal secretion testing was positive for Chlamydia trachomatis RNA, and the patient was clinically diagnosed with probable anorectal LGV. Oral doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 21 days led to marked ulcer regression at 3 weeks and near-complete mucosal healing by 6 weeks. This case highlights the importance of considering sexually transmitted proctitis in young men who have sex with men patients with atypical rectal ulcers.

title: Gastric volvulus following Nissen fundoplication: a case report and review of reported cases, risk factors, and management strategies.
abstract: Gastric volvulus is a rare but potentially life-threatening complication following Nissen fundoplication, with delayed diagnosis increasing the risk of gastric ischemia, necrosis, and perforation. We report the case of a 72-year-old man who presented on postoperative Day 10 with progressive dysphagia, severe epigastric pain, and intolerance to oral intake following robot-assisted laparoscopic Nissen fundoplication. Computed tomography and upper gastrointestinal contrast study demonstrated marked gastric distension with obstruction at the gastroesophageal junction. Urgent diagnostic laparoscopy revealed a complete retroesophageal organoaxial gastric volvulus around an intact fundoplication wrap. The patient subsequently underwent robot-assisted gastric decompression, reduction of the volvulus, takedown of the fundoplication, and posterior gastropexy. Postoperative recovery was uneventful. This case highlights the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion for gastric volvulus in patients with persistent obstructive symptoms after fundoplication and demonstrates that prompt minimally invasive surgical intervention can prevent catastrophic complications.

title: Modified Sullivan-type segment III hepatojejunostomy for radiologically presumed unresectable hilar cholangiocarcinoma: a technical case report.
abstract: Hilar cholangiocarcinoma may present with advanced biliary obstruction requiring palliation. An 80-year-old frail woman with jaundice and severe pruritus had contrast-enhanced computed tomography findings radiologically consistent with Bismuth-Corlette type IV hilar cholangiocarcinoma. No tissue diagnosis was obtained. Cancer antigen 19-9, carcinoembryonic antigen, alkaline phosphatase, magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography, endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography, and percutaneous transhepatic cholangiography were unavailable at the treating hospital and were not performed. Because referral and non-operative biliary drainage were not feasible and the patient requested active symptom-directed treatment, a modified Sullivan-type segment III hepatojejunostomy was performed. Operative time was 85 min and blood loss 100 ml. Pruritus resolved and bilirubin decreased from 191.78 to 127.81 μmol/l by postoperative Day 10. The patient died ~2 months later from disease progression. The procedure therefore provided short-term symptomatic improvement and partial biochemical improvement only, illustrating a potential palliative option when standard drainage modalities are inaccessible.

title: Primary Epstein-Barr virus-negative lymphoepithelioma-like carcinoma of the supraglottic larynx mimicking nasopharyngeal carcinoma: a case report.
abstract: Lymphoepithelioma-like carcinoma (LELC) of the larynx is exceptionally rare and can closely mimic undifferentiated nasopharyngeal carcinoma. A 78-year-old man presented with progressive dysphonia and dysphagia. Endoscopy and computed tomography showed a supraglottic lesion with bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy (cT2N2M0). Biopsy demonstrated poorly differentiated non-keratinizing carcinoma with dense lymphoid stroma and a Schmincke-type pattern. Tumor cells were positive for p40, p63, and pancytokeratins; Epstein-Barr virus testing was negative. After exclusion of a nasopharyngeal primary, the diagnosis of primary laryngeal LELC was established. Definitive cisplatin-based chemoradiotherapy with intensity-modulated radiotherapy (70 Gy in 35 fractions) achieved complete clinical and radiological response at 12 months with preserved swallowing and phonatory function.

title: Robot-assisted total laparoscopic pancreaticoduodenectomy with transvaginal specimen extraction: a case report.
abstract: Natural orifice specimen extraction surgery reduces incision-related complications and accelerates postoperative recovery while maintaining oncologic safety, whereas the da Vinci robotic surgical system further enhances the precision of minimally invasive procedures. This case report describes a robot-assisted total laparoscopic pancreaticoduodenectomy combined with transvaginal specimen extraction (RPD-TVSE). The patient was a 64-year-old female with moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma of the descending duodenum. The procedure took 350 min, with intraoperative blood loss of 200 mL; no blood transfusion was administered during the perioperative period. The patient was able to ambulate on postoperative day 1, with no adverse events recorded. Histopathology confirmed tumor staging as pT2N0M0, with all surgical margins negative. At 12-month follow-up, no evidence of recurrence was observed. This case demonstrates that RPD-TVSE is technically feasible and yields favorable short-term outcomes, providing a novel minimally invasive surgical option for female patients. However, long-term oncologic safety requires further investigation and validation.

title: Nerve-sparing resection of cervical vagal schwannoma with complete functional recovery: a case report.
abstract: Vagal schwannomas are rare benign neoplasms arising from the Schwann cells of the vagus nerve, representing 2%-5% of all peripheral nerve tumors and ~10% of head and neck schwannomas. They typically present as slow-growing, asymptomatic lateral neck masses and pose significant diagnostic and surgical challenges due to their proximity to critical neurovascular structures. We report a case of a 28-year-old Asian male who presented with a right-sided neck swelling. Imaging workup including ultrasound, magnetic resonance imaging, and computed tomography angiography identified a well-defined mass in the right carotid space at the level of C4-C5, displacing adjacent vascular structures. The tumor was surgically excised en bloc via a lateral transverse approach with full preservation of vagal nerve function, confirmed by intraoperative nerve monitoring. Histopathology confirmed the diagnosis of vagal schwannoma. This case highlights the importance of a multidisciplinary approach, thorough preoperative imaging, and meticulous intraoperative technique in achieving complete resection with minimal morbidity.

title: Primary borderline retroperitoneal mucinous cystic neoplasm and situs inversus totalis: a case report.
abstract: Primary retroperitoneal mucinous cystic neoplasms (PRMCNs) are rare tumors classified into cystadenoma, PRMCN with borderline malignancy (PRMCN-BM), and cystadenocarcinoma. We report a 60-year-old woman with left flank abdominal pain whose MRI revealed situs inversus totalis alongside a complex cystic lesion in the left retroperitoneum measuring 4.8 × 5.2 × 4.5 cm. She underwent laparotomy with complete resection of the lesion, and histopathology confirmed a primary retroperitoneal neoplasm with borderline malignancy, with an uneventful postoperative course and no recurrence after 8 months. To date, only 35 cases of mucinous cystadenomas with borderline malignancy have been documented in the literature. Clinical presentation is variable, imaging lacks specific diagnostic criteria, and serum tumor markers have no diagnostic value. Surgical resection remains the curative therapeutic approach, and histopathology is essential for the definitive diagnosis, which continues to pose a preoperative challenge.

title: Myofibrosarcoma of the maxillary sinus with orbital floor involvement: a case report.
abstract: Myofibrosarcoma is a rare spindle-cell malignancy with myofibroblastic differentiation, and primary maxillary sinus involvement is exceptional. A 36-year-old woman presented with progressive unilateral nasal obstruction, purulent rhinorrhea, and hemifacial pain. Computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a destructive 44 × 45 × 57 mm right maxillary sinus mass involving the orbital floor and extending into the nasal cavity, ethmoid cells, and pterygopalatine fossa. Histology and immunohistochemistry supported the diagnosis of myofibrosarcoma. Partial maxillectomy with titanium orbital floor reconstruction was performed. Several soft-tissue margins were positive, whereas gingival and bony margins were clear. Postoperative radiotherapy delivered 66 Gy in 33 fractions. This case illustrates the diagnostic complexity of sinonasal spindle-cell tumors and the individualized role of radiotherapy when local control is threatened by anatomically constrained positive-margin disease.

title: Delayed diagnosis of congenital pulmonary airway malformation in an infant: diagnostic challenges and surgical implications.
abstract: Although congenital pulmonary airway malformation (CPAM) is usually diagnosed during prenatal screening, delayed presentation may increase diagnostic uncertainty and operative complexity. We report, to our knowledge, the first case of CPAM diagnosed and surgically managed in Syria in a 4-month-old infant presenting with a 1-month history of dyspnea, fever, and poor feeding in the absence of routine prenatal screening. Initial chest radiography, although technically limited, demonstrated a rounded opacity in the right hemithorax, while non-contrast chest computed tomography (CT) revealed multicystic lesions with a hyperattenuating intralesional component, raising suspicion for secondary infection or pleuropulmonary blastoma (PPB). The patient underwent right upper and middle bilobectomy, and histopathological examination confirmed CPAM and excluded PPB. This case highlights the complementary roles of postnatal CT, surgery, and histopathology in confirming CPAM and excluding PPB, particularly when delayed presentation increases operative complexity.

title: Sporadic ampullary adenoma mimicking adenocarcinoma in the absence of genetic predisposition: a case report.
abstract: Ampullary tumors are uncommon and are frequently associated with hereditary cancer syndromes. Sporadic ampullary adenomas are infrequently reported and may mimic adenocarcinoma clinically and radiographically. We present a 71-year-old male with obstructive jaundice and imaging concerning for malignancy who was found to have a high-grade ampullary adenoma following attempted pancreaticoduodenectomy. Operative management required modification of the standard approach due to intraoperative anatomical distortions. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges in differentiating benign from malignant ampullary lesions and the implications for surgical management.

title: Internal herniation through Petersen's defect following Roux-en-Y gastric bypass presenting as subacute bilateral lower extremity edema due to IVC compression - a case report.
abstract: A 38-year-old woman with a history of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) 2 years prior presented to the bariatric clinic on multiple occasions with postprandial abdominal pain and bloating and bilateral lower extremity edema. Abdominal pain did not improve despite antiacid medication and dietary recommendations. Computed tomography scan of the abdomen revealed an internal hernia (IH) through Petersen's defect (a potential space between the Roux limb and transverse colon), with a mass effect on the inferior vena cava by herniated bowel. Diagnostic laparoscopy confirmed the diagnosis. Reduction of the hernia and defect closure resulted in full symptom resolution. This case highlights the importance of high clinical suspicion for IH in any patient with a history of RYGB and abdominal pain, even when symptoms are chronic and/or atypical. Early recognition is important for prompt treatment and prevention of bowel ischemia and necrosis.

title: Emphysematous gastritis with extensive portal venous gas and endoscopic mucosal necrosis: gastric preservation despite an alarming presentation.
abstract: Emphysematous gastritis (EG) is a rare, potentially life-threatening condition. Extensive gastric pneumatosis and portal venous gas may suggest irreversible ischemia, although radiological severity and mucosal injury do not necessarily indicate transmural necrosis. A 70-year-old man presented with acute epigastric pain and vomiting. Computed tomography (CT) demonstrated extensive gastric and duodenal pneumatosis with portomesenteric venous gas but patent visceral arteries. Immediately after CT, he developed cardiac arrest, with return of spontaneous circulation after approximately 14 min. Emergency laparoscopy showed a viable stomach without perforation or transmural necrosis, whereas intraoperative endoscopy demonstrated extensive necrotic-appearing gastric mucosa. Gastrectomy was therefore avoided. Follow-up CT 4 days later showed complete resolution of pneumatosis and portomesenteric venous gas. The patient subsequently died from post-anoxic neurological injury and multiorgan failure. Surgical exploration and gastric resection should remain distinct decisions in severe EG, integrating imaging, endoscopy, and direct assessment of gastric viability.

title: Documented Fracture-Healing Outcomes After Operative and Nonoperative Management of Closed Mid-Diaphyseal Humerus Fractures in Active-Duty Service Members.
abstract: Introduction Closed diaphyseal humerus fracture treatment is nuanced with regard to the selection of surgical candidates. Fracture union is crucial, with historical data suggesting rivaling union rates between operative and nonoperative treatment; however, recent literature suggests increased union rates with operative treatment. Although nonoperative treatment of most fracture patterns is supported by the literature, there remains an argument for operative treatment for select patient populations, especially when considering union rates. Evidence regarding fracture-healing outcomes in young active-duty populations remains limited. We sought to characterize documented fracture-healing outcomes after operative and nonoperative management of closed diaphyseal humerus fractures in active-duty service members and to evaluate completeness of healing-status ascertainment. Methods This study queried the Medical Assessment and Readiness System (MARS), Womack Army Medical Center, Fort Bragg, NC, which contains information from the Military Health System (MHS) care system. This study defined a retrospective cohort of patients diagnosed with closed diaphyseal humerus fractures (OTA/AO 12A/B/C), using International Classification of Diseases (9th and 10th revision) codes, sustained from January 2011 to December 2022. Treatment type, including operative or nonoperative, was identified. We excluded patients with open humerus fractures; proximal humerus fractures; distal humerus fractures; and those treated with external fixation. The primary outcome measure was a diagnosis of union or malunion/nonunion. Unadjusted comparisons between groups were conducted using likelihood ratio chi-square tests. Results The study population comprised 402 patients with closed humeral diaphyseal fractures; 314 (78.1%) were managed nonoperatively and 88 (21.9%) operatively. Fracture-healing status could be classified in 216 patients (53.7%), whereas 186 (46.3%) lacked sufficient documentation to determine the primary outcome. Outcome ascertainment was more complete after operative than nonoperative management (61/88 [69.3%] vs. 155/314 [49.4%]; P = .001). Among those with documented healing status, union occurred in 149 of 155 nonoperatively managed fractures (96.1%; 95% CI, 91.8%-98.6%) and 59 of 61 operatively managed fractures (96.7%; 95% CI, 88.7%-99.6%). Discussion Among active-duty service members with documented healing status after closed diaphyseal humerus fracture, observed union rates were high after both nonoperative and operative management. However, treatment was nonrandom, important fracture-specific treatment-selection variables were unavailable, and healing status was determined from available clinical documentation, recorded radiographic interpretations, diagnosis codes, and revision procedures rather than standardized radiographic adjudication. These limitations, together with incomplete and differential outcome ascertainment and few nonunion/malunion events, preclude estimation of a comparative treatment effect. The findings should therefore be interpreted descriptively rather than as evidence of equivalence between operative and nonoperative treatment.

title: The Ongoing Utility of Historical Military Photofluorographs-Tools to Identify Fallen US Soldiers From Past Wars as Cross-Validated by DNA and Dental Data in 180 Cases.
abstract: Introduction Mass chest X-ray formed a routine part of induction processes to the US armed forces in the 1940-1950s for tuberculosis screening. Today, the skeletal structure recorded in these medical miniature films serves to identify these same soldiers. In the US military's accounting/repatriation setting, chest radiograph comparisons have grown to be a primary identification mechanism alongside DNA and dental records. Identifications are now routinely conducted with contributions from miniature radiographic films. This article reviews the miniature radiographic film as an identification tool and provides the first evaluation of findings (180 cases) against gold standards of DNA and dental analyses for the very same cases. Materials and methods This article reviews both miniature film photofluorographs and the standardized chest radiograph comparison (CXR) protocol employed by the Defense POW/MIA Accounting Agency (DPAA) for identification. Additionally, all DPAA cases (2010-2025) where radiographic CXR resulted in a match result (280) were reviewed for additional DNA and/or dental record findings, providing 180 cases where dual-modality result existed to cross-validation test the radiographic analyses. Results For 172 DNA cases, there was no instance of disagreement between the chest radiograph result and the independently acquired Armed Forces DNA Identification Laboratory's DNA result. For 8 dental cases reporting a positive match result, the CXR identity finding was identical (both evidence lines identified the same person). To be conservative, we assume that the next future CXR case to be conducted using miniature films will yield an erroneous result, thereby setting a positive predictive value for radiographic comparison of 99.4% (=180 correct results/181 total decisions). Conclusions Miniature chest radiographs provide useful identification-relevant information. DPAA casework provides a rare circumstance to evaluate the accuracy of miniature film radiograph comparisons across a large sample, as multiple independent and parallel lines of analysis exist for single cases. Evaluation of these cases (180 in total) reveals that the military miniature films supply the same name associations that DNA and forensic odontology provide. The positive predictive value is high (99.4%), conservatively assuming the next case to be an incorrect one. This confirms the value of the miniature chest film and CXR methods, when DNA and dental records alone are unable to provide definitive answers.

title: IgG4-related kidney disease: treatment standard.
abstract: IgG4-related disease is a systemic, immune-mediated, fibro-inflammatory condition that can affect virtually any organ. IgG4-related kidney disease represents one of the most clinically relevant manifestations and encompasses a spectrum of renal manifestations, including IgG4-related tubulointerstitial nephritis, membranous nephropathy, and obstructive uropathy secondary to retroperitoneal fibrosis. The diagnosis remains challenging and requires integration of clinical and laboratory findings, along with imaging, and histopathology, as no single biomarker is sufficiently sensitive or specific. Although systemic immunosuppressive therapies largely overlap across manifestations, the practical management differs substantially between parenchymal kidney disease and retroperitoneal fibrosis, particularly with regard to mechanisms of kidney injury, the need for interventional procedures, treatment goals, and monitoring strategies. Glucocorticoids are the cornerstone of induction therapy and typically provide rapid clinical responses; however, the chronic-relapsing course of IgG4-related disease and the burden of glucocorticoid-related toxicity have prompted investigation in steroid-sparing strategies. Conventional immunosuppressive agents have been used with controversial results, whereas B-cell-targeting therapies, particularly rituximab, have demonstrated high efficacy in both induction and maintenance settings. Management should ultimately be individualised, taking into account the pattern of renal involvement, organ dysfunction, and likelihood of reversibility. In patients with obstructive uropathy due to retroperitoneal fibrosis, interventional procedures may be required alongside immunosuppressive therapy. Long-term monitoring is essential because of the relapsing nature of the disease and the potential for chronic kidney disease. This Treatment Standard provides a practical, nephrology-oriented framework for the diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of IgG4-related kidney disease, integrating current evidence with emerging insights from immunopathogenesis and clinical trials.

title: An evidence-based workflow for integrating molecular testing with histopathology in the workup of meningiomas.
abstract: Background Meningiomas are graded using histologic and molecular criteria according to the World Health Organization (WHO) classification. However, there is scant evidence considering the specific value of each individual atypical histological feature that contributes to WHO grading. There is also little evidence-based guidance as to which cases should receive molecular testing. Methods Detailed histological information was collected for 1058 resected meningiomas, including cases with genomic DNA methylation and copy number variant (CNV) data, next-generation sequencing, and RNA risk score. Integrated analyses were conducted using known prognostic variables, including WHO Grade, Ki-67, mitotic index (MI), and atypical histologic features (necrosis, hypercellularity, macronucleoli, sheeting, and small cells). Results Necrosis, elevated MI, and increased WHO grade correlated with specific DNA methylation patterns, RNA risk groups, and chromosomal CNVs. Predictive analysis identified MI as the strongest single correlate, and suggested the presence of ≥ 2 atypical features as an optimal threshold for recurrence prediction. Sheeting architecture was the only independent histologic correlate of recurrence. Integration of histologic and molecular features suggests that tumors with high MI have poor prognosis regardless of molecular profile. Further analysis of low MI tumors revealed specific predictors of unfavorable molecular profiles. Conclusions These data indicate that some atypical histopathologic features are more powerful than others, and can be used on initial screening to increase the yield of molecular profiling of meningiomas. Furthermore, we propose that molecular testing may actually have greatest added value in cases with low, not high, MI.

title: AI in Neuro-Oncology: An Overarching Review.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being applied across neuro-oncology domains to analyze complex, high-dimensional, multimodal data. Despite major advances in the biological understanding and classification of CNS tumors, clinical outcomes for many of them remain poor, reflecting intra- and inter-tumor heterogeneity and limitations of conventional reductionist approaches. AI offers a paradigm shift to capture this heterogeneity and provide quantitative, reproducible diagnostic, predictive, and prognostic insights. This article describes a joint effort across the Response Assessment in Neuro-Oncology (RANO) working groups to provide an overarching review of the AI use across six key domains of neuro-oncology: neuroimaging, neuropathology, laboratory medicine, neurosurgery, drug discovery, and clinical trials. Applications closest to clinical use include imaging segmentation and quantification, AI-assisted image reconstruction, DNA methylation-based classification, and workflow optimization. Radiogenomics, WSI-based molecular prediction, AI-guided surgical targeting, liquid biopsy interpretation, AI-guided drug discovery, digital twins, and in silico trials remain promising but require stronger prospective validation. Key challenges include limited availability of large diverse datasets, variability in data acquisition and reference standards, and limited external validation. This review provides a unifying framework for understanding the role of AI across neuro-oncology and highlights key considerations for its responsible implementation, emphasizing standardization, reproducibility, multi-institutional validation, and human oversight.

title: MRI-Based Machine Learning to Differentiate True Progression from Pseudoprogression in Glioblastoma: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Background Differentiating true progression (TP) from pseudoprogression (PsP) after chemoradiation for glioblastoma remains clinically difficult. We evaluated externally validated diagnostic performance of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based machine learning models and appraised study quality and transparency. Methods PubMed, Embase, MEDLINE, and Cochrane Library were searched through October 1, 2025 (PROSPERO registration CRD420251144894). Eligible adult glioblastoma studies used MRI-based machine learning to distinguish TP from PsP against histopathology and/or clinicoradiologic follow-up. The primary meta-analysis included external test cohorts with extractable 2 × 2 data; internal and combined internal and external test analyses were secondary. Diagnostic accuracy was synthesized with bivariate random-effects models. Results Thirty-one studies including 2,344 patients undergoing imaging assessment were included. Seven external test cohorts, including 219 patient observations, entered the primary meta-analysis. Pooled sensitivity was 0.78 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.63-0.88), specificity was 0.75 (95% CI, 0.63-0.84), and summary area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was 0.81 (bootstrap 95% CI, 0.69-0.91). Internal test cohorts showed higher apparent performance than external cohorts (AUC, 0.91 vs 0.81), but the difference was not statistically significant (difference, -0.09; 95% CI, -0.22 to 0.02; P = 0.12). Risk of bias was frequently high or unclear, and reporting transparency was heterogeneous. Conclusions MRI-based machine learning showed moderate-to-good external validation performance for TP-versus-PsP discrimination, but evidence remains limited by small external test cohorts, bias, and incomplete reporting. Larger transparent multicenter validations are needed before routine clinical implementation.

title: Keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma of the distal Esophagus in a young adult woman with celiac disease: a case report.
abstract: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) usually affects the upper or middle esophagus and is strongly associated with tobacco and alcohol use. We report a 28-year-old woman with longstanding celiac disease who presented with progressive dysphagia, weight loss, retrosternal pain, and melena. Endoscopy showed a partially obstructing distal esophageal mass; biopsy confirmed moderately differentiated keratinizing ESCC, while duodenal biopsy showed active celiac disease. CT and PET imaging revealed regional lymphadenopathy without distant metastasis. She underwent feeding jejunostomy, nutritional support, and neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy, but follow-up imaging showed interval disease progression. The patient's young age, squamous cell histology in a distal esophagus, and the absence of conventional risk factors make this an unusual presentation. This case emphasizes the need for high clinical suspicion and early endoscopic evaluation in young patients with celiac disease presenting with alarming symptoms, even in the absence of classic risk factors for esophageal cancer.

title: Inflammatory Pseudotumor of the liver mimicking peritoneal Carcinomatosis: a diagnostic challenge.
abstract: Inflammatory pseudotumor of the liver is a rare benign entity with non-specific radiological features that can closely mimic malignant hepatic lesions, making its diagnosis challenging. We report the case of a patient in whom a focal hepatic lesion was detected on abdominal ultrasound, with imaging findings consistent with underlying cirrhosis. Subsequent contrast-enhanced computed tomography demonstrated a dysmorphic liver with infiltrative subcapsular hepatic masses, associated with micronodular infiltration of the peritoneal fat and cardiophrenic angle lymphadenopathy, raising strong suspicion for a malignant hepatic process with peritoneal carcinomatosis. The diagnosis of inflammatory pseudotumor was ultimately confirmed by a CT-guided percutaneous liver biopsy. This case emphasizes the importance of considering inflammatory pseudotumor in the differential diagnosis of hepatic lesions, as this entity may closely mimic malignant etiologies on imaging.

title: An elusive cause of recurrent hypoglycemia: delayed diagnosis of insulinoma treated with curative distal pancreatectomy in a resource-limited setting.
abstract: A 43-year-old woman presented with recurrent hypoglycemia and episodes of loss of consciousness. On admission, her blood glucose was 37 mg/dL (reference range: 70-99 mg/dl), with recovery after intravenous dextrose, fulfilling Whipple's triad. She had a two-year history of dizziness, fatigue, diaphoresis, and neuroglycopenic symptoms, often relieved by frequent soft drink intake, leading to weight gain. She was previously misdiagnosed with a neurologic disorder, resulting in delayed evaluation. Laboratory findings showed elevated serum insulin levels of 65 μU/mL (reference range: 2.6-24.9 μU/mL) during hypoglycemia. Contrast-enhanced CT identified a 1.7 × 1.3 cm mass in the pancreatic body without metastasis. The patient underwent distal pancreatectomy with splenectomy. Postoperatively, hypoglycemic episodes resolved completely. Histopathology confirmed insulinoma. This case highlights the importance of considering insulinoma in patients with recurrent hypoglycemia. Delayed diagnosis may occur due to nonspecific symptoms and misdiagnosis. Careful clinical assessment, basic biochemical testing, and imaging can facilitate timely diagnosis and effective surgical management in resource-limited settings.

title: Left pulmonary aplasia with ipsilateral renal agenesis and double superior vena cava in a term neonate: a case report.
abstract: Background Unilateral pulmonary agenesis/aplasia is rare and often accompanied by extrapulmonary anomalies that affect prognosis. Case report A term male neonate delivered by cesarean section for fetal distress required brief invasive ventilation and was subsequently stabilized. Chest radiography revealed left hemithorax opacification. Contrast-enhanced CT on day 4 demonstrated a reduced left hemithorax with an absent left pulmonary parenchyma, a blind-ending left main bronchus, and an absent ipsilateral pulmonary arterial supply, consistent with left pulmonary aplasia. Evaluation also identified left renal agenesis with compensatory right renal hypertrophy and double superior vena cava, with discordant drainage descriptions across modalities requiring confirmation. The infant transitioned to room air, established feeds, and was discharged clinically stable on day 9 after birth. Conclusion Definitive anatomic characterization of unilateral thoracic opacity in neonates should prompt systematic cardiovascular and genitourinary screening and coordinated multidisciplinary follow-up in an outpatient setting.

title: Durable response to vebreltinib in heavily pretreated MET-amplified intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma: a case report.
abstract: Background MET amplification, although detected in only 2%-5% of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinomas (ICC), represents an actionable oncogenic driver. Treatment options after failure of first-line immunochemotherapy remain limited, and clinical data on vebreltinib, a novel highly selective MET inhibitor, in this molecular subset are scarce. Case presentation A 61-year-old woman with metastatic ICC harboring high-level MET amplification (tissue gene copy number, 26.79) experienced disease progression on first-line durvalumab plus gemcitabine/cisplatin, second-line liposomal irinotecan/fluorouracil plus lenvatinib and durvalumab, radiotherapy, and transarterial chemoembolization. Following a brief period of vebreltinib (200 mg twice daily) plus durvalumab that was interrupted by grade 4 myelosuppression, the patient continued on vebreltinib monotherapy after hematologic recovery. Restaging computed tomography demonstrated a partial response (PR), with carbohydrate antigen 19-9 normalizing (a 99.2% reduction). This response lasted over 6 months until eventual disease progression.
