title: Gray and white matter structural alterations in migraine with and without aura: A multimodal MRI and JuSpace analysis.
abstract: Objective To characterize gray and white matter structural alterations in migraine without aura (MwoA) and migraine with aura (MwA) relative to healthy controls (HC), test direct differences between the migraine groups, and examine spatial associations between voxel-based morphometry findings and molecular and cellular reference templates. Background Structural and diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) studies have reported gray and white matter abnormalities in migraine, but findings vary across cohorts, imaging methods, and clinical subgroups. Whether migraine with and without aura show distinct structural patterns remains uncertain, and the molecular and cellular context of these alterations is incompletely understood. Methods This cross-sectional group-comparison analysis was embedded in an ongoing prospective single-center study at The First Affiliated Hospital of Dalian Medical University in Dalian, China, and included participants recruited from August 2025 to March 2026. Thirty HC, 40 participants with MwoA, and 15 participants with MwA underwent T1-weighted and diffusion MRI. Diffusion tensor imaging, neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging, and diffusional kurtosis imaging metrics were analyzed using tract-based spatial statistics; gray matter microstructure and volume were assessed using gray matter-based spatial statistics and voxel-based morphometry (VBM). JuSpace Toolbox correlated unthresholded VBM statistical parametric t (spmT) maps with neurotransmitter- and cell-related templates. Models adjusted for age, sex, and education; VBM additionally adjusted for total intracranial volume; and direct MwoA-versus-MwA sensitivity models included Patient Health Questionnaire-9. Results Relative to HC, MwoA showed higher mean and radial diffusivity and lower neurite density index, whereas MwA showed lower free-water fraction (all threshold-free cluster enhancement-family-wise error [FWE], p < 0.05). No diffusional kurtosis imaging or corrected gray matter-based spatial statistics result was significant. VBM showed lower gray matter volume in MwoA in left cerebellar Crus I (77 voxels; peak-level whole-brain family-wise error (FWE)-corrected p value (pFWE) = 0.022) and right inferior frontal gyrus, pars triangularis (6 voxels; pFWE = 0.025), and in MwA in right inferior frontal gyrus, pars triangularis (85 voxels; pFWE = 0.019). Direct MwoA-versus-MwA comparisons were nonsignificant in primary and Patient Health Questionnaire-9-adjusted models. JuSpace identified seven and 11 false discovery rate (FDR)-significant neurotransmitter-related associations for MwoA-versus-HC and MwA-versus-HC, respectively; no cell-related template survived FDR correction for MwoA-versus-HC, whereas nine survived for MwA-versus-HC (q < 0.05). No region of interest-clinical association survived Bonferroni correction. Conclusion Multimodal MRI identified gray and white matter alterations in both migraine groups relative to HC, whereas direct MwoA-versus-MwA comparisons were nonsignificant. JuSpace provided complementary spatial context for the VBM findings. These results broaden the structural characterization of migraine but do not establish imaging differences between the two migraine groups.

title: Association between bacterial load and volumetric bone loss in teeth with persistent apical periodontitis: A cone-beam computed tomography segmentation-based observational study.
abstract: Aim To quantitatively compare the bacterial DNA load in root apices and periapical lesions surgically retrieved from teeth with failed root canal treatment, and to investigate the association between bacterial DNA load in both anatomical locations and the three-dimensional (3D) volumetric extent of periapical bone loss, as well as relevant clinical and demographic variables. Methodology Root apices and periapical lesions were surgically obtained from patients with failed root canal treatments. Samples were cryopulverized and bacterial DNA was quantified by q-PCR assay. The volume of the periapical lesions was calculated by cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) images segmentation using Blue Sky Bio software. Demographic and clinical data including gender, age, previous retreatment, tenderness to percussion, tooth position, and periapical healing after 1 year were preliminarily associated with the lesion volume. Normality of the variables was analyzed by the Shapiro Wilk test, and global comparisons were explored by ANOVA when variances were similar. The Student t test was used for pair-by-pair comparisons. Results Seventy-nine samples (40 root apices and 39 lesions) were successfully amplified. A greater number of DNA copies was found in apices as compared with apical lesions (p < 0.05). Analysis by lesion volume showed that a higher bacterial load in apices was associated with larger apical lesions, as well as in lesions of patients under 50 years old (p < 0.05). Clinical parameters such as tooth position and patient age showed an association with the volume of apical lesions (p < 0.05). Conclusions Root apices harbour higher bacterial DNA than periapical lesions, regardless of the volume of apical bone loss. Apices associated with large volume lesions present a greater amount of bacterial DNA. Preliminary associations were identified between certain clinical and demographic factors (age and tooth position) and increased lesion volume.

title: Melanoma Prognostication Using AI-Guided Histopathology.
abstract: Accurate diagnosis and risk stratification are central for optimal management of patients with melanoma. Current American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) staging systems inadequately stratify patients with clinically meaningful metastatic potential. Manual histopathologic interpretation compounds this limitation, particularly for diagnostically ambiguous lesions at the benign-malignant interface, where concordance is highly variable. This review examines how computational pathology and convolutional neural networks (CNNs) can improve histopathologic diagnosis and risk stratification of melanoma, evaluate current image-based deep learning (DL) approaches, and outline a path toward explainable, multimodal prognostic tools. We review published DL models applied to hematoxylin and eosin whole-slide images (H&E WSIs) for melanoma diagnosis, subtype classification, and survival prediction, and discuss integration with transcriptomic and spatial proteomic data modalities. Computational pathology, informed by deep learning, can reliably identify melanomas at risk of disease recurrence and progression. These inferences can be enhanced by integration of spatial molecular profiling, which can also provide mechanistic explainability to the H&E-based DL models. However, limitations in dataset diversity, external validation, model interpretability, and generalizability across populations and image acquisition protocols currently prevent clinical adoption. Outcome-anchored, multimodal computational pathology pipelines integrating H&E WSIs with spatial multi-omic profiling offer a biologically grounded and scalable framework for personalized risk stratification in stage I-III CM, with potential to standardize diagnosis, discover novel prognostic features, and inform individualized treatment strategies.

title: Can We Diagnose Early Melanoma by Genomics?
abstract: Melanoma incidence has increased approximately 6-fold over the past 40 years, driven primarily by melanoma in situ and thin invasive melanomas, which are among the most subjective lesions to diagnose on histopathology. This review examines whether genomics clarifies the "gray zone" between benign and malignant pigmented lesions, or instead recasts existing histopathologic ambiguity in molecular terms, while also considering whether genomic classification shifts overdiagnosis upstream instead of resolving underlying diagnostic uncertainty. Across cytogenetic, mutation-based, and gene-expression platforms, current assays perform best in unequivocal melanoma-versus-nevus comparisons and lose accuracy in diagnostically ambiguous lesions where clarification is most needed. Gene expression profile (GEP) tests can be useful diagnostic aids in tissue-rich equivocal lesions, including atypical Spitz tumors, MELTUMPs, and cellular blue nevus/blue nevus-like melanocytoma differentials. One clinicopathologic-genomic model, the Merlin CP-GEP test, has been prospectively validated for predicting sentinel lymph node status and is now recognized as supporting sentinel lymph node biopsy decisions in T1b/T2a melanomas. Importantly, a low-risk prognostic GEP class assignment should not displace the standard sentinel lymph node biopsy discussion. GEP tests are least useful for small, thin, equivocal junctional proliferations, precisely the lesions that are most difficult to diagnose. Pre-biopsy non-invasive assays carry the additional risk of lowering, rather than raising, the biopsy threshold. Overall, current genomic tools should be viewed as an adjunct to, rather than a replacement for, histopathology and clinical context.

title: Intraoperative Ultrasound Guided Sling Adjustment During Transobturator Sling Placement: A Preliminary Pilot Report of the Technical Protocol and Feasibility.
abstract: Objectives To describe a qualitative intraoperative ultrasound protocol for transobturator mid-urethral sling adjustment and assess technical feasibility. Methods This retrospective pilot series included 58 consecutive women with urodynamically confirmed stress urinary incontinence or stress-predominant mixed urinary incontinence undergoing outside-in transobturator sling placement. Sagittal and axial images guided gentle traction for a visible tape-urethra gap and tension release for urethral encroachment. Sling-arm oscillation supplemented assessment when acoustic shadowing limited visualization. Feasibility measures included visualization, adjustment frequency, final sonographic findings, scanning duration, and intraoperative complications. Clinical outcomes were summarized using available cases. Results The tape was visualized in all 58 procedures and adjusted in 26 (44.8%). No final residual gap or encroachment was observed. Median scanning duration was 3 min 45 s (interquartile range, 3-4 min); no intraoperative complications were recorded. All 58 women provided baseline and 3-month questionnaire data. Mean six-item Urogenital Distress Inventory scores decreased from 68.3 ± 17.2 to 20.0 ± 6.7; seven-item Incontinence Impact Questionnaire scores decreased from 75.4 ± 10.5 to 18.2 ± 6.7. At 36 months, 20/58 women (34.5%) had outcome data. All 20 met the objective stress continence criterion (exact two-sided 95% confidence interval, 83.2%-100%); none met the objective voiding dysfunction criterion (exact two-sided 95% confidence interval, 0%-16.8%). These findings concern only the retained subgroup. Conclusions The protocol was technically feasible in this single-surgeon, single-center series. Reproducibility, workflow burden, and clinical benefit require prospective evaluation.

title: Association Between Local Factors and Implant-Related Complications: A Population-Sampled Cross-Sectional Analysis.
abstract: Aim To investigate the role of local factors and the association with peri-implantitis and peri-implant soft-tissue dehiscence (PISTD). Materials and methods A randomly selected sample of Norwegian patients who underwent implant therapy in 2014 was examined (242 patients; 732 implants). Clinical and radiographic parameters were recorded, including soft-tissue phenotype, mucosal margin mobility, connection type, platform switching, emergence angle, implant location and presence of adjacent teeth. To account for clustering of implants within patients, mixed-effects logistic regression models were applied. Results Mucosal margin mobility, bone-level implants without platform switching, emergence angle > 45°, anterior implant location and daily smoking were identified as significant risk indicators for peri-implantitis. Thin soft-tissue phenotype, mucosal margin mobility, absence of adjacent teeth, peri-implantitis and external connection were detected as significant indicators for PISTD. Peri-implantitis and PISTD were present in 8.7% and 25.0% of implants, respectively. Conclusions Local factors and soft-tissue-related parameters, many modifiable during treatment planning, were associated with peri-implantitis and PISTD. Particular attention should be given to soft-tissue phenotype, connection design, platform switching and prosthetic emergence angle. The relationship between systemic and local risk factors should be further investigated.

title: Experience-based recommendations for the diagnosis and management of early-stage nail unit melanoma.
abstract: Background Nail unit melanoma (NUM) is a distinct form of melanoma that most often arises from the nail matrix. No recommendations as to the management of nail melanoma, particularly of early-stage melanoma (in situ, stage IA, IB), exist. Objectives To provide practical, experience-based recommendations for the diagnosis, differential diagnosis and management of early-stage NUM, developed by an international expert panel. Methods Based on clinical and histopathological experience and an extensive literature search, the authors present recommendations for the management of patients with lesions suspicious for NUM. Results Clinically, most cases present as a longitudinal pigmented band in an adult nail. It represents 1.5-2.5% of all melanomas in Caucasians but up to 50% in Black patients. Considering that the nail unit surface area accounts for less than 1% of the total body surface, the nail matrix can be regarded as a hotspot for melanoma development. Early diagnosis is critical, as treatment at the in situ or minimally invasive stage is associated with high cure rates. While dermoscopy is a useful diagnostic aid, nail matrix biopsy with histopathology remains the gold standard. Laboratory tests and standard imaging studies are not diagnostic; however, they may assist in surgical planning for advanced cases. Complete surgical excision is the treatment of choice. Wide local excision is recommended for early-stage disease, with specific margins (6 mm for standard lesions; 10 mm in the presence of the Hutchinson sign). Amputation is generally reserved for thicker tumours (>1 mm). A 10-year follow-up period is recommended to monitor for potential recurrence. Conclusions Early diagnosis and treatment of nail unit melanoma at the in situ or minimally invasive stage (IA/IB) are associated with high cure rates. In contrast, advanced disease with deep invasion or metastasis carries a poor prognosis-therefore, timely recognition and intervention are essential to optimize outcomes.
originalAbstract:
Background

Nail unit melanoma (NUM) is a distinct form of melanoma that most often arises from the nail matrix. No recommendations as to the management of nail melanoma, particularly of early-stage melanoma (in situ, stage IA, IB), exist.

Objectives

To provide practical, experience-based recommendations for the diagnosis, differential diagnosis and management of early-stage NUM, developed by an international expert panel.

Methods

Based on clinical and histopathological experience and an extensive literature search, the authors present recommendations for the management of patients with lesions suspicious for NUM.

Results

Clinically, most cases present as a longitudinal pigmented band in an adult nail. It represents 1.5-2.5% of all melanomas in Caucasians but up to 50% in Black patients. Considering that the nail unit surface area accounts for less than 1% of the total body surface, the nail matrix can be regarded as a hotspot for melanoma development. Early diagnosis is critical, as treatment at the in situ or minimally invasive stage is associated with high cure rates. While dermoscopy is a useful diagnostic aid, nail matrix biopsy with histopathology remains the gold standard. Laboratory tests and standard imaging studies are not diagnostic; however, they may assist in surgical planning for advanced cases. Complete surgical excision is the treatment of choice. Wide local excision is recommended for early-stage disease, with specific margins (6 mm for standard lesions; 10 mm in the presence of the Hutchinson sign). Amputation is generally reserved for thicker tumours (>1 mm). A 10-year follow-up period is recommended to monitor for potential recurrence.

Conclusions

Early diagnosis and treatment of nail unit melanoma at the in situ or minimally invasive stage (IA/IB) are associated with high cure rates. In contrast, advanced disease with deep invasion or metastasis carries a poor prognosis-therefore, timely recognition and intervention are essential to optimize outcomes.

title: Health Economic & Implementation Determinants of Prehospital Stroke Triage Tools: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Effective prehospital stroke triage enables faster treatment and better patient outcomes. Although prehospital triage innovations are rapidly emerging, evidence regarding the balance between costs and benefits as well as implementation issues remains limited. This review aims to synthesise published evidence on health economics and implementation determinants of prehospital triage tools for acute suspected ischaemic stroke patients. A systematic search was conducted across five databases (CINAHL, Cochrane, EMBASE, PubMed, and Web of Science) between 1995 and 2025. Results were reported narratively, and reporting quality was assessed using CHEERS, STROBE-simulation, COREQ, CONSORT, SQUIRE, and GRAMMS. Included were empirical studies of EMS-operated prehospital triage innovations for acute suspected stroke patients. The main outcome measures were health economic outcomes (e.g., ICER) and system-level implementation determinants (CFIR constructs). From 6491 screened studies, thirty-one were included: thirteen studies included health economic outcomes and eighteen reported implementation determinants. Prehospital triage tools assessed were: MSU (n = 14), telemedicine (n = 13), clinimetrics (n = 1), prehospital MRI (n = 1), biomarkers (n = 1), and an AI-based microwave tool (n = 1). Most studies (68%) were of high reporting quality. Positive results regarding cost-effectiveness were reported (n = 11), including cost-savings (n = 1), as well as implementation determinants (n = 11). However, evidence on sustained implementation was limited. Barriers included innovation design, complexity, workflow compatibility, work and IT infrastructure, and costs. Included studies suggest most prehospital stroke triage tools are cost-effective, but implementation remains largely context-dependent. Barriers, including innovation complexity, role delineation, workflow fit, design, and costs, highlight the need for future studies to integrate health economics into an implementation science framework alongside clinical outcomes.

title: When the Algorithm Speaks First: Trust, Reliance and the Reconstruction of Clinical Metacognition.
abstract: Aims of the journal addressed This paper addresses three of the aims of the Journal: clinical decision making, health philosophy and person-centred healthcare. Retinal imaging serves as the analytic case. The question at issue, what epistemic attitude a clinician may properly hold towards an algorithmic output issued for an individual patient, arises in every discipline and every health system in which such systems are deployed, and the argument is tested throughout against systems that read no images. Rationale, aims and objectives Diagnostic artificial intelligence increasingly delivers a conclusion before the clinician has formed one, and medical education has responded by adding modules on the critical appraisal of algorithmic output. Such curricula rest upon two unsound foundations: they extend a form of metacognitive instruction shown not to improve diagnostic accuracy and they ask clinicians to cultivate an attitude whose defining feature is the relaxation of validation. This paper establishes what epistemic attitude a clinician may hold towards an algorithmic output and derives the form that clinical metacognition must take in consequence. Methods Conceptual analysis, drawing upon the philosophy of trust and epistemic dependence, the cognitive science of clinical reasoning and empirical studies of artificial intelligence in clinical practice. Retinal medicine serves as the analytic case, chosen because it is the domain in which the position under contest is strongest; the argument is tested throughout against systems that process no images. Results Trust and reliance are distinct attitudes. On the account adopted here, to trust a medical algorithm is to rely upon it while relaxing the monitoring of the conditions that make it reliable; trust is reliance from which validation has been withdrawn. Regulatory clearance, institutional adoption and published performance supply legitimate grounds for trusting the assemblage that produces a system, yet none of them, singly or together, warrants reliance upon its output for an individual patient. Three asymmetries separate algorithmic from human epistemic dependence: the algorithm can be neither interrogated nor held to account; its errors fall on whole classes of patients at once; and its warrant holds of a population while the decision is owed to a person. The metacognition this situation demands is knowledge, not disposition, and stands untouched by the evidence against generic metacognitive instruction. Conclusions Clinical metacognition requires reconstruction around three competences: calibrated reliance, awareness of distributed epistemic labour, and vigilance towards confidence-masked uncertainty. Each is content-dependent, teachable and assessable. Since none can be exercised where institutions supply neither the means of interrogation nor the time it takes, the reform of education and the reform of clinical governance are, in this respect, a single undertaking.

title: Organ Wet Mount (Squash) Preparations in Fish Pathology: An Underused, Rapid and Low-Cost Tool for Tissue-Level Diagnosis During Necropsy.
abstract: Rapid, practical diagnostic approaches are essential for effective fish health management, yet cytological wet mount assessment of internal organs remains underused and inconsistently described in peer-reviewed aquatic veterinary literature. Organ wet mount (squash preparation) cytology offers a simple, low-cost method for immediate evaluation of fresh tissues. Unlike impression smears and aspirates, in which cells are assessed largely in isolation, squash preparations retain structural relationships within the tissue, providing tissue-level information at the point of examination that would otherwise await histopathology. The technique is widely applicable and requires minimal equipment, but guidance on its application beyond gill, skin, and fin samples is limited. A survey of fish health professionals confirmed that internal organ preparations are used less than external wet mounts. This review outlines the use of organ squash preparations during fish necropsy, emphasising technique, interpretation, and recognition of common findings rather than a comprehensive overview of disease. Key limitations, such as post-mortem changes, are discussed, as is the role of targeted special stains and follow-up diagnostics. Greater awareness and more consistent use of organ squash cytology have the potential to improve early detection of disease and support more targeted diagnostic decision-making in fish health investigations.

title: Integrating Plain 2D Ultrasound and Clinical Data for Identification of At-Risk MASH: A Multicenter Proof of Concept Study.
abstract: Background Identifying people with at-risk metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is a major challenge. We aimed to use deep learning to develop a convolutional neural network (CNN) model to facilitate the detection of at-risk MASH. Methods A multi-center cohort study was conducted across five tertiary hospitals in Japan and China. Clinical data and conventional ultrasound images were retrospectively collected. Organ segmentation using YOLO version 11 with quality control was performed, followed by creation of an EfficientNet-B6 CNN regression model, with image-level predictions averaged per patient, to estimate FAST and AGILE 3+ risk categories. Model performance was assessed using agreement across clinically relevant rule-out and rule-in thresholds, R 2 , root mean squared error (RMSE), and area under the receiver operating curve (AUROC). Results The final dataset comprised 416 patients for training (7643 images), 139 for internal validation (2463 images), and 154 for external testing (3539 images). The CNN model demonstrated good agreement with FAST (R 2 = 0.684; RMSE = 0.131; category agreement = 0.71) and moderate agreement with AGILE 3+ (R 2 = 0.445; RMSE = 0.1964; category agreement = 0.63). For FAST, AUROC was 0.974 (95% CI 0.947-0.993) for 0.35 and 0.932 (95% CI 0.884-0.969) for the 0.67 cut-off. For AGILE 3+, AUROC was 0.908 (95% CI 0.854-0.950) for 0.451 and 0.902 (95% CI 0.839-0.953) for the 0.679 cut-off. Conclusion The CNN model applied to clinical ultrasound images can approximate the accuracy of VCTE-based composite risk scores for detecting at-risk MASH. This may support the detection of at-risk MASH in settings with limited access to transient elastography.

title: Impact of AI-Assisted Endoscopy on Secondary Review and Referral Decisions in Gastric Cancer Screening: A Multicenter Real-World Study.
abstract: Objectives Artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted endoscopy may support gastric cancer screening, but its impact on structured secondary human review remains unclear. We evaluated secondary review modifications and referral decisions before and after AI implementation. Methods This retrospective multicenter study included 5013 screening esophagogastroduodenoscopy examinations performed before (n = 2021) and after (n = 2992) AI implementation. The primary outcome was secondary review modifications. Secondary outcomes included referral for further diagnostic evaluation. Multivariable logistic regression analyses adjusted for age, sex, Helicobacter pylori eradication status, prior-year endoscopy, and endoscopist experience were performed. Interaction analyses according to endoscopist experience and inverse probability of treatment weighting analyses were conducted. No external reference standard was available to verify secondary-review modifications or referral decisions. Results Secondary review modifications increased from 1.2% in the pre-AI period to 3.7% in the AI period (p < 0.01). A significant interaction was observed between AI implementation and endoscopist experience (p for interaction < 0.01), with increased modifications primarily among nonexpert endoscopists. Cancer-related modifications remained uncommon but increased after AI implementation (0.6% vs. 0.2%, p = 0.04). Referral rates decreased from 4.9% to 2.8% (p < 0.01), and AI implementation was independently associated with lower odds of referral (adjusted OR = 0.53; 95% confidence interval = 0.36-0.77). Conclusions AI-assisted endoscopy was associated with lower referral rates; however, secondary review modifications persisted after AI implementation, particularly among nonexpert endoscopists. These findings describe workflow changes and do not establish the clinical validity of the modifications or the appropriateness of referral decisions.

title: Metaplasia and the Origins of Gastric Cancer-Implications for Screening and Surveillance.
abstract: Gastric intestinal metaplasia (IM) is a key step in the development of intestinal-type gastric cancer (GC) and a checkpoint for preventive strategies. The risk of progression to GC is highest for incomplete IM and extensive severe IM as classified by scoring systems such as operative link on gastric intestinal metaplasia (OLGIM) assessment, whereas the majority with mild or focal IM do not progress. Its pathogenesis is characterized by Helicobacter pylori-triggered chronic inflammation driving epithelial lineage reprogramming and CDX1/2 activation. IM clones develop and acquire early driver mutations (TP53, APC, and FBXW7), 8q/MYC gains, telomere attrition, and promoter hypermethylation, establishing a precancerous field, from which further evolution to dysplasia and cancer may occur. Recent preliminary data have suggested the possibility of reversing IM by MEK inhibition to induce mucosal reprogramming. Clinical management centers on H. pylori eradication, surveillance by high-quality endoscopy and guided by risk stratification using OLGIM or endoscopic grading of gastric intestinal metaplasia (EGGIM). Future work should prospectively validate tissue and blood biomarkers, integrate image-based risk scores into routine care, and test antiprogression and field-modifying therapies in randomized trials. In conclusion, IM is an actionable checkpoint for cancer interception, and its finding in a patient should prompt the consideration of surveillance and preventive strategies to avert progression to GC.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Ultrasound for Sarcopenia Assessment: A Scoping Review.
abstract: Background Muscle ultrasound offers a portable, non-invasive, and cost-effective option for sarcopenia assessment, but operator dependency limits its standardization. Artificial intelligence (AI) may help automate and improve ultrasound-based muscle evaluation. This scoping review aims to map the current landscape of AI-assisted ultrasound for sarcopenia assessment, including research trends, methods, clinical uses and performance, and to suggest future work. Methods Following Joanna Briggs Institute guidelines and the PRISMA-ScR checklist, we searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, CINAHL, ProQuest, CNKI, WanFang Data, Yiigle, VIP, and Sinomed up to July 25, 2026. Two researchers independently selected studies and extracted data. Results Thirty studies were included. This field is developing rapidly, with 76.7% of studies published in the last 3 years, primarily from Spain and China. Model development and validation studies (43.3%) were most common. U-Net and its variants were the predominant AI architectures, mainly for image segmentation. B-mode ultrasound with high-frequency linear probes was frequently used. The rectus femoris was the most assessed muscle for sarcopenia (73.3%). AI-integrated models for sarcopenia diagnosis achieved AUCs of 0.640-0.950. Reported Dice coefficients for muscle segmentation ranged from 0.73 to 0.99. Future efforts should deepen image-processing strategies to extract clinically relevant features and facilitate standardized, scalable implementation in clinical practice.

title: Opportunistic Screening for Bone Demineralization by Whole Body CT in a Red-Handed Howler Monkey (Alouatta belzebul) Under Human Care.
abstract: An eight-year-old male red-handed howler monkey (Alouatta belzebul) underwent whole-body computed tomography for gastrointestinal signs. Quantitative CT of the lumbar vertebrae opportunistically revealed severe bone hypoattenuation, demineralization, and deteriorated trabecular architecture. This incidental diagnosis of metabolic bone disease was directly attributed to chronic inadequate management conditions, specifically a severely imbalanced diet and insufficient sunlight exposure in captivity.

title: Pulmonary Tuberculosis in Rhesus Macaque (Macaca mulatta): A Case Report.
abstract: Pulmonary tuberculosis caused by the Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (MTC) was diagnosed in a 6-year-old female rhesus macaque (Macaca mulatta) presented with a three-month history of intermittent coughing, dyspnea, weight loss, and inappetence. Hematological evaluation revealed moderate regenerative anemia and neutrophilic leukocytosis, while the thoracic radiography demonstrated a diffuse nodular interstitial pulmonary pattern consistent with tuberculosis. The diagnosis was confirmed by IS6110-targeted PCR. This case underscores the utility of combining radiographic and molecular diagnostic approaches for the early confirmation of tuberculosis in nonhuman primates and highlights its important zoonotic implications.

title: Genetic landscape of a neonatal hypogonadotropic hypogonadism series: Novel variants and phenotypic spectrum.
abstract: To describe clinical presentation and genetic findings in a cohort of infants with congenital hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (CHH) diagnosed before 2 years of age. From a large cohort of patients who underwent next-generation sequencing (NGS) for CHH between 2019 and 2025, we identified all patients tested at ≤2 years of age. Genetic analysis consisted of a targeted CHH gene panel, followed by a CPHD-NGS panel. In one remaining patient with neurodevelopmental defects, whole-exome sequencing was performed. Phenotypic data were collected through the GENHYPOPIT registry. Twelve male infants (1.5% of the total cohort) met the inclusion criteria; one additional patient via familial screening was included, for a total of 13 patients. All had micropenis; four had associated cryptorchidism (bilateral in half of cases). CHH was biologically confirmed during mini-puberty in 10 infants, at a median age of 6.8 weeks. Seven of these 10 infants received gonadotropin therapy, at an average of 4.1 months. MRI revealed bilateral olfactory bulb agenesis in five cases. A pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant was identified in 7 of 12 patients (58%), involving TACR3 (n = 2), ANOS1, FGFR1 (including two novel variants), SOX10, GLI2 (through the CPHD panel), and SOX11 (identified by exome sequencing). A genetic cause was identified in 58% of cases, a diagnostic yield higher than reported in pubertal cohorts. Early genetic diagnosis allowed anticipatory monitoring for syndromic manifestations and associated pituitary deficiencies-particularly relevant for FGFR1 and GLI2 variant carriers at risk of CPHD. Our findings support the inclusion of GLI2 and SOX11 in targeted HH gene panels.

title: Metastasis of Invasive Ductal Carcinoma of the Breast to the Uterine Cervix 30 Years Post-Mastectomy: A Case Report.
abstract: Metastasis of invasive ductal carcinoma of the breast to the uterine cervix is rare, with only one report of a case occurring more than 20 years after the primary surgery. A 69-year-old woman presented with abnormal uterine cervical cytology (atypical glandular cells without tumor diathesis) 30 years after undergoing breast cancer surgery. Magnetic resonance imaging revealed a 38-mm cervical mass. Modified radical hysterectomy was performed. The resected specimen exhibited an immunohistochemical profile of GATA3(+)/mammaglobin(+)/PAX8(-), which definitively excluded primary cervical adenocarcinoma and confirmed the diagnosis of metastatic invasive ductal carcinoma. Crucially, although the primary tumor was hormone receptor-positive, cervical metastasis exhibited receptor conversion to HER2-positive status. This case underscores the importance of considering metastatic breast cancer in the differential diagnosis of cervical masses in breast cancer survivors regardless of the disease-free interval. This further highlights the necessity for receptor re-evaluation in metastatic lesions to guide appropriate targeted therapy.

title: Sex-Discordant Monochorionic Dizygotic Twins After Double Blastocyst Transfer: Blood Chimerism Demonstrated by Multimodal Genetic Testing.
abstract: A 38-year-old woman conceived after intracytoplasmic sperm injection and frozen-thawed double blastocyst transfer. First-trimester ultrasonography suggested monochorionic diamniotic twins, but discordant external genitalia were identified at 21 weeks of gestation. Delivery at 37 weeks resulted in phenotypically normal female and male infants. Placental histopathology confirmed monochorionic diamniotic placentation. Postnatal multimodal genetic evaluation, including G-banding, single nucleotide polymorphism array, and buccal cell X/Y fluorescence in situ hybridization, demonstrated mixed 46,XX/46,XY cell lines in peripheral blood, consistent with predominantly blood-limited chimerism. Single nucleotide polymorphism array analysis demonstrated admixture of two independently derived genomes and findings inconsistent with a primary dispermic mechanism. These results supported a diagnosis of monochorionic dizygotic twinning with predominantly blood chimerism, most likely reflecting intertwin cell exchange. This case highlights the value of integrating tissue-specific genetic findings with postnatal phenotypic and clinical assessment to interpret predominantly blood-limited chimerism in MCDZ twins.

title: Multi-Level Automated Classification of Temporomandibular Joint Degenerative Joint Disease on CBCT Using 3D Volumetric and 2D Slice-Based Approaches.
abstract: Background Temporomandibular joint degenerative joint disease (TMJ DJD) causes progressive osseous changes of the mandibular condyle and articular fossa. Although cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) enables detailed assessment, manual interpretation is time-consuming and subject to inter-observer variability. Objectives To develop and validate a multilevel AI framework for CBCT-based TMJ DJD assessment using three-dimensional classification, quantitative volumetric analysis, and two-dimensional slice-based detection. Methods Full-field-of-view CBCT scans from 222 patients were used for three-dimensional analysis. A 3D V-Net classified condyles into Normal, Osteophyte, Erosion, Flattening, and Severe Degeneration categories. Condylar volume was quantitatively compared between TMJ DJD and non-TMJ DJD groups and among degenerative subgroups. For slice-based analysis, 727 temporomandibular joints from 416 patients were retrospectively evaluated. Automated sagittal slice extraction based on the condylion landmark generated 5787 condylar and 666 articular fossa slices. YOLOv10 was used for multi-lesion detection of six condylar and three fossa categories. Results The 3D V-Net achieved an overall sensitivity of 79.47%. Condylar volume differed significantly between TMJ DJD and non-TMJ DJD groups (ANOVA, p = 0.025), whereas differences among the TMJ DJD subgroups were not statistically significant. For condylar slice-based detection, YOLOv10 achieved 94.0% sensitivity, 82.8% precision, 88.0% F1-score, and 91.3% AP@0.50. For articular fossa detection, YOLOv10 achieved 92.41% sensitivity, 83.91% precision, 87.95% F1-score, and 82.01% AP@0.50. Conclusions Three-dimensional AI enabled overall TMJ DJD classification but showed limited discrimination of specific subgroups, particularly erosion. Volumetric analysis differentiated DJD from non-DJD cases but not among DJD subgroups. In contrast, slice-based YOLOv10 effectively detected and labelled specific condylar and fossa degenerative changes, providing more detailed lesion-level characterization.

title: Internal Validation of a YOLOv8 Model for Classifying Temporomandibular Joint Disc Displacement With Versus Without Reduction on Open-Mouth Proton-Density-Weighted MRI.
abstract: Background The temporomandibular joint (TMJ) disc plays an important role in maintaining normal joint function. However, disc displacement is a common condition that can lead to pain, restricted jaw movement and chronic TMJ dysfunction. Objective To develop and evaluate a deep learning model capable of autonomously localizing the TMJ region from magnetic resonance (MR) images during mouth opening using the You Only Look Once (YOLO) v8 framework, and to discriminate between TMJ disc displacement with reduction (DDwR) and disc displacement without reduction (DDwoR). Methods This study included 237 patients (48 males, 189 females; age range, 19-83 [mean, 44.73 ± 18.3] years) who underwent MRI examination at our hospital for suspected TMJ disorders and were diagnosed with disc displacement based on imaging findings. After exclusion, 439 proton density-weighted MR images during mouth opening were preprocessed and divided on a patient basis into training (280 images), validation (71 images) and test (88 images) datasets. The TMJ region was manually annotated using LabelImg, including the condyles, articular disc and articular tubercle. The YOLOv8 deep learning model was trained for 200 epochs to localize the TMJ region and classify DDwR or DDwoR. Results The YOLOv8 model achieved promising results for the detection and classification of TMJ disc displacements. The performance metrics were a precision, recall and F1 score of 0.983, 0.988 and 0.987, respectively, indicating a high accuracy in detecting and identifying disc displacement patterns. Conclusion The YOLOv8 deep learning model demonstrated promising performance in automatically localizing and classifying TMJ disc displacement from MR images.

title: Subcutaneous Fat Density Is an Independent Predictor of Adverse Outcomes and Shows Early Improvement After Liver Transplantation.
abstract: Background and aims Body composition is increasingly recognised as a prognostic determinant in cirrhosis, particularly in liver transplant (LT) candidates. We aimed to assess adipose and muscle compartments on computed tomography (CT) before and after LT and to evaluate their associations with mortality. Methods We recruited prospectively 121 patients with cirrhosis listed for LT. CT scans at the third lumbar vertebral level were analysed to quantify cross-sectional area (cm 2 ) and density (Hounsfield units, HU) of skeletal muscle, subcutaneous adipose tissue (SAT), and visceral adipose tissue. A subset underwent a CT-scan 6 months post-LT. Results Most patients were male (76%), and the median MELD score was 14 (IQR 10-20). High SAT density (> -83 HU in women; > -74 HU in men) was associated with higher pre-transplant mortality (p = 0.005) and with reduced overall survival during follow-up (p = 0.005) compared to lower SAT density. The combined phenotype of low muscle density and high SAT density identified the subgroup with the poorest survival (p = 0.002). From baseline to 6 months post-LT, SAT density decreased significantly (p = 0.0134), whereas muscle parameters did not change significantly. Conclusions This prospective observational cohort study demonstrates that SAT density is a prognostic CT-derived marker in patients with cirrhosis awaiting LT with significant post-transplant dynamics. The impact of altered adipose tissue therefore warrants attention in this situation.

title: Distinct Plasma Proteomic Signatures Distinguish MASLD From Non-Steatotic Individuals but Not From MetALD.
abstract: Background and aims Metabolic dysfunction associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the most prevalent liver disease, yet accurate early detection remains challenging. A particular diagnostic obstacle is distinguishing MASLD from metabolic dysfunction and alcohol-related liver disease (MetALD), currently defined using clinically informed moderate alcohol consumption thresholds without biological validation. This study aimed to identify and externally validate plasma proteomic signatures associated with MASLD and assess whether proteomic profiles support a molecular distinction between MASLD and MetALD as currently defined. Methods We analysed plasma proteomic profiles using OLINK data from UK Biobank (UKB) participants with liver MRI. MASLD was defined as MRI-PDFF ≥ 5% and metabolic dysfunction (n = 165), MetALD (n = 46) as MASLD with additional moderate alcohol intake and controls as PDFF < 5% (n = 741). Results Compared to controls, participants with MASLD showed 17 upregulated and 3 downregulated proteins after Bonferroni correction (adjusted p < 0.05). Among upregulated proteins, leptin (LEP), fatty acid-binding protein, liver (FABP1) and aminoacylase1 (ACY1) and among downregulated, insulin-like growth factor-binding protein 1 (IGFBP1) were externally validated in an independent cohort (clinicaltrials.gov NCT02520609, n = 47). Individuals with MetALD showed no significant proteomic distinction from MASLD. Although the small MetALD sample size may have limited detection of differences, direct differential expression analysis did not identify statistically significant differences between MASLD and MetALD under the current clinical thresholds. Conclusions MASLD was associated with a reproducible plasma proteomic signature enriched for proteins involved in lipid metabolism, inflammation and hormonal regulation. We did not identify a clear proteomic distinction between MASLD and MetALD under the current alcohol thresholds. However, this finding should be interpreted considering limited power and potential alcohol-exposure misclassification.

We analysed plasma proteomic profiles using OLINK data from UK Biobank (UKB) participants with liver MRI. MASLD was defined as MRI-PDFF ≥ 5% and metabolic dysfunction (n = 165), MetALD (n = 46) as MASLD with additional moderate alcohol intake and controls as PDFF < 5% (n = 741).

Results

Compared to controls, participants with MASLD showed 17 upregulated and 3 downregulated proteins after Bonferroni correction (adjusted p < 0.05). Among upregulated proteins, leptin (LEP), fatty acid-binding protein, liver (FABP1) and aminoacylase1 (ACY1) and among downregulated, insulin-like growth factor-binding protein 1 (IGFBP1) were externally validated in an independent cohort (clinicaltrials.gov NCT02520609, n = 47). Individuals with MetALD showed no significant proteomic distinction from MASLD. Although the small MetALD sample size may have limited detection of differences, direct differential expression analysis did not identify statistically significant differences between MASLD and MetALD under the current clinical thresholds.

Conclusions

MASLD was associated with a reproducible plasma proteomic signature enriched for proteins involved in lipid metabolism, inflammation and hormonal regulation. We did not identify a clear proteomic distinction between MASLD and MetALD under the current alcohol thresholds. However, this finding should be interpreted considering limited power and potential alcohol-exposure misclassification.

title: Diagnostic Value and Influencing Factors of Ultrasound-Derived Fat Fraction for Quantifying MASLD in Children.
abstract: Background & aims To evaluate the diagnostic performance of ultrasound-derived fat fraction (UDFF) for quantifying Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) in children, using Magnetic resonance imaging-derived proton density fat fraction (MRI-PDFF) as the reference standard. Methods This prospective study enrolled 70 children with a median age of 12.23 years [IQR, 10.47-14.29] from December 2025 to April 2026. All participants underwent UDFF, MRI-PDFF, and point shear wave elastography (pSWE) examinations. Steatosis was defined as MRI-PDFF ≥ 6.4%. Correlations, agreement, diagnostic accuracy, and bias predictors were assessed using Pearson/Spearman correlation, Bland-Altman, ROC curves, and multivariable regression. Results Of 70 participants, 42 had MASLD. UDFF correlated strongly with MRI-PDFF (r = 0.84, p < 0.001). Overall mean bias was -2.19% (95% concordance limits: -15.07% to 10.68%), with a more pronounced systematic numerical bias observed in moderate-to-severe steatosis (mean bias -9.23%). No significant bias predictors were found. For detecting steatosis (≥ 6.4%), UDFF had an AUC of 0.98, optimal cutoff 5.5% (sensitivity 97.6%, specificity 92.9%, accuracy 95.7%); for ≥ S2 steatosis, the cutoff was 12.5% (AUC 0.96). Intraclass correlation for five repeated UDFF measurements was 0.98 (95% CI: 0.98-0.99). Visceral fat thickness (β = 2.004, p = 0.003) and measurement depth (β = 4.716, p = 0.033) independently predicted UDFF values. UDFF showed a weak negative correlation with pSWE Young's modulus (r = -0.258, p = 0.033). Conclusions UDFF is a non-invasive, accurate, and reproducible tool for quantifying paediatric hepatic steatosis. Although a systematic numerical bias exists relative to MRI-PDFF in moderate-to-severe cases, UDFF retains excellent discriminative ability and is suitable for screening, staging, and longitudinal follow-up of paediatric MASLD.

title: Ultrasound-Based Skeletal Muscle Assessment for Prognostication in Cirrhosis: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Background and aims Sarcopenia is a major determinant of adverse outcomes in cirrhosis, yet CT- and MRI-based assessments are difficult to implement in routine and longitudinal practice. Ultrasound is a feasible bedside alternative, but its prognostic role remains unclear. We performed a systematic review to evaluate the association between ultrasound-derived skeletal muscle measures and mortality in adults with cirrhosis. Methods This review followed PRISMA guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251056162). MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science and the Cochrane Library were searched to October 2025. Prospective studies assessing ultrasound-based muscle parameters and mortality in cirrhosis were included. Risk of bias was evaluated using QUIPS. Results Six prospective studies (n = 731) were included. Heterogeneity in muscle sites, ultrasound protocols, indexation methods, sarcopenia definitions and outcomes precluded meta-analysis. Lower ultrasound-derived muscle measures were consistently associated with higher mortality. In acute decompensation, reduced rectus femoris area predicted 90-day mortality (sHR 0.57; 95% CI 0.38-0.85). Rectus abdominis thickness and psoas indices were also associated with mortality. In hospitalized decompensated cirrhosis, ultrasound-defined sarcopenia was strongly associated with 6-month mortality (HR 6.37; 95% CI 3.15-12.87). In critically ill liver transplant candidates, higher serial rectus femoris muscle area measurements were associated with better survival. In advanced chronic liver disease, sarcopenia was linked to increased 1-year mortality. Conclusions In our systematic review, ultrasound-based muscle measures demonstrated a broadly consistent association with mortality; although not yet fully validated, they represent a promising bedside prognostic tool. Standardization is needed before clinical implementation.

title: Empirically Informed Blood Vessel Network Reconstruction for Multimodality Image-Based Vascular Systems Biology.
abstract: Objective Reconstruction of vascular topology from imperfect 3D imaging data is essential for accurate hemodynamic simulations. Therefore, we developed a "gap-filling" method predicated on vascular biology and empirical patterns to restore incomplete vessels, independent of the imaging modality and spatial resolution employed. Methods Our gap-filling algorithm reconstructs a vascular network based on distributions of its extant morphological features and employs different rules for healthy and tumor tissue. Algorithm performance was evaluated on (i) incomplete synthetic vascular trees with simulated CT noise, (ii) micro-CT-acquired brain tumor vasculature, (iii) micro-MRI-derived vasculature from a healthy mouse brain, and (iv) vasculature from the murine hippocampus imaged with light-sheet microscopy (LSM). Results For synthetic vascular trees, our algorithm restored more gaps when the volume fraction was between 80% and 95%. Peak vessel segment recovery occurred for intermediate volume fractions (86%-89%). Gap-filling performance was impacted when image noise was introduced. Across CT, MRI, and LSM, our method successfully reconnected missing vessel segments while preserving the overall features of the vascular network. Gap-filling of tumor vasculature, with its abnormal topology, was better when tumor-specific reconstruction rules were employed. Conclusions Our method showed efficient restoration of vascular network connectivity for 3D data derived from common imaging modalities at different resolutions. We also demonstrated the significance of applying distinct biologically-informed rules when reconstructing healthy and tumor vascular networks.

title: CT-Based Clinical-Radiomics for Differentiating Talaromyces marneffei Spondylitis From Tuberculous Spondylitis Before Pathogen Confirmation: A Multicentre Diagnostic Study in an Endemic Region.
abstract: Background Talaromyces marneffei spondylitis (TMS) is an uncommon but clinically important form of talaromycosis in endemic regions. Where talaromycosis and tuberculosis overlap, TMS may be worked up as tuberculous spondylitis (TBS), delaying fungal investigations and antifungal treatment. Objectives To assess whether pretreatment CT, routine clinical variables and radiomics features can help differentiate TMS from TBS at the initial assessment stage. Patients/methods This retrospective multicentre study included 263 patients meeting the prespecified composite reference standard (83 TMS and 180 TBS). Centre A formed the training and internal-validation cohorts; Centres B and C formed the external cohort (n = 50; 16 TMS and 34 TBS). Six clinical variables and 14 CT radiomics features were used to develop clinical, radiomics and combined models. Results TMS showed a stronger systemic inflammatory phenotype, whereas TBS generally showed more frequent disc-endplate involvement and osseous destruction. The clinical-radiomics model achieved the highest AUCs in the training, internal validation and external validation cohorts: 0.958 (95% CI, 0.924-0.992), 0.940 (95% CI, 0.871-1.000) and 0.927 (95% CI, 0.867-0.987), respectively. The external confidence interval was wide, reflecting the limited external sample size. Conclusions In regions where talaromycosis and tuberculosis overlap, a pretreatment CT-based clinical-radiomics approach may help flag patients in whom TMS should be considered early. This approach could support earlier fungal investigations while definitive microbiological, molecular or histopathological results are pending. It addresses only the TMS-versus-TBS differential and is not a general spinal-infection triage tool; the findings support further evaluation in endemic settings.

title: Differential Diagnosis Performance of ChatGPT in Oral and Maxillofacial Pathology.
abstract: Objective To evaluate ChatGPT (GPT-5.1) for ranked differential diagnoses in oral and maxillofacial pathology, assess image effects on diagnostic performance and examine output stability across repeated runs. Methods This retrospective diagnostic accuracy study included 160 biopsy-confirmed cases. Cases were evaluated using a standardised prompt under two conditions: text-only and text plus clinical photographs and/or radiographs. Each case underwent three independent runs. Performance was measured using Top-1, Top-3, Top-5 and Top-10 accuracy. Results Top-1 accuracy was 44.0% for text-only and 43.3% for text + image inputs. Accuracy increased at broader thresholds, with Top-10 accuracy reaching 80.7% and 82.9%, respectively, but no significant differences were observed between input conditions at any Top-K threshold. Top-1 performance was stable across runs, although variability was observed at broader Top-K thresholds in the text-only condition. Conclusions ChatGPT ranked the reference diagnosis first in fewer than half of cases, while broader differential lists more often included it. Images did not significantly improve accuracy, although heterogeneous and non-standardised visual inputs may have limited detection of multimodal effects. These findings support further investigation for hypothesis generation and educational use rather than clinical decision support or replacement of expert judgement and histopathological confirmation.

title: Differential Expression of P53, CDKN2A, NOTCH1, and CASP8 in Oral Epithelial Dysplasia: An In Vitro Study to Explore Potential Malignant Transformation.
abstract: Objective This study aimed to better understand the expression of P53, CDKN2A, NOTCH1, and CASP8 proteins in progressive and nonprogressive oral epithelial dysplasia (OED) cell lines to predict malignant transformation. Materials and methods Normal oral keratinocytes (NHOK810), nonprogressive OED (D30-mild, D25-severe), progressive OED (D20-moderate, D19-severe), and oral squamous cell carcinoma (H357, BICR31, and ORL188) were co-cultured with irradiated 3T3 fibroblasts. Western blotting was used to assess the protein expression of p53, CDKN2A, NOTCH1, and CASP8 in these cell lines. Bootstrapping, one-way ANOVA, and subsequent post hoc analyses were performed for multiple comparisons. Results CDKN2A and NOTCH1 had low expression in progressive OED (p = 0.0008 and 0.0012) respectively relative to nonprogressive OED, indicating a negative tendency. Conversely, p53 demonstrated significantly higher expression in progressive OED (p = 0.0112) compared to nonprogressive OED, reflecting a positive trend of expression throughout disease progression. There was a significant difference in CASP8 expression between nonprogressive and progressive cell lines (p = 0.039); however, no linear pattern was observed as the disease advanced. Conclusion The current study illustrates that the high expression of p53, combined with low expression of CDKN2A and NOTCH1, may serve as helpful markers, providing a potential molecular complement to histopathology for predicting malignant transformation in OED.

title: Comparison Between Interlaminar and Transforaminal Endoscopic Lumbar Discectomy for Sciatic Scoliosis Secondary to Lumbar Disc Herniation: A Retrospective Study With a Minimum 1 Year Follow-Up.
abstract: Objective This study aims to compare the clinical and radiographic outcomes of interlaminar and transforaminal endoscopic lumbar discectomy (IELD and TELD) in the treatment of lumbar disc herniation (LDH) with sciatic scoliosis. Methods Patients with sciatic scoliosis secondary to LDH who had undergone IELD or TELD between January 2022 to June 2024 were reviewed. Radiographic parameters, including Cobb angle, apical vertebral translation (AVT), and coronal balance distance (CBD), were measured preoperatively and postoperatively to assess curve evolution. Clinical outcomes were evaluated using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS) and the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI). Meanwhile, perioperative data were also collected. Comparisons between the groups were made by independent t-tests and χ 2 tests. Results A total of 134 patients in the IELD group and 103 patients in the TELD group were included in this study. There was no significant difference in intraoperative blood loss (13.4 ± 7.8 mL vs. 11.5 ± 7.1 mL, p = 0.067) and postoperative length of stay (2.5 ± 0.6 days vs. 2.5 ± 0.8 days, p = 0.378) between the two groups; however, the IELD group demonstrated shorter operation time (87.2 ± 17.4 min vs. 96.1 ± 23.3 min, p = 0.001) and fewer intraoperative fluoroscopy times (4.9 ± 0.7 vs. 10.3 ± 2.7, p < 0.001) compared to the TELD group. Both groups showed significant improvements in VAS and ODI scores (p < 0.05), with no significant differences between the groups. Before surgery, 86.9% (206/237) patients had a disc herniation at the convex side of the lumbosacral curve and 86.5% (205/237) patients showed a trunk shift toward the opposite side of disc herniation. After surgery, 91.8% (123/134) of the IELD group and 90.3% (93/103) of the TELD group achieved resolution of scoliosis (AVT ≤ 10 mm) within 12 months. At the final follow-up, the AVT, Cobb angle, CBD, and SVA in the IELD group were 2.7 ± 2.0 mm, 1.0° ± 0.8°, 1.2 ± 0.9 mm, and 3.4 ± 3.1 mm, respectively, with no significant differences compared to the 2.8 ± 2.7 mm, 1.1° ± 0.8°, 1.2 ± 0.8 mm, and 3.7 ± 3.5 mm in the TELD group. Conclusions Both IELD and TELD are effective and safe for LDH with sciatic scoliosis, with comparable radiographic and clinical outcomes in terms of scoliosis correction. IELD is associated with shorter operation time and fewer intraoperative fluoroscopy times in this cohort.

Both IELD and TELD are effective and safe for LDH with sciatic scoliosis, with comparable radiographic and clinical outcomes in terms of scoliosis correction. IELD is associated with shorter operation time and fewer intraoperative fluoroscopy times in this cohort.

title: Multidimensional Management of Degenerative Scoliosis: A Comprehensive Narrative Review Integrating Diagnostic Assessment, Surgical Decision-Making, and Patient-Centered Outcomes.
abstract: Degenerative scoliosis (DS) is a common spinal deformity in aging populations and an important contributor to low back pain, neurological symptoms, and functional decline. Unlike adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, DS develops in a previously non-scoliotic spine through progressive asymmetric degeneration of the intervertebral disks, facet joints, and supporting spinal structures. Despite its growing clinical burden, management remains heterogeneous, with decision-making often fragmented across radiographic assessment, treatment planning, and postoperative outcome evaluation. Building on previous reviews of DS, this article provides a structured clinical update that organizes contemporary evidence across diagnostic assessment, individualized treatment selection, perioperative risk optimization, and patient-centered outcomes. A narrative literature review was conducted to evaluate current concepts in DS diagnosis, risk stratification, treatment strategies, and patient-centered outcomes. Relevant literature from major biomedical databases was identified and qualitatively synthesized according to clinical relevance. Current evidence supports a comprehensive assessment of DS that integrates deformity morphology, spinopelvic alignment, segmental degeneration, neurological status, bone quality, and patient-specific risk factors. Beyond coronal Cobb angle measurement, advanced imaging and alignment parameters may provide complementary information for phenotyping and treatment planning. The literature increasingly supports individualized treatment selection based on deformity severity, sagittal imbalance, physiological reserve, neurological status, and functional goals, with options ranging from nonoperative care to minimally invasive or more extensive reconstructive procedures. Surgical planning may also incorporate alignment objectives, biomechanical considerations, complication risk, frailty, and patient-reported outcomes. DS management is evolving from deformity correction-centered strategies toward a multidimensional, patient-centered paradigm. This narrative review synthesizes current evidence across diagnostic evaluation, individualized treatment selection, surgical planning, and outcome assessment while recognizing that many management strategies remain supported by heterogeneous evidence and require patient-specific consideration. Future research is needed to refine predictive models, personalized alignment strategies, and emerging technology-assisted approaches.

title: Disseminated Bartonella or Post-Transplant Lymphoproliferative Disease in Pediatric Transplant Patients: A Diagnostic Challenge.
abstract: Post transplant lymphoproliferative disease (PTLD) and infection remain the two most common complications of solid organ transplant and carry a risk of significant morbidity and mortality. PTLD is a highly variable disease with clinical signs and symptoms that are non-specific and require a high degree of suspicion to detect. The most common presenting symptoms of PTLD are malaise, fatigue, fever, and a mononucleosis-like picture; night sweats, weight loss, and lymphadenopathy are also frequent manifestations. An infection with Bartonella Henselae is another known cause of local lymphadenopathy. However, in immunocompromised individuals, Bartonella Henselae is far more likely to cause a systemic response that may mimic PTLD. The specifics regarding differentiating systemic bartonella and PTLD in pediatric solid organ transplant patients are not well described. There have been more detailed descriptions of disseminated bartonella mimicking PTLD in solid organ transplants in adult patients, but this has not been thoroughly reported or described in the pediatric population. Upon literature review, only five cases of disseminated bartonella in pediatric kidney transplant recipients have been described, with three of them possibly associated with PTLD. The past cases described antimicrobial diagnostics for bartonella and other infections, but none of these reported full histopathological findings or associated imaging studies for work-up of PTLD. In addition, past cases have only been described in Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) and Cytomegalovirus (CMV) negative children. There is no consensus for treatment duration and antibiotic choice for confirmed systemic bartonella infection in pediatric kidney transplant patients due to concerns of nephrotoxicity and drug interactions. This patient who presented with fever, lymphadenopathy, nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain was worked up and treated for both Bartonella Henslae and PTLD. PET Scan and biopsies were taken for the diagnosis of PTLD and the patient had Bartonella serologies and PCR testing done as part of a broader infectious workup. Clinical decisions regarding his treatment plan and the cause of his symptoms were made based on response to treatment and the likelihood of underlying etiology based on the timeline which his symptoms improved. After an extensive workup for PTLD and altering immunosuppressive regimens temporarily for possible PTLD we ultimately determined the cause of the patients' symptoms to be secondary to B. henselae infection. The patient was treated appropriately for disseminated Bartonella and improved significantly. He has followed up as an outpatient with continued improvement in symptoms and resumed his previous immunosuppression regimen as PTLD has been ruled out. Bartonella and PTLD are diagnoses that need to be carefully considered and treated in vulnerable populations. Pediatric patients should be managed cautiously with both etiologies under consideration, and more research is needed for specific recommendations regarding differentiating and treating the two simultaneously when clinical presentation is questionable. Given the overlapping symptoms, a thorough workup to rule out and treat PTLD if necessary is recommended given its significant mortality if missed. With biopsy being the gold standard, we recommend careful consideration of performing a biopsy while treating underlying infectious concerns in cases where PTLD is a possibility in pediatric populations.

title: Non-invasive Imaging Modalities for Breslow Thickness Estimation in Melanoma: A Scoping Review.
abstract: Background Breslow thickness (BT) is the most important prognostic biomarker in cutaneous melanoma and directly influences surgical management, sentinel lymph node biopsy decisions and survival outcomes. Several non-invasive imaging modalities have been investigated for preoperative BT estimation; however, their relative performance and clinical applicability remain unclear. Objective To evaluate the agreement between non-invasive imaging-derived and histopathologically measured BT and to compare the technical characteristics, diagnostic performance, and clinical utility of currently available imaging modalities for preoperative melanoma staging. Methods A scoping review was conducted according to Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and reported following PRISMA-ScR guidelines. MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to December 1, 2025. Original studies evaluating non-invasive imaging techniques for BT estimation in cutaneous melanoma were included. Imaging modalities assessed comprised dermoscopy, reflectance confocal microscopy (RCM), optical coherence tomography (OCT), ultrasound (US), multispectral imaging (MSI), photoacoustic techniques, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT), and artificial intelligence (AI)-based approaches. Results Ninety-two studies met the inclusion criteria. Dermoscopy provided indirect assessment of invasiveness, while RCM and OCT offered complementary microstructural information but limited direct thickness estimation. US, particularly high-frequency (≥20 MHz) and ultra-high-frequency (≥50 MHz) systems, showed the strongest and most consistent evidence for direct BT assessment, with correlation coefficients often exceeding 0.90 and high performance across clinically relevant thresholds. Nevertheless, performance varied across devices, probe frequencies, acquisition protocols, and operators, with frequent overestimation and reduced accuracy in selected subgroups (in situ and thin melanomas). MSI showed moderate-to-good classification performance, while photoacoustic techniques yielded promising results but limited to small cohorts. Evidence for MRI and SPECT was scarce. AI-based approaches achieved moderate-to-good predictive performance but did not consistently outperform experienced clinicians, with generalizability limited by dataset and methodological heterogeneity. Conclusions US currently represents the most extensively validated and clinically applicable non-invasive modality for preoperative BT estimation. A hierarchical imaging approach appears most appropriate, with dermoscopy as the first-line diagnostic tool, RCM and OCT providing additional lesion characterization, and HFUS enabling complementary depth assessment in lesions strongly suspicious for melanoma. Emerging photoacoustic and AI-based approaches require further validation, while histopathology remains the reference standard for definitive diagnosis and BT measurement.

title: Polarization Sensitive Optical Coherence Tomography for Surgical Margin Assessment for Canine Soft Tissue Sarcoma.
abstract: Soft tissue sarcomas (STSs) and skeletal muscle both appear high scattering on spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) imaging, which resulted in instances of misclassification by observers in prior soft tissue sarcoma margin assessment studies. Polarization-sensitive optical coherence tomography (PS-OCT) is an extension of OCT that provides additional information about tissue polarization contrast. In this prospective study we wanted to evaluate whether PS-OCT improves tissue differentiation and diagnostic accuracy compared to spectral-domain OCT (SD-OCT) alone. PS-OCT images from surgical margins of 10 resected STS were compared with histopathology to identify characteristic features of normal and neoplastic tissues. Then, six observers of varying OCT image interpretation experience assessed surgical margins from 30 resected STS using SD-OCT alone and SD-OCT combined with PS-OCT. PS-OCT images demonstrated distinct birefringence (optical patterns), corresponding to tissue organization: skeletal muscle exhibited alternating high and low birefringence bands, fascia showed variable birefringence and STS had uniformly low birefringence. Overall diagnostic accuracy was high for both modalities [correct classification rate: SD-OCT alone 93.7% (95% confidence interval (CI): 90.1, 96.0) vs. SD-OCT combined with PS-OCT 92.6% (95% = CI: 89.3, 95.4)]; adding PS-OCT did not significantly improve accuracy across all observers (p = 0.82), though expert observers benefited significantly (p = 0.0018). Interobserver and intraobserver agreement ranged from substantial to near perfect. These findings suggest PS-OCT can be interpreted reliably after brief training and may enhance accuracy for experienced users. Further research should explore structured training and real-time applications for comprehensive surgical margin evaluation.

title: A New Application of 64 CuCl 2 PET/CT: Imaging of Cats With Mammary Carcinoma.
abstract: Feline mammary carcinoma (FMC) is an aggressive and highly metastatic cancer that shares molecular and clinical characteristics with human triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), making it a relevant comparative model for a disease lacking targeted therapies. This study investigated the feasibility and clinical utility of 64 CuCl 2 PET/CT imaging in cats with naturally occurring mammary carcinoma. Eight cats (seven tumour-bearing, one healthy control) were administered an intravenous dose of 64 CuCl 2 and underwent whole-body PET/CT imaging. Semi-quantitative analysis was performed using standardized uptake values (SUVs), and tumour-to-muscle ratios were calculated to assess lesion conspicuity. Serum ceruloplasmin concentrations were measured as a marker of systemic copper metabolism. All primary masses were 64 Cu-avid and conspicuous, with consistently elevated tumour-to-muscle ratios across tumour-bearing cats, allowing clear differentiation between neoplastic and normal tissue. Imaging provided additional staging information by identifying locally invasive and metastatic disease that was not fully evident on physical examination. Physiologic tracer distribution was characterized by high uptake in the liver and gallbladder and low uptake in skeletal muscle, which served as a reliable reference tissue. Serum ceruloplasmin concentrations varied widely and did not correlate with tumour uptake. These findings suggest that 64 CuCl 2 PET/CT is a feasible functional imaging modality for FMC, potentially aiding in tumour detection. This was an exploratory study, and not all imaging results could be confirmed by cytology or histopathology. Nonetheless, our findings suggest that 64 CuCl 2 PET/CT should be investigated further as a method for probing copper utilization in FMC.

title: Clinical Presentation, Acute Clinical Response, Drug Tolerability, and Short-Term Outcome of Cats Treated for Acute Congestive Heart Failure With Pimobendan (2017-2022): 71 Cases.
abstract: Objective To describe clinical effects, drug tolerability, and short-term outcomes of cats treated with pimobendan (PB) in conjunction with other therapies for acute congestive heart failure (CHF). Design Retrospective single-center study (2017 to 2022). Setting Academic teaching and referral hospital. Animals Seventy-one cats with acute CHF treated with PB and furosemide. Treatment included dobutamine (DB) in 15 cases. Measurements and main results Physical examination results, laboratory results, and radiographic pulmonary infiltrate scoring were assessed in all cats at admission and 24 h later. Respiratory rate and radiographic pulmonary infiltrate scores decreased after 24 h of therapy (p < 0.0001 for both values). Anemia and hypochloremia were more common than azotemia, hyponatremia, and hypokalemia on Day 1. Serum chloride and potassium concentrations decreased, and serum creatinine concentration increased after therapy (p < 0.05), but none of these values was associated with prolonged hospitalization or reduced survival. Cats receiving PB exhibited few adverse clinical signs. Seven of 15 cats (47%) that received concurrent DB therapy were suspected of having adverse effects that responded to decreased dosage or discontinuation of the medication. There was no difference in survival to discharge (p = 0.17) or days of hospitalization (p = 0.78) between cats receiving DB therapy and those that did not. Overall survival to discharge was 76%, and 75% of cats discharged alive were discharged in ≤3 days. Conclusions The short-term prognosis for cats treated for acute CHF was good, and PB therapy appeared to be well tolerated. Most cats showed clinical and radiographic improvement in the first 24 h of therapy and were hospitalized for ≤3 days. The addition of DB to therapy in some cats did not alter survival and was associated with adverse clinical signs in 7/15 cats (47%) treated with DB.

title: Effect of thoracic duct identification by CT lymphangiography and intraoperative contrast on surgical outcome in cats with idiopathic chylothorax.
abstract: Objective To report the success of thoracic duct (TD) enhancement in cats with idiopathic chylothorax on preoperative computed tomography lymphangiography (CTLA) and intraoperative TD colorization (IOC), and to compare surgical outcomes between cats that did and did not have successful pre- and intraoperative TD enhancement. Study design Multi-institutional retrospective study. Animals A total of 24 cats undergoing preoperative CTLA, IOC and TD ligation between February 2016 and January 2025. Methods Signalment, preoperative diagnostics, method of iohexol administration and quality of TD enhancement on CTLA, surgical procedure, success of TD enhancement via intraoperative colorization, postoperative complications, and clinical outcome were reviewed. Results TD enhancement on CTLA was successful in 70.8% of cats, with similar quality of enhancement appreciated with metatarsal and popliteal iohexol injection. TD colorization with indocyanine green (ICG) seen via near-infrared fluorescence (NIRF) was successful in four of five (80%) cats, while methylene blue was successful in eight of 15 (53%) cats. When both TD enhancement on CTLA and IOC occurred, clinical resolution rates were highest (77%) and significantly longer survival times were observed (p = .002), compared to when either CTLA or IOC (53%) or neither (25%) was successful. Conclusion Successful enhancement of the TD via CTLA and IOC led to higher clinical resolution rates and was associated with longer survival compared to when only one or neither modality was successful. Clinical significance The success of TD enhancement via CTLA and IOC may have prognostic significance for cats with idiopathic chylothorax.

title: Outcome following lag screw fixation of non-C3 carpal slab fractures in horses.
abstract: Objective To describe clinical features and short- and long-term outcomes of horses treated with lag screw fixation of slab fractures of the radial carpal (Cr), intermediate carpal (Ci), ulnar carpal (Cu), second (C2) or fourth (C4) carpal bones. Study design Retrospective case study. Animals Horses (n = 19) treated with lag screw fixation for slab fractures of Cr, Ci, Cu, C2 or C4. Methods Medical records of patients with carpal slab fractures were reviewed, and those undergoing internal fixation of slab fractures involving Cr, Ci, Cu, C2, or C4 carpal bones from January 2008 to January 2026 were included. Long-term outcomes were obtained by a standardized questionnaire. Descriptive data are presented. Results Predominant breeds included Thoroughbreds (7/19) and Warmbloods (7/19). A total of 10 of 19 fractures were caused by traumatic falls, including six during recovery from general anesthesia. Five of 19 surgeries were performed with arthroscopic guidance, and 14/19 surgeries were performed with computed tomography (CT) guidance. Survival beyond 1 year was 88%, with 53% returning to previous athletic function and 71% owner satisfaction. Conclusion Prognosis for return to the previous level of work was good and comparable to that previously reported for internal fixation of C3 slab fractures. Clinical significance Lag screw fixation provides good outcomes in survival, return to work, and owner satisfaction for slab fractures of Cr, Ci, Cu, C2, or C4.
