title: Beyond chemobrain: A stepwise approach to identifying cognitive impairment in non-CNS cancer survivors.
abstract: Cancer-related cognitive impairment (CRCI) is common in patients with non-central nervous system malignancies, but its identification remains difficult because symptoms are heterogeneous, may predate treatment, and are not captured by a single measure. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on epidemiology, clinical phenotype, risk factors, neuropsychological assessment, neuroimaging, and practical pathways for identifying CRCI in oncology care. Emerging literature highlights subjective-objective discordance and self-awareness as clinically relevant dimensions. Prevalence varies by timing and method, with higher estimates from self-report than from screening tools or formal batteries. Identification is more reliable when assessment combines patient-reported outcomes (PRO), brief objective screening, and focused neuropsychological testing within baseline vulnerability and concurrent symptom burden. Older age, lower cognitive reserve, pretreatment cognitive impairment, systemic illness, fatigue, insomnia, mood symptoms, pain, and medication effects are major modifiers. In clinical settings, neuroimaging is useful primarily for differential diagnosis: conventional brain MRI excludes competing neurologic disorders, while volumetric MRI, diffusion imaging, resting-state functional MRI, and [18F]FDG-PET currently provide group-level evidence rather than individual diagnostic signatures. At present, CRCI is best identified through a stepwise clinical strategy integrating PRO evaluation, objective testing, risk profiling, and selective imaging, considering individual patient modifiers rather than a single diagnostic test.

title: Prognostic value of CT-measured baseline tumor volume in nivolumab-treated metastatic renal cell carcinoma.
abstract: Objective To evaluate the association between baseline metastatic tumor volume measured on computed tomography (CT) and survival outcomes in patients with metastatic renal cell carcinoma (mRCC) receiving nivolumab as second line or later line therapy. Materials and methods We retrospectively analyzed 43 patients with mRCC treated with nivolumab between August 2013 and March 2022. Baseline metastatic tumor volume was measured on CT scans obtained within 30 days before treatment initiation. The cohort median (117 cm 3 ) was used as an exploratory, data derived cut-off to define low- and high-volume groups. Progression free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards models. Results Median PFS and OS were 26.97 and 28.11 months, respectively. Median PFS was 40.62 months in the low-volume group and 9.74 months in the high-volume group (p=0.012), while median OS was 46.9 and 12.89 months, respectively (p=0.006). High tumor volume and multiple metastatic sites were associated with poorer survival outcomes. Baseline imbalances in IMDC risk classification and nivolumab treatment line were observed between groups. Conclusion Higher baseline metastatic tumor volume was associated with poorer survival outcomes in patients with mRCC treated with nivolumab. CT-based tumor volumetry may provide complementary prognostic information; however, these exploratory findings require validation in larger, prospective cohorts.

title: Artificial intelligence in veterinary diagnostic histopathology: Concepts, applications, and clinical implementation.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) in human diagnostic histopathology has advanced rapidly, but clinical adoption has lagged behind research. Veterinary diagnostic pathology, being less regulated, could adopt AI faster, but the extent of its integration into diagnostic laboratories is unknown. This article combines a narrative introduction to key concepts, a scoping review of published applications, and an exploratory survey of diagnostic laboratories to provide an overview of AI in veterinary diagnostic histopathology. The narrative review highlights emerging approaches, including vision transformer-based foundation models and self-supervised learning, which may improve generalizability and reduce data requirements, although adaptation to the veterinary context remains challenging. The scoping review identified 34 studies published through a September 5, 2025, literature search, indicating steady but limited growth. Most used convolutional neural networks for relatively low-level tasks such as cell quantification, area measurement, and diagnosis. The survey had a low response rate (2 of 5 laboratories). Both respondents recognized potential benefits of AI. One laboratory had incorporated 2 AI models into routine diagnostic workflows and was evaluating additional applications, while the other had not yet implemented AI but was actively considering several models. Reported barriers included generalizability, latency, and cost. Overall, AI research in veterinary diagnostic histopathology is growing, but clinical adoption remains incompletely characterized. While less restrictive regulation may allow faster uptake than in human medicine, the lack of oversight places responsibility for validation on laboratories and pathologists. For trustworthy implementation, veterinary pathologists must understand AI fundamentals, and the field should prioritize standards for validation, transparency, and reporting.

title: Enhancing the translational potential of the ovine pulmonary adenocarcinoma model.
abstract: Ovine pulmonary adenocarcinoma (OPA) is a transmissible lung cancer of sheep caused by Jaagsiekte sheep retrovirus (JSRV), resulting in substantial animal welfare concerns and economic losses worldwide. We previously developed a bronchoscopic JSRV catheter instillation technique targeting the cardiac lung lobe that reliably reproduced the spectrum of OPA lesions observed in naturally occurring disease. Beyond its value for investigating JSRV pathogenesis, this experimental system provides a large animal platform for studying human lung cancer. Here, we sought to enhance its translational utility by increasing the number of virus inoculation sites and introducing a novel transbronchial intraparenchymal injection technique. Two-month-old lambs received JSRV at 4 lung sites: the left and right cardiac lobes by bronchoscopic catheter instillation and the left and right ventral diaphragmatic lobes by transbronchial intraparenchymal injection. Disease progression was monitored by monthly computed tomography, with postmortem examination and immunohistochemistry confirming OPA in 17/18 (94%) inoculated sheep. Six sheep (35%) developed advanced OPA, generating 22 gross tumors for translational studies. Bronchoscopic catheter instillation produced larger, faster-growing tumors with increased connective tissue, bronchus-associated lymphoid tissue, and intra-airway fluid, whereas intraparenchymal injection generated smaller, localized lesions. Radiomic analysis further demonstrated distinct tumor evolution between the 2 delivery methods. These findings show that both inoculation techniques are safe and effective, while also producing complementary tumor phenotypes. By increasing tumor yield per animal while generating lesions with differing growth characteristics, this refined OPA model provides a more versatile and translationally relevant platform for lung cancer research, while supporting the reduction in animal use.

title: High-Grade Percutaneous Medial Collateral Ligament Pie-Crusting Is Not Associated With Clinically Meaningful Valgus Instability.
abstract: Background Medial collateral ligament (MCL) pie-crusting is used during medial meniscal surgery to improve visualization and reduce the risk of chondral injuries. However, some surgeons extend the release site beyond routine incremental perforation, and the effect of this more extensive release on postoperative medial laxity remains unclear. Purpose To determine whether high-grade percutaneous MCL pie-crusting during medial meniscus posterior root tear (MMPRT) repair results in clinically meaningful valgus instability postoperatively as assessed by valgus stress radiography. Study design Case series; Level of evidence, 4. Methods A retrospective review was performed of patients who underwent isolated MMPRT repair with high-grade MCL pie-crusting and no prior knee ligament surgery. High-grade pie-crusting was defined intraoperatively by an audible and palpable release and a substantial medial compartment opening (≥6 mm) under arthroscopic visualization. Postoperative bilateral valgus stress radiographs were obtained at a mean of 5.9 ± 2.0 months with the knee positioned at 20° of flexion. Gapping was measured in millimeters, and the side-to-side difference was calculated using the contralateral knee as an internal control. Medial collateral ligament (MCL) pie-crusting is used during medial meniscal surgery to improve visualization and reduce the risk of chondral injuries. A retrospective review was performed of patients who underwent isolated MMPRT repair with high-grade MCL pie-crusting and no prior knee ligament surgery. A total of 21 patients met inclusion criteria. The mean medial compartment gapping was 7.84 ± 1.65 mm in the operative knee and 6.62 ± 1.37 mm in the contralateral knee. High-grade percutaneous MCL pie-crusting advanced to a defined intraoperative endpoint during MMPRT repair resulted in small increases in medial compartment gapping that remained below biomechanically defined instability thresholds. title: Iron oxide nanoparticles for hepatocellular carcinoma theranostics: From nanoplatform design to clinical translation.
abstract: The challenges in early diagnosis and effective treatment of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) are largely attributable to the underlying cirrhosis, impaired hepatic reserve, and the added complexity of heterogeneous tumor vascularity in many patients. Iron oxide nanoparticles (IONPs) are promising platforms for HCC diagnosis and treatment because of their magnetic properties, tunable magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) contrast, magnetothermal conversion capability, and modifiable surface chemistry. These features enable IONPs to be used for image-guided diagnosis, liver-directed locoregional therapy, systemic drug delivery, and treatment monitoring. In this review, we summarize the composition, crystal structure, size-dependent magnetic properties, surface modification, and in vivo fate of IONPs, along with how these characteristics influence their performance in HCC imaging and therapy. For diagnostic applications, we focus on passive accumulation, particularly mononuclear phagocyte system (MPS)-mediated hepatic contrast, ligand-mediated active targeting, and multimodal imaging. We then review therapeutic strategies, including magnetic hyperthermia (MHT), stimuli-responsive drug delivery, and combination therapy. Major barriers to clinical translation are also addressed, encompassing the heterogeneous enhanced permeability and retention (EPR) effect, high background uptake by non-tumoral liver tissue, liver function-related safety concerns, limitations of alternating magnetic fields, and manufacturing reproducibility.

title: GFC-Unet: An optimized 3D U-Net-based method for brain tumor segmentation.
abstract: Accurate brain tumor segmentation is critical for diagnosis and treatment planning. However, U-Net-based models struggle with complex tumor morphologies and fine boundaries. This paper proposes a novel brain tumor segmentation network, termed GFC-Unet. Built upon the 3D U-Net architecture, this network introduces three core modules: (1) the Multi-modal Feature Recalibration (MFR) module; (2) the Gated Feature Convolution (GFC) module; and (3) the Feature Uncertainty Evaluation (FUE) module. Experimental results on the Brain Tumor Segmentation (BraTS) 2020 and 2021 datasets demonstrate that GFC-Unet achieves Dice coefficients of 92.82%, 87.74%, and 87.47% on BraTS2020, and 92.61%, 87.49%, and 86.89% on BraTS2021 for whole tumor (WT), tumor core (TC), and enhancing tumor (ET), respectively. Ablation studies validate the effectiveness of each module. Furthermore, extended experiments on the Data Science Bowl (DSB) 2018 cell nucleus segmentation and International Skin Imaging Collaboration (ISIC) 2018 skin lesion segmentation tasks demonstrate the strong generalization capability. By integrating these modules, GFC-Unet improves segmentation accuracy and boundary delineation, demonstrating promise for supporting clinical decision-making.

title: Photon-counting CT in tumor imaging: A review of comparative evaluations and technical innovations.
abstract: Malignant tumors remain a major global public health challenge, and the limitations of conventional energy-integrating detector computed tomography (EID-CT) in spatial resolution, early lesion detection, and quantitative analysis continue to constrain precise diagnosis and treatment of tumors. Photon-counting computed tomography (PCCT), an emerging CT technology, has shown promising potential in tumor imaging. In this study, the literature on PCCT in oncologic imaging was searched and screened. Existing reviews lack an integrated analysis of comparative evaluation and technological innovation for oncological applications, with insufficient large-sample clinical evidence and discussion of multimodal imaging-AI integration. Regarding these issues, the included literature was classified and analyzed based on comparative evaluation research and technological innovation research. First, the medical background and theoretical basis of PCCT in tumor imaging are introduced. Subsequently, recent relevant studies are reviewed from the perspectives of comparative evaluation and technological innovation. Finally, the current research status and development trends in this field are analyzed and discussed. PCCT achieves high-resolution, low-dose, spectral tumor imaging for lesion detection and tissue characterization. Therefore, PCCT may support precise imaging diagnosis and personalized tumor treatment.

title: Bilateral Palatal Root Agenesis of Maxillary Fourth Premolars in 2 Welsh Corgis: A Cone Beam Computed Tomography (CBCT)-Based Case Report.
abstract: Palatal root agenesis of the maxillary fourth premolar (PM4) is a rarely reported developmental anomaly in dogs. This report describes 2 cases of bilateral palatal root agenesis in Welsh Corgis that had complicated crown-root fractures. Initial intraoral radiography suggested absence of the palatal root; however, cone beam computed tomography (CBCT) with 3-dimensional reconstruction provided definitive visualization confirming complete bilateral absence of the palatal roots and associated root canal systems in both patients. Based on these anatomical findings, conventional root canal treatment was performed only on the mesiobuccal and distal roots, which resulted in favorable clinical outcomes during the follow-up period. Furthermore, a 10-year retrospective review of 6683 dental records across 2 referral hospitals identified only 2 cases among 244 Welsh Corgis, which corresponded to record-based frequencies of 0.03% (95% CI, 0.004-0.108%) in the overall canine population and 0.82% (95% CI, 0.099-2.929%) in Welsh Corgis. These findings suggested that palatal root agenesis of the maxillary PM4, although rare, may occur bilaterally and should be carefully considered during diagnosis and treatment planning of fractured carnassial teeth. This study highlighted the utility of CBCT in distinguishing true root agenesis from other anatomical variations. Although both cases occurred in Welsh Corgis, larger studies are required to determine whether any breed-related tendency exists.

title: AMSSE-SwinTrans: A harmonized multimodal hybrid framework with explainable AI for ischemic stroke lesion segmentation.
abstract: BackgroundAccurate ischemic stroke lesion segmentation from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is important but challenging due to variability in lesion morphology. Traditional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) effectively capture local spatial features but often struggle to capture long-range contextual dependencies needed for irregular lesions. Transformer-based architectures are good at capturing global context; however, they are computationally expensive and difficult to deploy in resource-constrained environments. The black-box nature of deep learning models limits their clinical adoption owing to lack of transparency.ObjectiveThis study introduces AMSSE-SwinTrans, a lightweight hybrid CNN-Transformer framework to make stroke lesion segmentation accurate, efficient and interpretable across different MRI modalities.MethodsThis study proposes AMSSE-SwinTrans, a lightweight hybrid CNN-Transformer framework that combines adaptive multi-scale squeeze-and-excitation (AMSSE) module with simplified transformer blocks employing multi-head self-attention, along with explainable AI (XAI) for clinical interpretation. The model was evaluated on a single-channel harmonized multimodal two-dimensional MRI Slices from ATLAS v2.0 and ISLES 2022 dataset.ResultsThe model achieved an overall Dice of 0.8629, lesion-specific Dice of 0.7535. An ablation study demonstrated a significant performance improvement when each component was added. The model comparisons were all significant with Wilcoxon signed-rank test yielding p-value ( p < 0.001) across all comparisons. With only 27.67 M parameters, 17.67 GFLOPs, and 9.22 ms inference time per slice, the architecture is well-suited for deployment in resource-constrained clinical settings. The interpretability of the model is supported by Attention Rollout and Grad-CAM++ visualizations.ConclusionAMSSE-SwinTrans establishes itself as a resource-efficient and interpretable framework for multimodal stroke lesion segmentation.

title: AI-driven biosensor data fusion for multimodal activity recognition in health monitoring systems.
abstract: BackgroundAI-driven healthcare monitoring systems are increasingly being developed to support elderly individuals through continuous and discreet monitoring of routine behavioral patterns.ObjectiveThis study aims to develop a multimodal framework for identifying mobility patterns by integrating inertial and vision-based sensor data to improve the accuracy and robustness of behavioral recognition.MethodsInertial data are denoised using a median filter, while video feeds are converted into grayscale frame sequences and enhanced using a Gaussian filter. Rectangular windowing is applied to inertial data, whereas U-Net is used for visual segmentation. Features are extracted using Gammatone Filter Cepstrum (GFC), Gaussian Likelihood Threshold Model (GLTM), Power Spectral Density (PSD), and temporal moments from inertial data, and Distance Transform, Gist, ORB, and SURF from visual data. The modalities are fused using shared class labels, followed by fuzzy-logic-based feature optimization and classification using a CNN-GRU hybrid model.ResultsThe proposed multimodal framework achieves 95.20% accuracy on the Continuous Multimodal Human Action Dataset (C-MHAD) and 94.79% on the multi-modal 3D human pose estimation dataset using mmWave, RGB-D, and inertial sensors (mRI) dataset, demonstrating improved behavioral categorization compared with unimodal approaches.ConclusionThe results highlight the potential of multimodal inertial and vision-based sensing for robust AI-assisted healthcare monitoring. However, evaluation is currently limited to public benchmark datasets and requires further validation in clinical settings.

title: Design and fabrication of a lumbar spine simulator for fluoroscopy-guided intervertebral disk puncture.
abstract: Fluoroscopy-guided spinal interventions require anatomically representative and radiographically compatible physical models for procedural simulation. Cadaveric specimens and animal models, while valuable, are limited by cost, availability, ethical considerations, and restricted repeatability. These limitations motivate the development of cost-efficient lumbar spine simulators compatible with C-arm fluoroscopic imaging. Vertebrae and pelvic structures were generated from open-source STL files and fabricated using fused deposition modeling. Post-processing included surface polishing and fabrication of silicone molds to reproduce vertebral geometry. Combinations of two-component polyurethane casting resin, calcium sulfate, barium sulfate, and iohexol were tested to evaluate radiographic visibility and identify a suitable radiopaque formulation. Vertebral elements were assembled using silicone interfaces to form puncturable intervertebral spaces. Soft tissues and skin were imitated using gelatin-glycerin foam and pigmented silicone. Radiographic appearance was assessed under C-arm fluoroscopy. Among the tested formulations, polyurethane composite containing 5 wt% calcium sulfate provided sufficient radiographic visibility while avoiding excessive radiopacity and was selected for the final simulator. The simulator reproduced key lumbar anatomical features and enabled clear visualization of the needle trajectory under fluoroscopy. Design optimization produced a lighter and more compact configuration than the initial prototype. This study presents a reproducible 3D-printed lumbar spine simulator with tunable radiographic properties compatible with fluoroscopic imaging. The proposed design provides a cost-efficient physical model for image-guided procedural simulation and technical development, intended for non-commercial academic and educational use.

title: A multivariate Bayesian biomarker screening algorithm that incorporates clinical covariates.
abstract: Advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) has limited treatment options and poor survival. Early detection of HCC improves survival, but current ultrasound screening is inconsistent and poorly adhered to. Biomarker-based blood tests offer a more accurate, accessible, and reliable alternative. Recent developments in methods for early detection of HCC have focused on the trajectories of multiple biomarkers, assuming that biomarkers follow a joint hierarchical mixture model with random changepoints. We extend this model, allowing covariates to influence three aspects of the model: biomarker trajectories, diagnosis times, and subject-specific prior risks. We evaluated whether covariates could capture unexplained heterogeneity in biomarker levels to improve early detection. A Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm was implemented to derive posterior distributions used in risk calculations among future patients and to determine whether a patient has a positive screen. The screening algorithm was evaluated through simulation studies under a range of possible covariate extensions. The Hepatitis C Antiviral Long-term Treatment against Cirrhosis (HALT-C) trial was used to further study the proposed biomarker screening algorithms for HCC using cross-validation.

title: Mammogram utilization among women with vision and/or hearing loss: Insights from the 2022 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance Survey.
abstract: PurposePersons with sensory loss face significant barriers when accessing healthcare services, specifically screening for breast cancer. The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention recommend that women aged 40-74 get screened for breast cancer every 2 years; however, few studies have analyzed whether sensory loss influences the receipt of mammograms. The purpose of this study was to examine the association between sensory (vision, hearing, or dual) loss and mammography utilization among women 40-74 years of age.MethodsThis study used data for women aged 40-74 from the 2022 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance Survey (n = 55,363) to analyze the relationship between self-reported sensory loss and receipt of breast cancer screenings. Weighted complex samples logistic regression analyses were conducted using SPSS Version 29.ResultsWomen aged 40-74 with dual sensory (both vision and hearing) loss were half as likely to have received a mammogram in the past 2 years (adjusted odds ratio (AOR) = .533, 95% confidence interval (CI) = [.354-.803]) in comparison to those with neither disability. Women aged 40-74 with dual sensory (both vision and hearing) loss were twice as likely to have not received a mammogram in the past 5 years or more (AOR = 2.480, 95% CI = [1.317-4.669]) in comparison to those with neither disability.ConclusionWomen aged 40-74 with dual sensory loss were significantly less likely to receive mammograms. Further research focused on understanding and addressing the factors influencing access to breast cancer screenings is needed.

title: Breast cancer overdiagnosis due to mammography screening-A long-term follow-up population study of BreastScreen Norway.
abstract: ObjectivesEstimates of breast cancer overdiagnosis related to mammography screening vary substantially. Overdiagnosis is commonly defined as cases that would not have been detected during the person's remaining lifetime in the absence of screening. We here aim to quantify overdiagnosis in the population-based BreastScreen Norway mammography screening program using long-term follow-up and more detailed modeling than previous studies.SettingWe applied data on Norwegian screening patterns and breast carcinoma incidence for the period 1987-2019, covering women aged 49-84, leveraging the gradual implementation of the organized biennial BreastScreen Norway screening program for women aged 50-69 during 1995-2005.MethodsUsing an extended age-period-cohort model, we estimated excess lifetime risk of invasive breast cancer and ductal carcinoma in situ in the presence of program screening, as an indicator of overdiagnosis among screen-detected cases.ResultsLifetime risk of breast carcinomas was 6.6% (95% confidence interval: 2.5%-10.7%) higher for invited than for non-invited women. This indicates that 18% (95% confidence interval: 7.3%-28.0%) of screen-detected cases may be overdiagnosed, and that approximately one in 86 (95% confidence interval: 54-210) screened women were overdiagnosed during their screening period. Using effect estimates from previous studies, we estimated that approximately three women are overdiagnosed for every breast cancer death prevented by screening, and that 87% of overdiagnosed tumors might grow extremely slowly.ConclusionsOverdiagnosis related to mammography screening is a considerable problem, but its extent may be smaller than reported in some previous studies. Most overdiagnosed tumors likely grow very slowly.

title: Diagnostic Utility of Velopharyngeal MRI in Children With Unexplained Velopharyngeal Insufficiency.
abstract: ObjectiveTo explore the utility of velopharyngeal MRI in contributing additional diagnostic information for patients with velopharyngeal insufficiency (VPI) of unknown etiology.DesignRetrospective cohort study.SettingTertiary children's hospital.ParticipantsChildren with clinically significant VPI without a confirmed etiology.InterventionsStandardized perceptual speech assessment with nasometry, non-sedated MRI, and multidisciplinary review for treatment planning.Main Outcome MeasuresMRI-informed etiologic classification, anatomic and functional contributors to VPI, and management recommendations.ResultsAmong 89 children, six (6.7%) presented with clinically significant VPI of unknown etiology on routine examination. MRI identified occult submucous cleft palate or atypical levator veli palatini morphology in five (83.3%) and adenoid-supported VP closure in three (50%). Involution was expected to unmask increased pharyngeal depth in two (33.3%). MRI supported patient-specific recommendations for speech therapy, surgical interventions, and longitudinal monitoring.ConclusionsMRI provided clinically meaningful diagnostic information beyond routine examination and informed management decisions for children with VPI.

title: Lung Localization of Endosalpingiosis: Challenges of Rare Manifestation of Müllerianosis.
abstract: Endosalpingiosis (ES) is a benign, nonneoplastic condition of the Müllerian system characterized by the ectopic implantation of fallopian tube-like ciliated columnar epithelium. Unlike endometriosis, ES lacks endometrial stroma and therefore does not produce the characteristic hemorrhagic episodes or extensive inflammatory responses associated with endometriosis. Although ES is primarily identified in the visceral pelvic peritoneum, extrapelvic manifestations are exceedingly rare, with pulmonary and pleural localization, accounting for ∼0.1% of reports. This report describes the clinical presentation of thoracic ES in a 40-year-old woman who presented with catamenial spontaneous primary pneumothorax. Despite a remote surgical history for ovarian endometriosis 10 years earlier, the patient had a prolonged period of clinical latency and no evidence of current pelvic recurrence. Videothoracoscopic surgery revealed a 5-mm apical pulmonary nodule and diffusely calcified pleural plaques. Histopathology and immunohistochemistry are remain gold-standard diagnostic methods for differentiating ES from thoracic endometriosis syndrome or malignancy. The diagnosis was confirmed by epithelial immunoreactivity for Müllerian transcription factors (PAX8 and WT1), keratin 7, and estrogen/progesterone receptors, together with the absence of cluster of differentiation 10 expression, which argued against endometrial stroma, and calretinin negativity, which argued against mesothelial origin. The pathophysiology of thoracic ES may resemble that of pulmonary endometriosis, involving transdiaphragmatic or vascular migration of Müllerian cells. For symptomatic presentations, surgical excision combined with long-term suppressive hormonal therapy is recommended to reduce epithelial proliferation. Given that the emerging literature suggests a possible link between ES and gynecological malignancies, rigorous long-term postoperative surveillance remains essential.

title: Aberrant Desmin Expression in a Middle Ear Neuroendocrine Tumor: Expanding the Immunophenotypic Spectrum.
abstract: Middle ear neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) are uncommon neoplasms that exhibit both epithelial and neuroendocrine differentiation. Aberrant desmin expression in middle ear NET has not been documented previously and may create a diagnostic pitfall due to morphologic overlap with myogenic and rhabdoid tumors. A 52-year-old man presented with right ear pain, fullness, and facial deviation. Imaging revealed a soft-tissue mass involving the middle ear cavity and the mastoid air cells, with ossicular erosion. Histopathology showed an infiltrative neoplasm arranged in nests, trabeculae, cords, and pseudoacini composed of monomorphic cells with plasmacytoid/rhabdoid morphology. Immunohistochemically, the tumor cells showed diffuse positivity for KRT, synaptophysin, chromogranin, and diffuse strong desmin expression, while myogenin, MYOD1, p63, calponin, TTF1, CDX2, and GATA3 were negative. SMARCB1/INI1 expression was retained, and the Ki67 index was <2%. A diagnosis of middle ear NET with aberrant desmin positivity was rendered. The patient remained disease-free 18 months following surgical excision. The index patient expands the immunophenotypic spectrum of middle ear NET by documenting diffuse aberrant desmin expression. Awareness of this unusual finding is important to avoid misdiagnosis as rhabdomyosarcoma or other rhabdoid neoplasms. Accurate diagnosis requires careful integration of morphologic and immunohistochemical features, and long-term follow-up remains essential despite the generally indolent behavior of middle ear NETs.

title: IDH-Mutant Astrocytomas in Patients Older than 55 Years: A Retrospective Analysis.
abstract: Diffuse gliomas are the most common malignant brain tumors in adults, stratified by isocitrate dehydrogenase ( IDH1/IDH2 ) mutation status. While the median age for central nervous system (CNS) World Health Organization (WHO) grade 2 to 3 IDH-mutant astrocytomas is 38 years, older patients of >55 years predominantly exhibit IDH-wildtype gliomas and confer a poorer prognosis. To examine the clinicopathologic spectrum of IDH-mutant astrocytomas in older adults, we retrospectively reviewed all astrocytic tumors diagnosed at our institution between 2021 and 2024 in patients >55 years. Twenty-two IDH-mutant astrocytomas (median age: 63 years; range: 56-79; male:female = 9:13) were identified and compared descriptively to a historical cohort of 179 IDH-mutant astrocytomas in younger patients. Grade distribution among older patients paralleled that of younger adults: CNS WHO grade 2 (55%), grade 3 (18%), and grade 4 (27%). Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed T2/FLAIR mismatch sign in 25% of grade 2 tumors and in none of the higher grades; 50% of grade 2 tumors demonstrated contrast enhancement. IDH1 p.R132H accounted for 95% of mutations, with 1 p.R132G variant. ATRX loss was seen in 71% and strong p53 immunoreactivity in 83% of evaluable tumors. Copy-number analysis ( n = 10) revealed CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion in 10% and heterozygous loss in 20% . Despite their rarity, IDH-mutant astrocytomas in older adults are more prevalent than historically appreciated and maintain imaging and molecular profiles akin to tumors in younger adults. Accordingly, IDH1 p.R132H-specific immunohistochemistry remains a cost-effective first-line screening tool irrespective of age.

title: Silent Hypoxemia in High-Altitude Pulmonary Edema: A Case Report.
abstract: We report a case of a trekker who ascended to Tilicho Lake (4919 m) from Kathmandu (1400 m) in 3 days. On day 3, he descended to Shree Kharka (4045 m). The following day, he trekked to Yak Kharka (4025 m) where, although he had no symptoms, he measured his own oxygen saturation (SpO 2 ) at 72% in ambient air. Overnight, his SpO 2 ranged from 75-80% on oxygen 2L/min via nasal cannula. The next day his SpO 2 dropped to 47% while still on oxygen. He descended on horseback to Manang (3500 m), where his SpO 2 was 70% on room air. He was diagnosed with high-altitude pulmonary edema (HAPE). He was treated with oxygen, 4L by nasal cannula, and nifedipine. The following day, he flew to Kathmandu, where he made a full recovery. Trekkers may develop life-threatening HAPE without obvious symptoms or signs. Slow ascent can decrease the likelihood of developing HAPE, but trekkers do not always follow the recommended ascent rate. Early detection, by history and physical examination and with point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS), if available, is critical in resource-limited regions such as ours. The keys to managing HAPE are early recognition and management, including descending to a lower altitude as soon as possible.

title: Limb Body Wall Complex: Report of a Discordant Case in a Monozygotic Twin Pregnancy.
abstract: Limb Body Wall Complex (LBWC) is a rare, severe congenital malformation syndrome characterized by thoracoabdominal wall defects, craniofacial anomalies, and limb and spinal malformations. Its incidence ranges from 0.04 to 3.3 per 10,000 births. We present a case of LBWC diagnosed in a monochorionic diamniotic twin pregnancy at 17 weeks of gestation. The mother was 28-year-old, primigravida, and had no notable medical history. Ultrasound identified abnormal positioning of 1 embryo, suggestive of adherence to the amnion. First-trimester scans revealed increased nuchal translucency and foot malposition in fetus A, while fetus B showed a cystic hygroma along with significant abdominal wall and spinal anomalies. Selective termination of fetus B was performed at 17 weeks but was complicated by the intrauterine demise of both fetuses. Postmortem examination of fetus B confirmed classical LBWC features: abdominopelvic wall defect with evisceration adherent to the placenta, lower limb amyotrophy, severe kyphoscoliosis, and craniofacial abnormalities. The pathogenesis of LBWC remains unclear, with hypotheses including early amnion rupture, vascular disruptions, and embryonic developmental errors. Diagnosis is typically made by prenatal ultrasound in the first trimester. LBWC is generally lethal, warranting pregnancy termination. While multiple pregnancies may increase the risk, discordant presentation in monochorionic twins remains exceptionally rare.

title: Pretreatment MRI radiomics for predicting recurrence and metastasis after hypofractionated stereotactic radiosurgery in uveal melanoma.
abstract: PurposeTo develop and internally evaluate pretreatment MR-based radiomics models for predicting local recurrence and metastasis after hypofractionated stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) for uveal melanoma.MethodsThis retrospective study analyzed pretreatment MRI (T1-weighted, T2-weighted, contrast-enhanced T1-weighted) of 88 SRS-treated UM patients. Tumors were segmented on the axial slice with the greatest cross-sectional area, and 854 radiomic features were extracted for each sequence. After inter-observer reproducibility filtering (ICC ≥ 0.80) and elastic-net feature selection, separate Gaussian Naive Bayes models for local recurrence and metastasis were developed using the retained features with a 70:30 train-test split. SMOTE was applied within training folds to address class imbalance. Held-out test set performance was assessed using AUC, F1 score, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values.ResultsThe local-recurrence model achieved an AUC of 0.958, accuracy of 0.889, sensitivity of 1.00 (3/3), and specificity of 0.875 (21/24). The metastasis model showed limited discrimination (AUC, 0.528; accuracy, 0.815; sensitivity, 0.333 [1/3]; specificity, 0.875 [21/24]). Among three-fraction treatments, a total dose >45 Gy was associated with less local recurrence ( p = 0.010), whereas no other clinical variable was significantly associated with either outcome.ConclusionMRI radiomics showed promising discrimination for local recurrence but limited discrimination for metastasis. These findings should be interpreted with caution given the small number of events in the test set and warrant external validation in larger cohorts .

title: Hemodialysis vascular access flow measurements by AFM ® and Transonic ® devices: A bicentric comparative study.
abstract: Objective Clinical monitoring remains central to vascular access care, while surveillance of vascular access blood flow (Qa) provides information for detecting dysfunction. Ultrasound dilution (UD), such as Transonic ® , is widely used for Qa measurement but may be limited by workflow, personnel, and time constraints. Alternatively, conductivity-based approaches integrated into dialysis machines enable automated intradialytic estimation of Qa without interrupting treatment. This bicentric study evaluated agreement between an automated ionic dialysance-based method, AFM ® , and UD, and assessed its clinical performance across prespecified Qa ranges. Methods We conducted an observational method-comparison study in two Italian hemodialysis centers. Paired Qa measurements were obtained in 64 patients during routine hemodialysis sessions using AFM ® and Transonic ® . Agreement and association were assessed using Spearman correlation, Passing-Bablok regression, Bland-Altman analysis, Lin's concordance correlation coefficient, and weighted Cohen's kappa. Clinical performance was evaluated across prespecified Qa ranges: ⩽600, >600 to <2000, and ⩾2000 mL/min. Results Median Qa was 1145 (IQR, 807-1536) mL/min with AFM and 1436 (IQR, 947-1980) mL/min with UD. The two methods showed strong correlation (ρ = 0.849, p < 0.001) and moderate-to-good concordance (CCC = 0.73). Bland-Altman analysis revealed a systematic underestimation at higher flows, with magnitude-dependent variability. Overall categorical agreement was 84% (weighted κ = 0.72). Performance was highest in the clinically relevant ranges of ⩽600 and >600 to <2000 mL/min, with 100% and 93% sensitivities, and F1-scores of 0.89 and 0.88, respectively. Agreement declined in the high-flow range (⩾2000 mL/min), where sensitivity dropped to 53%. Conclusion AFM ® showed strong correlation and substantial clinical agreement with UD, particularly in the low- and intermediate-flow ranges most relevant to routine vascular access surveillance. Its automated intradialytic implementation supports its use as a practical screening tool for Qa surveillance. However, high-flow measurements should be interpreted cautiously and further evaluated when clinically indicated.

title: Autologous haematopoietic stem cell transplantation affects paramagnetic rim lesions in multiple sclerosis.
abstract: Background Available literature shows a marginal or no effect of disease-modifying therapies on paramagnetic rim lesions (PRLs), a promising magnetic resonance imaging marker of chronic inflammation in multiple sclerosis. Objective To investigate longitudinal changes in PRL count in people with multiple sclerosis treated with autologous haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (AHSCT), exploring their potential as predictors of treatment response. Methods Monocentric study including 30 AHSCT-treated people with multiple sclerosis who performed at least two brain magnetic resonance imaging scans with susceptibility-weighted imaging either (i) before and after AHSCT (pre/post-AHSCT group; n = 12) or (ii) after AHSCT only (post-AHSCT group; n = 18). Results In the pre/post-AHSCT group, PRL count decreased in 2/5 (40%) PRL-positive cases over a median of 21 (7-74) months; 5/26 (19%) PRL s resolved. In the post-AHSCT group, PRL count decreased in 4/7 (57%) PRL -positive cases over a median of 51 (6-57) months; 10/20 (50%) PRL s resolved. The annualised paramagnetic rim lesion disappearance rate was -0.36 and -0.43 in the two groups, respectively. No new PRL appeared. Baseline PRL count correlated with disability in the pre/post-AHSCT group only (r = 0.741, p = 0.006). Conclusions Given the reported long persistence of PRLs, these data indicate that AHSCT may accelerate their disappearance, suggesting an effect within the central nervous system on microglia/macrophages. PRLs could predict response to central nervous system-bioavailable treatments.

title: Survivor bias and disease progression in observational cohorts in multiple sclerosis.
abstract: Background Long-term studies on multiple sclerosis progression often face dropout, possibly among those with more aggressive disease, biasing the cohort. Objectives We assessed potential survivorship bias in a long-term observational multiple sclerosis cohort. Methods Three hundred sixty-one patients with multiple sclerosis were followed for 10 years, with clinical assessments, blood biomarkers and magnetic resonance imaging at baseline, follow-up 1 and follow-up 2. Progression was defined as an Expanded Disability Status Scale increase. Dropout was analysed and predicted; estimated Expanded Disability Status Scale was calculated for dropouts to assess bias. Brain volumes were normalized. Results One hundred and sixty-two patients with multiple sclerosis completed all follow-ups; 81 showed progression. Dropout rates were 97/361 at follow-up 1 and 102/264 at follow-up 2. Dropouts had worse Expanded Disability Status Scale, Nine-Hole Peg test, Timed 25-Foot Walk, lower brain volume and higher lesion volume before dropping out. Blood biomarkers did not differ. Main dropout predictors were higher baseline Expanded Disability Status Scale, lesion volume, worse Nine-Hole Peg test and shorter disease duration. Median estimated Expanded Disability Status Scale at follow-up 2 for dropouts was 5.5 versus 3.5 for non-dropouts. Discussion Fewer than half completed the study. High lesion load and worse clinical status predicted dropout. This may cause underestimation of progression and reduced statistical power. Similar bias may affect other long-term studies in chronic diseases.

title: Pedal acceleration time-Guided management of diabetic foot ulcers with borderline ischemia.
abstract: Background: The management of diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) with borderline ischemia remains challenging due to the absence of reliable physiological markers to guide revascularization decisions. Pedal acceleration time (PAT) is a Doppler-derived measure of distal perfusion that may improve risk stratification. This study aimed to evaluate a PAT-guided management strategy in patients with DFUs and borderline perfusion by assessing its ability to guide treatment allocation, and its association with wound healing and amputation-free survival (AFS). Methods: In this prospective quasi-experimental study, 263 consecutive patients with DFUs and abnormal ankle-brachial index (ABI) findings were enrolled. PAT was measured using duplex ultrasound of the pedal arteries. A predefined cutoff of ⩾ 180 ms was used to guide treatment allocation: patients with a PAT ⩾ 180 ms underwent endovascular revascularization, whereas those with a PAT < 180 ms underwent debridement alone. Primary outcomes included AFS, wound healing, major adverse limb events (MALE), and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) at 24 months. The diagnostic accuracy of PAT for detecting significant infrapopliteal stenosis was assessed using conventional angiography as the reference standard. Results: At 24 months, AFS was higher in the revascularization group than in the debridement-alone group, although this difference was not statistically significant (64.2% vs 58.4%; p = 0.344). However, a Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated a significant difference in AFS over the follow-up period (log-rank p < 0.05). Overall survival and freedom from reintervention did not differ significantly between groups. Multivariable analysis identified advanced stages of the Wound, Ischemia, and foot Infection (WIfI) classification and a higher PAT category as predictors of major amputation. Advanced WIfI stage was also associated with nonhealing, and the PAT category showed a borderline association with nonhealing. A receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance of PAT for detecting significant arterial stenosis, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.88. At a cutoff ⩾ 180 ms, sensitivity was 84.0% (95% CI 76.6-89.4) and specificity was 81.2% (95% CI 73.8-86.8), with an overall accuracy of 82.5%. Conclusions: PAT provides a useful physiological adjunct to distal perfusion assessment in DFUs with borderline ischemia. A threshold of ⩾ 180 ms identifies patients with hemodynamically significant disease, and it is associated with improved risk stratification for revascularization. These findings support further evaluation of PAT as an adjunctive assessment tool in patients with borderline ischemia.

title: Emerging hydrogel platforms for disease modeling, diagnosis, and imaging of Alzheimer's disease.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disease characterized by the presence of amyloid plaques, neurofibrillary tangles, neurodegeneration, cognitive decline, and dementia. The exact pathogenesis is not well understood, as appropriate pathological and therapeutically relevant disease models remain limited. Hydrogels are hydrophilic, three-dimensional (3D) polymer networks composed of synthetic or natural materials and have diverse neuroscience applications, including drug delivery, tissue engineering, and regenerative medicine. Currently, hydrogel in vitro platforms are becoming increasingly explored for AD pathogenesis, as brain extracellular matrix-mimicking biodegradable components, for delivery of growth factors for neurons and other brain cells, AD-specific peptide release, engineered multi-region brain organoids, and therapeutic drug delivery. Beyond disease modeling, hydrogels are being used to evaluate emerging AD diagnostic and therapeutic strategies, such as biomarker sensing and the integration of imaging. Recent AD diagnostic platforms have leveraged hydrogels as biomolecule-capture matrices and signal-transduction elements to detect AD-associated biomarkers via minimally invasive or implantable systems. Hydrogels have also been harnessed in magnetic resonance imaging, ultrasound, computed tomography, and positron emission tomography imaging modalities to support imageable vehicles for therapeutic delivery. Such platforms hold promise for bridging physiologically relevant neurobiological investigation with more accessible, efficient clinical tools for AD. This review highlights recent advances in hydrogel-based disease models, diagnostic tools, and imaging technologies and their potential to integrate with brain organoids, artificial intelligence, and 3D printing to enhance mechanistic and translational applications for AD.

title: An exploratory synthetic MRI-derived FLAIR-DIR contrast in olfactory-limbic regions in mild cognitive impairment.
abstract: BackgroundOdor identification impairment is an early feature of Alzheimer's disease and predicts memory decline, but its microstructural basis remains unclear.ObjectiveTo evaluate FD, a semi-quantitative synthetic magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-derived Fluid-Attenuated Inversion Recovery (FLAIR)-Double Inversion Recovery (DIR) contrast, against myelin volume fraction (MVF) in olfactory-limbic brain regions of patients diagnosed with mild cognitive impairment (MCI).MethodsSixteen healthy controls (HC) and 17 individuals diagnosed with MCI completed olfactory and cognitive testing and underwent 3T MRI using a QALAS sequence. MVF maps were generated and FD was computed as (FLAIR - DIR)/FLAIR. Group differences were examined in olfactory-limbic gray matter and associated white-matter tracts, and voxel-wise regression assessed FD-odor identification associations, including models adjusted for voxel-wise MVF. Region of interest and voxel-wise analyses were exploratory and largely uncorrected for multiple comparisons.ResultsCompared with HC, MCI showed lower FD across olfactory-limbic gray matter and white-matter pathways, including hippocampus, amygdala, orbitofrontal cortex, thalamus and corpus callosum, whereas MVF differences were more limited. Better odor identification was associated with higher FD in hippocampal/parahippocampal regions and insula, persisting after MVF adjustment. MVF showed positive associations in the right parahippocampal gyrus, left thalamus and genu of the corpus callosum. In an exploratory secondary analysis reported in the Supplemental Material, FD-based classification exceeded chance but was not separable from age alone.ConclusionsFD is a semi-quantitative relaxation-contrast metric showing regional patterns partially distinct from MVF. These exploratory findings require replication in larger, demographically matched, biomarker-confirmed cohorts before FD can be regarded as a marker of early olfactory-limbic microstructural change in MCI.

title: Changes in gray matter volume associated with gait speed and muscle mass in older adults with mild cognitive impairment.
abstract: BackgroundMild cognitive impairment (MCI) is an early stage of cognitive decline between normal aging and dementia. Gait speed, a key marker of physical function, has been associated with both cognitive decline and brain atrophy. Sarcopenia, characterized by age-related loss of muscle mass and function, has also been linked to structural brain changes.ObjectiveTo investigate the associations between sarcopenia, its individual components and regional gray matter volume (GMV) in older adults with MCI.MethodsThis cross-sectional study included 234 older adults with MCI. Sarcopenia, gait speed, handgrip strength, and appendicular skeletal muscle mass index (ASMI) were assessed according to the 2019 Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia criteria. Brain T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging was analyzed using voxel-based morphometry. Voxel-wise group comparisons were performed to identify GMV differences after adjustment age, sex, comorbidity, depressive symptoms, nutritional status, and total intracranial volume.ResultsSlower gait speed was significantly associated with lower GMV in the bilateral putamen and left superior frontal cortex. Lower ASMI was associated with higher GMV in the left inferior temporal cortex. No significant GMV differences were found by sarcopenia status or handgrip strength.ConclusionsSlower gait speed is associated with reduced GMV in motor-related brain regions, indicating early brain structural changes in older adults with MCI. Although lower ASMI was associated with higher GMV, this finding should be interpreted cautiously. These findings highlight the complex interactions between physical function and brain structure, emphasizing gait speed as a potential indicator of brain health in older adults with MCI.

title: Circulating Metalloproteinase Inhibitors and Artificial Intelligence-Derived Radiomics Predict Persistent Endoleak After Endovascular Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Repair: A Multimodal Biological-Imaging Model.
abstract: Objective Persistent endoleak after endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair (EVAR) reflects ongoing aneurysm sac biological activity and remains insufficiently predicted by anatomical surveillance alone. We aimed to evaluate whether integration of circulating matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), tissue inhibitors of metalloproteinases (TIMPs), and artificial intelligence (AI)-derived radiomic features from computed tomographic angiography (CTA) improves prediction of persistent endoleak. Methods We conducted a retrospective observational study including 62 consecutive patients undergoing elective infrarenal EVAR between January 2020 and December 2024. Plasma levels of MMP-1, MMP-2, MMP-9, MMP-10, TIMP-1, and TIMP-2 were measured preoperatively and at 1 and 12 months post-EVAR. Computed tomography angiography data sets were analyzed using a standardized semi-automated radiomics pipeline with reproducibility testing and penalized feature selection. The primary endpoint was persistent endoleak at 12 months. Multivariable logistic regression was constructed with event-per-variable control and internally validated using bootstrap resampling. Results Persistent endoleak occurred in 18 patients (29%). Patients with persistent endoleak exhibited significantly higher MMP-9 levels, lower TIMP-1 and TIMP-2 levels, and markedly elevated MMP-9/TIMP-1 ratios at 1 month (all P < .01). Radiomics demonstrated increased intraluminal thrombus (ILT) entropy and reduced ILT density in the endoleak group. A parsimonious model including MMP-9/TIMP-1 ratio and ILT entropy yielded an optimism-corrected area under the curve (AUC) of 0.81 with good calibration, outperforming sac diameter change alone (AUC = 0.62). Conclusions Persistent endoleak is associated with systemic proteolytic imbalance and imaging-detectable thrombus heterogeneity. Integration of biological and radiomic markers improves risk stratification compared with morphological surveillance alone and warrants prospective validation.Clinical ImpactThis study proposes a novel multimodal approach to post-EVAR surveillance by integrating circulating metalloproteinase inhibitors with AI-derived CT radiomics. Combining biological biomarkers with quantitative analysis of peri-EVAR thrombus volume and density may improve identification of patients at risk of persistent endoleak beyond conventional imaging assessment. For clinicians, this approach could enable earlier risk stratification, support personalised surveillance intervals, and identify patients who may benefit from closer imaging follow-up or intervention. The innovation lies in integrating systemic biological activity with local imaging phenotypes within a predictive model, moving EVAR surveillance from a predominantly anatomical strategy towards a personalised, data-driven biological-imaging paradigm.

title: Volumetric Analysis versus Diameter Measurement for Early Detection of Post-EVAR Sac Progression.
abstract: ObjectiveTo compare diameter- and volume-based surveillance after endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) and determine whether volumetric sac assessment identifies postoperative remodeling not captured by conventional maximum diameter measurement.MethodsThis retrospective single-center study included 383 patients who underwent elective EVAR for infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm between January 2016 and April 2024. All patients had preoperative and postoperative computed tomography angiography and at least 1 year of follow-up. Maximum sac diameter, total aneurysm sac volume, thrombus volume, thrombus density, neck morphology, and other anatomical variables were assessed using standardized morphometric and three-dimensional morphovolumetric measurements. Sac dynamics were classified by diameter criteria (≥5 mm decrease, stable, or ≥5 mm increase) and volumetric criteria (>10% decrease, stable, or >10% increase).ResultsEndoleaks occurred in 26.1% of patients (n = 100), and secondary interventions were required in 14.1% (n = 54), with a mean time to reintervention of 21.7 ± 10 months. At final follow-up, 74.7% demonstrated sac diameter reduction, 18.5% were stable, and 6.8% had enlargement, whereas volumetric analysis showed shrinkage in 81.7%, stability in 6.0%, and enlargement in 12.3%. At 1, 6, and 12 months, cohort mean diameter changed by -0.6%, -3.1%, and -6.5% from baseline, respectively, while cohort mean volume changed by -0.5%, -5.7%, and -12.5%. Among diameter-stable sacs, 32.4% enlarged volumetrically and 38.0% regressed volumetrically. In enlarging sacs, a 10% volume increase corresponded to an approximately 4 mm diameter increase (R 2 = 0.72; P < 0.001); this 4 mm value was a regression estimate, not the diameter threshold used for sac classification. Preoperative morphometric and morphovolumetric variables were associated with endoleak and secondary intervention in exploratory analyses.ConclusionVolumetric sac analysis identified additional postoperative remodeling beyond maximum diameter measurement, particularly in apparently stable sacs. A practical surveillance strategy combining rapid diameter-based screening with selective volumetric analysis in stable, borderline, or clinically suspicious cases may improve recognition of adverse sac behavior without requiring routine volumetry in every follow-up study.

title: A Study on Renal Artery Variations by CT Angiography and Their Clinical Importance.
abstract: AimThis study aimed to evaluate the prevalence, anatomical variations, and branching patterns of the renal arteries using multiphasic computed tomography angiography (CTA), based on the modified classification proposed by Cases et al (2017). Understanding renal artery variations is essential for preoperative planning, renal transplantation, endovascular procedures, and urological interventions.Materials and MethodsA retrospective analysis was conducted on 1220 abdominal CTA studies performed between March 2020 and June 2024. Fourteen cases were excluded according to predetermined exclusion criteria, resulting in 1206 studies being included in the final analysis (700 males, 520 females). All examinations were performed using a 128-slice CT scanner (Siemens SOMATOM; syngo CT VC 40). CTA protocols included 5-mm acquisition and 1-mm reconstruction, with administration of 100-120 mL of iodinated contrast at 5-6 mL/s via an 18G antecubital cannula. Post-processing involved multiplanar reformation, volume rendering, and 3D reconstruction. Two experienced radiologists independently reviewed all studies. Renal arteries were categorized into Types A-E and Patterns I-V. "Early division" (Types B and E) and "polar branches" (Types C and D) were further grouped for analytical purposes.ResultsAmong 1206 CTA studies, Type A (normal hilar artery) was the most common in both kidneys, with a slightly higher prevalence on the right (74.29%) than on the left (67.99%). Polar branches were more frequent in the left kidney, whereas early divisions were more common in the right kidney. Pattern 1 was predominant bilaterally (RK: 85.73%; LK: 77.61%), followed by Pattern 2. Significant differences were observed between the kidneys in the distribution of Types A, C, D, and Patterns 1 and 2.ConclusionCTA provides excellent visualization of renal artery variations, enabling precise classification and improving surgical, interventional, and transplant planning. Recognition of these anatomical differences is essential for minimizing procedural complications.

title: Symptomatic Superior Vena Cava Lipoma Causing Near-Complete Venous Obstruction: A Case Report and Literature Review.
abstract: BackgroundLipomas are common benign mesenchymal tumors; however, intravascular localization is exceedingly rare. Superior vena cava (SVC) involvement represents an exceptional entity, with only a limited number of cases reported in the literature. Intravascular lipomas are frequently detected incidentally but may present with symptoms related to venous obstruction, including superior vena cava syndrome. We report a rare case of SVC-origin intravascular lipoma extending into the right brachiocephalic vein, accompanied by a focused review of previously published upper extremity cases.Case PresentationA 77-year-old male presented with facial and cervical edema, dyspnea exacerbated in the supine position, and distended cervical veins. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed a 5-cm elongated, fat-attenuation mass within the SVC extending into the right brachiocephalic vein, causing near-total (approximately 99%) luminal occlusion. Transthoracic echocardiography supported the diagnosis. The patient underwent surgical resection via median sternotomy under cardiopulmonary bypass. Following longitudinal venotomy of the SVC extending to the brachiocephalic vein, the tumor-adherent to the posterior venous wall-was completely excised with preservation of vascular integrity. Primary venous repair was performed. The diagnosis of lipoma was histopathologically confirmed. The patient initially showed marked symptomatic improvement; however, on postoperative day 5, sudden-onset dyspnea necessitated reintubation, followed by multiorgan failure and death. The precise cause of the acute deterioration could not be definitively established.Literature review identified only 21 previously reported upper extremity intravenous lipomas, with this case representing the 16th involving the SVC and the oldest reported patient.ConclusionUpper extremity intravenous lipomas are rare and may lead to significant venous obstruction. Cross-sectional imaging is essential for diagnosis and surgical planning. In symptomatic patients, complete surgical excision provides definitive treatment and symptom relief. Management of incidentally detected asymptomatic cases remains controversial and should be individualized.

title: Why clinicians in acute hospitals may fail to engage in direct communication with people with intellectual disability.
abstract: This case highlights the healthcare inequities faced by people with intellectual disability, including diagnostic overshadowing, communication barriers, and the need for personalised, meaningful adjustments in care. A woman in her fifties with mild intellectual disability, epilepsy, and diabetes insipidus experienced delayed diagnosis and treatment because healthcare providers assumed she could not tolerate magnetic resonance imaging; however, when the scan was eventually completed with supported communication, it revealed a serious brain tumour with metastases. The case shows that diagnostic overshadowing can arise not only from misattributing symptoms, but also from untested assumptions about a patient's ability to engage with diagnostic procedures. It also underscores the importance of involving patients and families directly in healthcare decisions to support autonomy and prevent avoidable harm. Addressing these systemic issues is essential to deliver equitable, patient-centred care in acute hospital settings.

title: Diffuse Serous Atrophy of Bone Marrow in the Ankle and Hindfoot with Focal Acute Lateral Malleolar Osteomyelitis: A Magnetic Resonance Imaging-Based Case Report.
abstract: Serous atrophy of bone marrow (SABM) is a rare marrow disorder associated with severe chronic illness and malnutrition. It results in characteristic magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) signal due to atrophy of fat cells and loss of hematopoietic cells with deposition of gelatinous material. This may be misinterpreted as a technical error from the MRI scanner or mimic infiltrative or infectious processes. We report a case of a 71-year-old severely malnourished and immunosuppressed man with a full-thickness ulcer over the right lateral malleolus who underwent an MRI of the right ankle without and with intravenous gadolinium contrast for evaluation of suspected osteomyelitis. Pre-contrast MRI images demonstrated diffuse abnormal marrow signal throughout the ankle and hindfoot consistent with SABM, given his profound cachexia and malnutrition. Post-contrast images demonstrated a small focus of enhancement at the lateral malleolus beneath the patient's ulcer, suggesting an additional diagnosis of acute osteomyelitis without cortical destruction. The marrow signal in SABM and osteomyelitis can be indistinguishable on non-contrast MRI sequences; post-contrast imaging and correlation with clinical examination are essential, as SABM does not demonstrate contrast enhancement and acute osteomyelitis demonstrates enhancement. Given the patient's frailty and poor healing capacity, conservative management was pursued. Recognizing SABM and osteomyelitis in the ankle and foot requires integration of the clinical context with MRI findings, in which invasive procedures and misdiagnosis can be avoided.

title: Alexander Disease Diagnosed in an Obstetrics Patient: A Case Report and Review of the Literature.
abstract: Alexander disease (AxD) is a rare autosomal dominant leukodystrophy due to pathogenic variants in glial fibrillary acidic protein ( GFAP) . Adult-onset AxD type II presents with heterogeneous neurologic and neuropsychiatric symptoms. We report a unique case diagnosed in the postpartum period that mimicked posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES). A 33-year-old gravida 2 para 1 at 36 weeks gestation presented with 10 days of progressive restlessness, delusions, insomnia, dysarthria, weight loss with inability to feed herself, and urinary/fecal incontinence. She underwent induction of labor due to concern for severe pre-eclampsia (elevated liver enzymes and creatine kinase, elevated blood pressure), received magnesium sulfate, and required emergent cesarean delivery for non-reassuring fetal status. However, her symptoms persisted postpartum. Brain magnetic resonance imaging revealed extensive bifrontal, periventricular, and pontine non-enhancing hyperintensities. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis was normal including negative infectious, autoimmune, and paraneoplastic studies. Electroencephalography showed mild background slowing but no epileptiform activity. Empiric methylprednisolone and acyclovir had limited effects. Given the imaging findings, a leukodystrophy panel was ordered, which identified a heterozygous pathogenic GFAP variant (Arg79Leu), confirming a diagnosis of AxD type II. She improved with rehabilitation, with mild residual dysarthria at the 2-month follow-up. This is the first case report to describe an onset of AxD in the peripartum period. In peripartum patients with neurological symptoms whose course and MRI findings are atypical for PRES or other more common disorders, adult-onset neurogenetic disorders such as AxD should be considered. This diagnosis has important reproductive implications and warrants genetic counseling.

title: Baseline Knee Extension Is Associated With Volumetric Femoral Cartilage Loss in the Central Region of the Mid-lateral and External Medial Femoral Condyles: Data From the Osteoarthritis Initiative.
abstract: ObjectiveData evaluating knee flexion contracture (FC)-associated regional changes on femoral articular cartilage are lacking. We compared regional femoral articular cartilage outcomes of people with knee osteoarthritis (OA) with and without FC using quantitative MRI data.MethodsArticular cartilage of the medial and lateral femoral condyles were segmented into internal, central, and external subregions on MRI. Goniometry measured knee extension. We tested for regional differences in cartilage thickness and percent denuded bone (i.e., 0mm cartilage thickness) in the presence or absence of FC, and for associations between cartilage outcomes with quantitative knee extension range of motion (ROM) using a linear model for 596 participants.ResultsFor FC versus no FC, cartilage thickness in the central lateral subregion was higher (2.36±0.42mm vs. 2.29±0.43mm; p<0.05), with higher percent denuded bone in the central lateral (0.92±3.5% vs. 0.39±2.2%; p<0.05) and central medial subregions (4.61±12.88% vs. 3.17±11.66%; p<0.05). Lost knee extension was associated with increased percent denuded bone in the internal lateral ( r= 0.095; p<0.05), central lateral ( r =0.90; p<0.05), and central medial subregions ( r =0.117 ; p<0.01) but with increased central lateral cartilage thickness ( r =0.110; p<0.01). After correcting for clinical factors, an association between lost knee extension and increased percent denuded bone remained in the central lateral femur [ β =0.059; (95% CI 0.003-0.114)].ConclusionConclusion: Lost knee extension was associated with increased percent denuded bone in the central lateral and external medial femur. Interventions to maintain and/or restore knee ROM may benefit femoral cartilage health. Longitudinal studies evaluating the impact of lost knee ROM on femoral cartilage are warranted.

title: Combined qualitative and quantitative MRI reveals short-term progression in facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy.
abstract: Facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD) is characterized by slowly progressive and heterogeneous muscle involvement; therefore, clinical measures show limited sensitivity to short-term change. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides useful biomarkers of muscle degeneration and disease activity. To investigate one-year longitudinal changes in lower leg muscles of patients with FSHD using qualitative (T1-weighted [T1w], STIR) and quantitative MRI (fat fraction [FF], water T2), and to assess their relationship with clinical function. Thirty-one patients with FSHD (21 men; age 44.2±17 years) and 30 matched controls underwent 3T MRI. Twenty-seven patients completed one-year follow-up. Semi-quantitative grading and quantitative measures were analyzed muscle-wise. Longitudinal changes and correlations with clinical scores were assessed. At baseline, T1w imaging showed marked inter- and intra-individual variability, with heterogeneous proximal-distal involvement in 22% of muscles and asymmetric involvement in 77% of patients. STIR hyperintensity was present in 25 patients. Over one-year, clinical decline was small (MRC: Δ=-0.26, p=0.018, SRM=-0.23; mobility: Δ=-0.41, p=0.031, SRM=-0.44). In contrast, quantitative MRI detected progression, with increases in FF (0.17±0.13 to 0.22±0.15, p<0.001, SRM=0.87), FF heterogeneity, and water T2 heterogeneity, while T1w scores and mean water T2 showed limited change. Progression was greatest in muscles with intermediate baseline FF (ΔFF/year: 0.049 vs 0.007, p<0.001). Baseline STIR and water T2 abnormalities predicted increases in FF but not T1w scores. FF correlated more strongly with clinical measures than T1w grading. Quantitative MRI is more sensitive than qualitative grading for detecting short-term disease progression in FSHD. Measures of heterogeneity and disease activity predict structural progression and represent promising biomarkers for clinical trials.

title: Evaluation of Management Pathways for Pseudophakic Cystoid Macular Edema in a Large United States Cohort.
abstract: Purpose To identify the common management pathways in the treatment of pseudophakic cystoid macular edema (CME). Methods A retrospective cohort study was conducted from 2005 to 2024 using the TriNetX United States Collaborative Network. Patients diagnosed with pseudophakic CME were included in the study, and patients with retinal comorbidities were excluded. Treatments initiated after the diagnosis of pseudophakic CME, including topical corticosteroids and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), periocular and intravitreal (IVT) corticosteroids, antivascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) injections, suprachoroidal corticosteroids, and pars plana vitrectomy (PPV), were tracked, and treatment sequences and imaging use over time were analyzed. Results A total of 23 035 patients met the inclusion criteria, with a mean age of 72 years; 54% were women, and 68% identified as White. The incidence of pseudophakic CME increased from 2.45% in 2005 to 17.6% in 2024. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) use increased over time, becoming the most common imaging modality (used in 90% of cases), while 20% of patients underwent no imaging. No treatment was documented in 40% of patients. Among those treated, 77% received topical corticosteroids and/ or NSAIDs as first-line therapy, followed by IVT steroids (7.4%), periocular steroids (6.5%), PPV (3.4%), and anti-VEGF injections (2%). IVT steroids were the most common second-line treatment (10.2%), primarily dexamethasone implants (82.8%), followed by triamcinolone (12.2%). Use of newer agents, including fluocinolone acetonide implants and suprachoroidal triamcinolone, was uncommon. Conclusions Despite the increased use of OCT and earlier detection of subclinical cases, a substantial proportion of patients with pseudophakic CME have no documented treatment. Topical steroids and/ or NSAIDs represent the most common first- line therapy, with IVT steroids commonly used after inadequate response to treatment.

Purpose

To identify the common management pathways in the treatment of pseudophakic cystoid macular edema (CME).

Methods

A retrospective cohort study was conducted from 2005 to 2024 using the TriNetX United States Collaborative Network. Patients diagnosed with pseudophakic CME were included in the study, and patients with retinal comorbidities were excluded. Treatments initiated after the diagnosis of pseudophakic CME, including topical corticosteroids and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), periocular and intravitreal (IVT) corticosteroids, antivascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) injections, suprachoroidal corticosteroids, and pars plana vitrectomy (PPV), were tracked, and treatment sequences and imaging use over time were analyzed.

Results

A total of 23 035 patients met the inclusion criteria, with a mean age of 72 years; 54% were women, and 68% identified as White. The incidence of pseudophakic CME increased from 2.45% in 2005 to 17.6% in 2024. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) use increased over time, becoming the most common imaging modality (used in 90% of cases), while 20% of patients underwent no imaging. No treatment was documented in 40% of patients. Among those treated, 77% received topical corticosteroids and/ or NSAIDs as first-line therapy, followed by IVT steroids (7.4%), periocular steroids (6.5%), PPV (3.4%), and anti-VEGF injections (2%). IVT steroids were the most common second-line treatment (10.2%), primarily dexamethasone implants (82.8%), followed by triamcinolone (12.2%). Use of newer agents, including fluocinolone acetonide implants and suprachoroidal triamcinolone, was uncommon.

Conclusions

Despite the increased use of OCT and earlier detection of subclinical cases, a substantial proportion of patients with pseudophakic CME have no documented treatment. Topical steroids and/ or NSAIDs represent the most common first- line therapy, with IVT steroids commonly used after inadequate response to treatment.

title: Germ line landscape stratification defines distinct molecular and prognostic groups in therapy-related myeloid neoplasms.
abstract: Abstract Exposure to chemotherapy (CT) and/or radiotherapy increases the risk of therapy-related myeloid neoplasms (t-MN), a heterogeneous group of disorders currently classified by treatment history rather than molecular features. Although germ line predisposition has been suggested in ∼20% of patients, its prevalence and clinical impact remain insufficiently defined. To address this, we analyzed 100 patients with t-MN by integrating clinical characteristics, prior treatment regimens, and genomic profiling. Somatic and germ line variants were identified using targeted next-generation sequencing (n = 33) or whole-exome sequencing (n = 67). Somatic abnormalities, including cytogenetic and/or molecular alterations, were detected in 89.8% of patients. Germ line variants were identified in 32.3% of patients, including mutations in cancer predisposition genes (19.8%) and myeloid disease-related genes (14.6%). Patient stratification by germ line landscape and gene category defined 2 prognostic scenarios and 3 subgroups with distinct clinical outcomes. Patients harboring germ line cancer predisposition variants were enriched for TP53 mutations and complex karyotypes and had an adverse prognosis. In contrast, patients with germ line myeloid-related variants and those without detectable germ line variants exhibited recurrent mutations in TET2, DNMT3A, SF3B1, SRSF2, RUNX1, and ASXL1, were associated with normal karyotypes, and had favorable outcomes. These findings underscore the importance of the germ line landscape in t-MN pathogenesis and support its incorporation into disease classification and risk stratification. Notably, CT exposure was associated with complex karyotypes and poor prognosis in patients with germ line cancer predisposition variants, highlighting a subgroup that may benefit from targeted surveillance and preventive strategies.

title: Prognosis and treatment-related toxicities in Down syndrome acute lymphoblastic leukemia in JCCG ALL-B12.
abstract: Children with Down syndrome (DS) have an increased risk of acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). Although recent reports describe some improvement, survival in DS-ALL remains inferior to that of non-DS-ALL. This study evaluated the prognosis, relapse patterns, and treatment-related toxicities of DS-ALL in the Japan Children's Cancer Group ALL-B12 trial, a nationwide prospective study using risk-adapted therapy. A total of 1,804 patients, including 44 DS-ALL, were analyzed. Risk classification used standardized criteria. The 5-year event-free survival and overall survival in DS-ALL were 70.5% and 81.8%, respectively, lower than 85.6% and 94.6% in non-DS-ALL (P < 0.001). Survival differences were most pronounced in standard-risk patients. DS-ALL showed fewer favorable genetics and relapse patterns dominated by isolated bone marrow events, with no CNS relapse. CRLF2 rearrangement was assessable in 43 of 44 DS-ALL cases; 15 of 43 (34.9%) were positive. In an exploratory analysis excluding canonical favorable or unfavorable subtypes (n = 36), the 5-year EFS in DS-ALL with and without CRLF2 rearrangement were 57.1% and 81.8%, respectively (P = 0.300), and the corresponding 5-year OS were 78.6% and 86.4%, respectively (P = 0.331). Treatment-related toxicities were more frequent in DS-ALL, including mucositis (27.3% vs. 7.1%), hyperglycemia (25.0% vs. 6.9%), and pulmonary infections (20.5% vs. 7.4%). Among DS-ALL patients with TP2 MRD ≥ 10-4 (n = 3), all relapsed and died within three years. No treatment-related death was recorded after induction, but one death of undetermined cause occurred. These findings highlight the continuing need to optimize DS-ALL therapy to reduce relapse and toxicity. UMIN CT Registry (UMIN000009339) and JCT (jRCTs041180101).
